name: Taj Mahal
tagline: Marble and gardens on the Yamuna
overview: Walk the formal gardens for views of the marble mausoleum and its river-facing terrace.

name: Agra Fort
tagline: A Mughal fortress above the Yamuna
overview: Red sandstone walls enclose courtyards, audience halls, and palaces built and adapted by Mughal rulers.

name: Fatehpur Sikri
tagline: Akbar’s former imperial capital
overview: Explore the sandstone palace precinct, stepped gateways, and the courtyards of the former capital.

name: Lucknow
tagline: Awadhi food and architectural heritage
overview: Pair the Bara Imambara and Rumi Darwaza with a walk through the food streets of the old city.

name: Sarnath
tagline: Buddhist archaeology near Varanasi
overview: See the Dhamek Stupa and excavated monastery grounds at the traditional site of the Buddha’s first sermon.

name: Jaipur
tagline: Palaces and bazaars in the Pink City
overview: Start in the walled city for the Hawa Mahal and market streets, then explore hilltop forts nearby.

name: Amber Fort
tagline: A hilltop palace above Maota Lake
overview: Climb through courtyards and decorated palace rooms for views over the lake and surrounding ridges.

name: Udaipur
tagline: Lakes and palace terraces
overview: Explore the City Palace and the streets around Lake Pichola, with viewpoints from both shores.

name: Jodhpur
tagline: Blue lanes below Mehrangarh
overview: Spend time in the fort museum and walk the blue-painted lanes and market around the old clock tower.

name: Jaisalmer
tagline: A sandstone city in the Thar
overview: The living fort and carved havelis make a natural pair with an excursion into the desert.

name: Pushkar
tagline: A lake town ringed by ghats
overview: Walk the lanes around Pushkar Lake and look for views from the hills above the town.

name: Ranthambore National Park
tagline: Dry forest and a hilltop fort
overview: Explore a landscape of forest, lakes, and ruins; wildlife sightings vary and park access is regulated.

name: Dholavira
tagline: A Harappan city on Khadir Island
overview: The archaeological site reveals a planned settlement with reservoirs, fortifications, and ceremonial spaces.

name: Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park
tagline: Medieval monuments below Pavagadh Hill
overview: Combine the mosques and fortifications at Champaner with a visit to the hill if time allows.

name: Rani ki Vav
tagline: A sculpted stepwell in Patan
overview: The descending terraces frame elaborate stone sculpture and offer a close look at historic water architecture.

name: Modhera Sun Temple
tagline: A temple and stepped tank from the Solanki era
overview: Walk the temple complex from its ceremonial tank to the carved assembly hall.

name: Somnath Temple
tagline: A coastal pilgrimage stop
overview: The seafront temple area pairs walks by the Arabian Sea with the pilgrimage sites around Prabhas Patan.

name: Mumbai
tagline: Waterfront walks and Victorian streets
overview: Explore the harbour edge around Colaba and the historic civic buildings and markets near Fort.

name: Elephanta Caves
tagline: Rock-cut shrines on an island
overview: A harbour ferry and stepped approach lead to cave temples with large sculptural panels.

name: Ajanta Caves
tagline: Buddhist caves above the Waghora River
overview: Rock-cut halls and monasteries follow a bend in the gorge; several preserve remarkable murals.

name: Ellora Caves
tagline: Monumental architecture carved from rock
overview: Set aside time for the Kailasa temple and the Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain caves along the ridge.

name: Old Goa
tagline: Churches of the former Portuguese capital
overview: Explore the basilica and cathedral precinct beside the Mandovi River and leave time for the archaeology museum.

name: Dudhsagar Falls
tagline: A waterfall in the Western Ghats
overview: The falls descend through forest near the state border. Access routes and conditions can change seasonally.

name: Palolem Beach
tagline: A crescent bay in South Goa
overview: Walk the shore early or late and explore the viewpoints around this sheltered coastal bay.

name: Gokarna
tagline: Temple lanes and coastal trails
overview: Combine the old town’s temple precinct with paths between the headlands and beaches.

name: Mysuru
tagline: Royal architecture and a lively market
overview: Visit Mysore Palace and Devaraja Market, with Chamundi Hill an option for a separate outing.

name: Badami Cave Temples
tagline: Rock-cut temples above a reservoir
overview: The stairway above Agastya Lake leads to a series of shrines cut into red sandstone.

name: Pattadakal
tagline: Chalukya temples by the Malaprabha
overview: Compare the northern and southern architectural forms in this compact temple complex.

name: Jog Falls
tagline: The Sharavathi’s plunge into a gorge
overview: View the falls from designated viewpoints, where flow can vary widely with the season.

name: Madikeri
tagline: Coffee country in the Kodagu hills
overview: Use the town as a base for estate visits, ridge viewpoints, and short forest outings.

name: Belur
tagline: Hoysala stone carving on a grand scale
overview: Walk the Chennakeshava Temple enclosure and look closely at the reliefs and sculpted pillars.

name: Fort Kochi
tagline: Port history and seaside lanes
overview: Walk between the waterfront, historic churches, and neighbourhood streets shaped by long-distance trade.

name: Alappuzha
tagline: Canals and backwater villages
overview: Explore the waterways near Vembanad Lake by a local ferry or a small organized boat trip.

name: Munnar
tagline: Highland tea estates and misty valleys
overview: Start with the tea landscapes around town and choose a marked nature walk or nearby viewpoint.

name: Periyar National Park
tagline: Lake and forest in the Cardamom Hills
overview: Use Thekkady as a base for regulated walks or trips on the lake, with wildlife sightings dependent on conditions.

name: Varkala
tagline: Coastal cliffs above the Arabian Sea
overview: Follow the cliff-top path for views down to the beach and out over the Arabian Sea.

name: Mahabalipuram
tagline: Pallava monuments beside the sea
overview: Visit the Shore Temple, monolithic rathas, and open-air reliefs on foot across the town.

name: Brihadisvara Temple
tagline: A Chola temple in Thanjavur
overview: The temple’s tall tower, spacious courtyard, and carved stone are best seen on a slow circuit.

name: Meenakshi Temple
tagline: A temple complex at the heart of Madurai
overview: Walk the streets around the gateway towers and see how the historic city grew around the temple.

name: Rameswaram
tagline: Pilgrimage and Pamban Island seascapes
overview: Combine the temple precinct with coastal views and a separate outing toward Dhanushkodi.

name: Ooty
tagline: Botanical gardens and Nilgiri viewpoints
overview: Visit the gardens and lake, or travel part of the hill railway for a different view of the landscape.

name: Kodaikanal
tagline: A lake town in the Palani Hills
overview: Walk the lake and the ridge viewpoints, leaving room for changes in visibility when clouds move in.

name: Kanyakumari
tagline: A headland at India’s southern tip
overview: Spend time on the seafront and look across to the offshore memorials; boat access depends on sea conditions.

name: Puducherry
tagline: Coastal streets and a historic promenade
overview: Explore the grid of streets near the promenade and the Tamil neighbourhoods farther inland.

name: Charminar
tagline: A monument at the heart of old Hyderabad
overview: See the monument from the surrounding bazaars and explore the streets leading to nearby historic buildings.

name: Golconda Fort
tagline: A fortified hill overlooking Hyderabad
overview: Walk the fort’s gateways and ascent for views across the masonry, ramparts, and city.

name: Ramappa Temple
tagline: A Kakatiya temple by a lake
overview: The sculpted pillars and carved stone brackets reveal the craftsmanship of the Kakatiya period.

name: Borra Caves
tagline: Limestone chambers in the Ananthagiri hills
overview: Follow the visitor route into the caverns, looking for stalactites and other formations along the lit path.

name: Tirumala Venkateswara Temple
tagline: Pilgrimage in the Seshachalam Hills
overview: The hilltop temple is a major pilgrimage destination. Check official arrangements before planning a visit.

name: Gandikota
tagline: A fort above the Pennar gorge
overview: Walk the fortified settlement and see the gorge from designated overlooks above the river.

name: Konark Sun Temple
tagline: A stone chariot on the Odisha coast
overview: Look for carved wheels, horses, and panels in the surviving complex of the temple to Surya.

name: Puri
tagline: Pilgrimage and a long Bay of Bengal shore
overview: Pair the town’s pilgrimage streets with time on the coast, checking temple access rules before visiting.

name: Chilika Lake
tagline: A brackish lagoon and bird habitat
overview: Choose a lake-side base according to the section you want to explore and travel with local boat operators.

name: Udayagiri and Khandagiri Caves
tagline: Rock-cut shelters above Bhubaneswar
overview: Climb the paths between clusters of excavated shelters and look for inscriptions and sculpted entrances.

name: Darjeeling
tagline: Tea slopes and Himalayan viewpoints
overview: Explore the hill town and its tea landscapes, keeping early starts for a better chance of clear mountain views.

name: Sundarbans National Park
tagline: Mangrove waterways in the Ganges delta
overview: Use permitted boat routes to explore the tidal landscape with local guides.

name: Victoria Memorial
tagline: A museum and gardens in Kolkata
overview: The building’s galleries and grounds make an easy pairing with a walk around the Maidan.

name: Bishnupur
tagline: Terracotta temples and craft traditions
overview: Walk between brick temples and examine the narrative reliefs that decorate their walls.

name: Mahabodhi Temple
tagline: A Buddhist pilgrimage site in Bodh Gaya
overview: Visit the temple precinct and Bodhi Tree, then explore the monasteries established nearby.

name: Nalanda Mahavihara
tagline: Monastic ruins of an early seat of learning
overview: Walk the excavated monasteries and temples to see how the residential and teaching spaces were arranged.

name: Sanchi
tagline: A hilltop group of Buddhist monuments
overview: Start with the Great Stupa’s carved gateways, then walk the paths linking monasteries and smaller stupas.

name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
tagline: Chandela temples and sculpture
overview: Allow time for the temple clusters and the details of their sculpted exterior walls.

name: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters
tagline: Sandstone shelters with prehistoric paintings
overview: Follow the marked route through shelters and outcrops in the forested foothills.

name: Orchha
tagline: Bundela palaces on the Betwa
overview: The riverside cenotaphs, fort complex, and temple streets make a compact walking circuit.

name: Chitrakote Falls
tagline: A broad waterfall on the Indravati
overview: The river drops through a wide horseshoe-shaped edge, with very different views at high and low flows.

name: Kanger Valley National Park
tagline: Forested valleys and limestone caves
overview: Plan a route around the individual caves, forest walks, and waterfall sites that are open to visitors.

name: Hundru Falls
tagline: The Subarnarekha descends the Ranchi plateau
overview: Visit this waterfall from Ranchi and use the designated paths and viewpoints on the steep approach.

name: Deoghar
tagline: A pilgrimage town around Baidyanath Temple
overview: Explore the temple quarter and the streets that serve the town’s long-standing pilgrimage routes.

name: Golden Temple
tagline: A Sikh shrine surrounded by a sacred pool
overview: Walk the marble circuit and learn about the community kitchen. Cover your head and follow the site’s guidance.

name: Jallianwala Bagh
tagline: A memorial in the heart of Amritsar
overview: The garden memorial commemorates the people killed in the 1919 massacre and is reached through old-city lanes.

name: Qutb Minar
tagline: A soaring minaret and an early Delhi complex
overview: Walk the courtyards and ruined structures around the sandstone tower in Mehrauli.

name: Sultanpur National Park
tagline: Wetland birding near Gurugram
overview: Follow the designated perimeter paths to view waterbirds; conditions and bird numbers vary by season.

name: Rock Garden of Chandigarh
tagline: A sculptural maze made with reused material
overview: Paths pass courtyards, figures, and cascades assembled from discarded tiles, ceramics, and other materials.

name: Rishikesh
tagline: Riverfront walks in the Himalayan foothills
overview: Explore walking routes along the Ganges and the neighbourhoods associated with yoga and pilgrimage.

name: Kedarnath Temple
tagline: A pilgrimage site high in the Garhwal Himalaya
overview: The temple is reached by an uphill pilgrimage route in a high mountain valley; the visiting season is limited.

name: Valley of Flowers National Park
tagline: An alpine valley known for wildflowers
overview: The protected valley is reached on foot, with weather and seasonal trail access central to planning.

name: Nainital
tagline: A Kumaon hill town around a lake
overview: Walk between the lake shore, hillside lanes, and viewpoints above this mountain basin.

name: Shimla
tagline: A ridge town with colonial-era architecture
overview: Walk between the Ridge and Mall Road, then explore the steeper neighbourhood lanes and wooded trails.

name: Manali
tagline: A town above the Beas River
overview: Start with the old-town lanes and deodar groves, then explore accessible river and valley viewpoints.

name: McLeod Ganj
tagline: Tibetan culture in the Dhauladhar foothills
overview: Explore the monastery precinct, food streets, and marked walking routes around the hill town.

name: Great Himalayan National Park
tagline: Protected Himalayan forests and valleys
overview: Use the designated access points and plan permitted trails according to conditions and experience.

name: Srinagar
tagline: Lake, gardens, and the old city
overview: Combine the Dal Lake waterfront with Mughal gardens and a separate walk through the older city.

name: Gulmarg
tagline: A high meadow beneath the Pir Panjal
overview: Choose walks or winter activities based on snow and weather conditions, and use designated routes.

name: Leh
tagline: Palace terraces and a high-altitude old town
overview: Explore the old lanes below Leh Palace and the town’s hillsides at an unhurried pace.

name: Hemis Monastery
tagline: A monastery tucked in a tributary valley
overview: The courtyards and exhibition spaces make this an accessible introduction to Ladakhi monastic heritage.

name: Kaziranga National Park
tagline: Floodplain grasslands with one-horned rhinos
overview: Use regulated routes through grassland and riverine habitats where rhinos and other wildlife live.

name: Majuli
tagline: A Brahmaputra island with monastic communities
overview: Allow time for river crossings and explore satras, village roads, and riverside landscapes.

name: Kamakhya Temple
tagline: A hilltop shrine overlooking Guwahati
overview: Climb or drive to the temple precinct on Nilachal Hill for views and a visit to an important pilgrimage site.

name: Dawki
tagline: A clear-water river at the southern border
overview: Visit the Umngot River from the town and look across the steep valley at the forested banks.

name: Tawang Monastery
tagline: A monastery overlooking the Tawang valley
overview: Explore the monastery courtyard, prayer hall, and viewpoints over the broad mountain valley.

name: Ziro
tagline: Rice fields and Apatani villages
overview: Walk valley roads between fields and settlements and learn about local farming traditions with a guide.

name: Loktak Lake
tagline: A lake known for floating vegetation
overview: Use the lakeshore viewpoints and regulated local routes to see the phumdis and surrounding hills.

name: Kisama Heritage Village
tagline: Architecture and traditions near Kohima
overview: Explore the village’s houses and performance spaces when open, with event schedules checked separately.

name: Reiek
tagline: A ridge high above forested hills
overview: Follow marked walking routes near the village for open views over the surrounding hills.

name: Neermahal
tagline: A palace in Rudrasagar Lake
overview: See the water palace and its setting from the lake shore or on an available local boat crossing.

name: Gangtok
tagline: A hill capital with monastery and ridge walks
overview: Explore the town’s ridge streets and use nearby monasteries and viewpoints to see the surrounding valleys.

name: Pelling
tagline: Monastery trails and mountain views
overview: Use the town as a base for the Pemayangtse monastery and the nearby ruins of Rabdentse.

name: Cellular Jail
tagline: A memorial to colonial-era imprisonment
overview: The galleries and surviving wings in Port Blair interpret the stories of prisoners held during British rule.

name: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island)
tagline: Forest-backed beaches in the Andaman Sea
overview: Explore the shore at Radhanagar and other designated beaches, with boat and water activity access dependent on conditions.

name: Agatti Island
tagline: A coral island with a shallow lagoon
overview: The island’s reef-fringed lagoon and beach walks are its main draws; check entry and transport arrangements before travelling.

name: Nashik
tagline: Godavari river city and India’s vineyard valley
overview: Nashik, formerly Nasik, is a city in the northern region of the Indian state of Maharashtra situated on the banks of the river Godavari, about 165 km (103 mi) northeast of the state capital Mumbai. The city lies in the Nashik Metropolitan Region.

name: Coonoor
tagline: Nilgiri tea estates, Sim’s Park, and mountain rail
overview: Coonoor or Kunnur (Tamil: [kunːuːr] ), is a taluk and a municipal town of the Nilgiris District in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. As of 2011, the town had a population of 45,494.

name: Warangal
tagline: Kakatiya stone gateways and Thousand Pillar Temple
overview: Warangal (Telugu: [ʋɐrɐŋɡɐl] ), also known as Orugallu, is a city in the Indian state of Telangana and the district headquarters of Warangal district. It is the second largest city in Telangana with a population of 811,844 per 2011 Census of India, and spreading over an 406 km2 (157 sq mi).

name: Araku Valley
tagline: Eastern Ghats coffee hills and tribal museum
overview: Araku Valley is a hill station in the Alluri Sitharama Raju district of Andhra Pradesh, India, located 111 km from Visakhapatnam.

name: Gopalpur-on-Sea
tagline: Calm Bay of Bengal beach town with historic lighthouse
overview: Gopalpur or Gopalpur-on-Sea is a coastal town and a Notified Area Council in Ganjam district in Odisha, India. Gopalpur is around 15 km from Berhampur.

name: Mandu
tagline: Afghan-era hilltop palaces like Jahaz Mahal
overview: Mandu or Mandavgad is an ancient city in the present-day Mandav area of the Dhar district. It is located in the Malwa and Nimar region of western Madhya Pradesh, India, at 35 km from Dhar city.

name: Pahalgam
tagline: Lidder River meadow valley of Betaab and Aru
overview: Pahalgam (Urdu pronunciation: [pɛɦɛlɡɑːm]) or Pahalgom (Kashmiri pronunciation: [pəhəlʲɡoːm]) is a town in Anantnag district of the Indian union territory of Jammu and Kashmir. It is located on the banks of Lidder River at an altitude of 2,200 m (7,200 ft) in the Vale of Kashmir.

name: Bomdila
tagline: Kameng ridge town with monastery and Eastern Himalaya views
overview: Bomdila is the headquarters of West Kameng district in the state of Arunachal Pradesh in India. Bomdila is one of the 60 constituencies of the state of Arunachal Pradesh.

name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
tagline: World’s only floating national park of phumdis
overview: The Keibul Lamjao National Park (Meitei: Keibul Lamjao Leipakki Lampak) is a national park in the Bishnupur district of the state of Manipur in Northeast India. It is 40 km2 (15.4 mi2) in area, the only floating national park in the world, and an integral part of Loktak Lake.

name: Mokokchung
tagline: Ao Naga cultural heartland of hilltop villages
overview: Mokokchung () is a municipality in the Mokokchung District of the Indian state of Nagaland. It serves as the district headquarters as well as the main urban hub of Mokokchung District.

name: Phawngpui (Blue Mountain)
tagline: Sacred highest peak of Mizoram with orchid cliffs
overview: Phawngpui (Pron: /ˌpʰɔ:ŋˈpʊɪ/), also known as Blue Mountain, is the highest mountain peak in the Mizo Hills (Lushai Hills) and in the state of Mizoram, India, with an elevation of 2157 m. It is in Lawngtlai district, in the southeastern region of Mizoram near the Myanmar border.

name: Kavaratti
tagline: Lagoon capital with coral reefs and Ujra Mosque
overview: Kavaratti (, Malayalam: [kɐʋɐɾɐt̪ːi]) is an atoll in the Indian Union Territory of Lakshadweep. The census town of Kavaratti, which is the major settlement in the atoll, serves as the capital of Lakshadweep.

name: Khangchendzonga Park
tagline: UNESCO alpine wilderness around the third highest peak
overview: Khangchendzonga National Park is a national park and part of the Khangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve in Sikkim, India. It was inscribed to the UNESCO World Heritage Sites list in July 2016, becoming the first "Mixed Heritage" site of India.

name: Sinhagad
tagline: Cliffside Maratha hill fort overlooking Pune
overview: Sinhagad (also known as the Lion's Fort) is an ancient hill fortress located at around 28 kilometres southwest of Pune, India. Previously known as Kondhana, the fort has been the site of many battles, most notably the Battle of Sinhagad in 1670.This is the highest peaks of Pune.

name: Mayapur
tagline: Confluence of Jalangi and Bhagirathi river temples
overview: Mayapur (Mayāpura) is a pilgrimage town in the Nabadwip CD block in the Krishnanagar Sadar subdivision of the Nadia district, West Bengal, India. It is situated at the confluence of the Jalangi River and the Bhagirathi, a distributary of the Ganges.

name: Bakkhali
tagline: Quiet Sundarbans delta beach and Henry Island mangroves
overview: Bakkhali is a village within the jurisdiction of the Namkhana police station in the Namkhana CD block in the Kakdwip subdivision of the South 24 Parganas district in the Indian state of West Bengal.

name: Indira Point
tagline: Southernmost lighthouse tip of India on Great Nicobar
overview: Great Nicobar is the southernmost and largest of the Nicobar Islands of India, north of Sumatra. It is part of India, in the Nicobar district within the union territory of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

name: Mathura
tagline: Sacred riverside city and birthplace of Krishna
overview: Mathura (Braj pronunciation: [mɐ.t̪ʰʊ.ɾäː] ) is a city and the administrative headquarters of Mathura district in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh. It is located 162 kilometres (101 mi) south-east of Delhi; and about 15 kilometres (9.3 mi) from the town of Vrindavan.

name: Vrindavan
tagline: Historic temple town on the Yamuna
overview: Vrindavan (pronounced [ʋɾɪnˈdɑːʋən] ; IAST: Vṛndāvana), also spelt Vrindaban and Brindaban, is a historic city in the Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh, India. It is located in the Braj Bhoomi region and holds religious significance for Hindus, who believe that Krishna, one of the main Gods in Hinduism, spent most of his childhood in this city.

name: Bikaner
tagline: Desert city of red sandstone havelis and Junagarh Fort
overview: Bikaner (IPA: [biːkaːneːɾ] ) is a city in the Indian state of Rajasthan. It is situated approximately 330 kilometres (205 mi) northwest of the state capital Jaipur, in the Thar Desert region of western Rajasthan.

name: Mount Abu
tagline: Aravalli hill station and Dilwara marble temples
overview: Abu Raj [formerly Mount Abu ()] is a hill station in the Sirohi district of the state of Rajasthan in western India. Here, the mountain forms a rocky plateau 22 km (14 mi) long by 9 km (5.6 mi) wide.

name: Chittorgarh
tagline: Hilltop Rajput fortress and Victory Tower
overview: Chittorgarh (Hindi pronunciation: [t͡ʃɪt̪ːɔːɽ.gəɽʱ] ; also Chitror, Chittor or Chittaurgarh) is a major city in the state of Rajasthan in western India. It lies on the Berach River, a tributary of the Banas, and is the administrative headquarters of Chittorgarh District.

name: Ajmer
tagline: Pilgrimage city framed by Ana Sagar Lake
overview: Ajmer (pronounced [əd͡ʑ.meːɾ] ) is a city in the Indian state of Rajasthan. It is the administrative headquarters of the Ajmer district and Ajmer division.

name: Sariska Tiger Reserve
tagline: Dry deciduous Aravalli hills and tiger reserve
overview: Sariska Tiger Reserve is a tiger reserve in Alwar district of Rajasthan, India. It stretches over 1,203.34 km2 (464.61 sq mi) including a core area of 881 km2 (340 sq mi) and a buffer zone 322.23 km2 (124.41 sq mi).

name: Alwar
tagline: Historic city below Bala Quila and Siliserh Lake
overview: Alwar (Rajasthani Pronunciation: [əlʋəɾ]) is a city in Rajasthan and the administrative headquarters of Alwar District in the state of Rajasthan. It is located 150 km south of Delhi and 150 km north of Jaipur.

name: Nathdwara
tagline: Shrinathji temple town and Pichwai art hub
overview: Nathdwara is a city in the Rajsamand district of the state of Rajasthan, India. It is located in the Aravalli hills, on the banks of the Banas River and is 48 kilometres north-east of Udaipur.

name: Rann of Kutch
tagline: Vast white salt marsh and Kutchi craft villages
overview: Kutch district (Kachhi: [kətːʃʰ]), is a district of Gujarat state in western India, with its headquarters (capital) at Bhuj. Covering an area of 45,674 km2, Kutch is the largest district of India.

name: Dwarka
tagline: Coastal pilgrimage city on the Arabian Sea
overview: Dwarka () is a coastal town and municipality of Devbhumi Dwarka district in the Indian state of Gujarat. It is located on the western shore of the Okhamandal Peninsula on the right bank of the Gomti River at the mouth of the Gulf of Kutch facing the Arabian Sea.

name: Bhuj
tagline: Walled desert town of Aina Mahal and Kutchi heritage
overview: Bhuj (Gujarati: [bʰudʒ] ) is a city and the headquarters of Kutch district in the Indian state of Gujarat. It was the capital of Kutch State, which was a princely state before it was merged into the Indian Union in 1947.

name: Lothal
tagline: Indus Valley port town with ancient brick dockyard
overview: Lothal (Gujarati pronunciation: [lot̪ʰəl]) was one of the southernmost sites of the ancient Indus Valley Civilisation, located in the Bhal region of the Indian state of Gujarat. Construction of the city is believed to have begun around 2300 BCE.

name: Junagadh
tagline: Ancient Girnar foothills, stepwells, and Uparkot Fort
overview: Junagadh () is the city and headquarters of Junagadh district in the Indian state of Gujarat. Located at the foot of the Girnar hills, 355 kilometres (221 mi) southwest of Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar (the state capital), it is the seventh largest city in the state.

name: Vadodara
tagline: Cultural capital famed for Laxmi Vilas Palace
overview: Vadodara (Gujarati: [ˌʋəˈɖo.d̪ɾɐ̯] ), also known as Baroda, is a city on the banks of the Vishwamitri River in the Indian state of Gujarat. It serves as the administrative headquarters of the Vadodara district.

name: Lonavala
tagline: Western Ghats hill station of misty valleys and caves
overview: Lonavala-Khandala is a hill station and a municipal council in the Pune district, Maharashtra. It is about 64 km (40 miles) west of Pune and 96 km (60 miles) to the east of Mumbai.

name: Mahabaleshwar
tagline: Sahyadri strawberry plateau and dramatic cliff viewpoints
overview: Mahabaleshwar () is a small town and a municipal council in Satara district, Maharashtra, India. It is a place of pilgrimage because the Krishna River, which considered sacred by Hindus, has its origin here along with five of its tributaries.

name: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
tagline: Gateway to Deccan forts and Bibi Ka Maqbara
overview: Aurangabad (), officially Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is a city in the Indian state of Maharashtra. It is the administrative headquarters of Aurangabad district and is the largest city in the Marathwada region.

name: Pune
tagline: Shaniwar Wada, Sahyadri treks, and cultural hubs
overview: Pune (Marathi: Puṇē, pronounced [ˈpuɳeː] ), previously spelled in English as Poona (the official name until 1978), is a city in the state of Maharashtra in the Deccan Plateau in Western India. It is the administrative headquarters of the Pune district, and of Pune division.

name: Alibag
tagline: Konkan coastal getaway with Kolaba sea fort
overview: Alibag (pronounced [əlibaːɡ]), also known as Alibaug, is a coastal city and a municipal council in the Raigad district of Maharashtra, India. It is the headquarters of the Raigad district, and is south of the city of Mumbai.

name: Ratnagiri
tagline: Konkan coast of Alphonso orchards and sea cliffs
overview: Ratnagiri (IAST:Ratnāgirī; [ɾət̪n̪aːɡiɾiː]) is a port city on the Arabian Sea in Ratnagiri District in southwestern Maharashtra, India. The district is part of the Konkan division of Maharashtra.

name: Kolhapur
tagline: Mahalaxmi temple city and Rankala Lake
overview: Kolhapur () is a city on the banks of the Panchganga River in the southern part of the Indian state of Maharashtra. Kolhapur is one of the most significant cities in South Maharashtra and has been a hub of historical, religious, and cultural activities for centuries.

name: Karla Caves
tagline: Ancient rock-cut Buddhist chaitya halls near Lonavala
overview: The Karla Caves, Karli Caves, Karle Caves or Karla Cells, are a complex of ancient Buddhist Indian rock-cut caves at Karli near Lonavala, Maharashtra. It is just 10.9 Kilometers away from Lonavala.

name: Panchgani
tagline: Volcanic tableland overlooking Krishna valley
overview: Panchgani, called Paachgani, is a hill station and municipal council in Satara district in Maharashtra, India. Panchgani attracts tourists throughout the year.

name: Panaji
tagline: Fontainhas Latin Quarter along the Mandovi riverfront
overview: Panaji (formerly Nova Goa; ; Goan Konkani: Ponnjem, IPA: [pɵɳd͡ʑɛ̃] ; Portuguese: Pangim), also known as Panjim, is the capital of the Indian state of Goa and the headquarters of the North Goa district. It was previously the territorial capital of the former Portuguese India (Estado da Índia).

name: Aihole
tagline: Cradle of Chalukyan stone temple architecture
overview: Aihole (ಐಹೊಳೆ), also referred to as Aivalli, Ahivolal or Aryapura, is a historic site of ancient and medieval-era Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments in Karnataka, India that dates from the sixth century through the twelfth century CE. Most of the surviving monuments at the site date from the 7th to 10th centuries.

name: Halebidu
tagline: Hoysaleswara temple carved in soapstone filigree
overview: Halebidu (IAST: Haḷēbīḍu, literally "old capital, city, encampment" or "ruined city") is a Hobli located in Hassan District, Karnataka, India. Historically known as Dvārasamudra (also Dorasamudra), Halebidu became the regal capital of the Hoysala Empire in the 11th century CE.

name: Bandipur National Park
tagline: Nilgiri biosphere forest of elephants and tigers
overview: Bandipur National Park is a national park covering 1,456.3 km2 (562.3 sq mi) in Chamarajnagar district in the Indian state of Karnataka. It was established as a tiger reserve under Project Tiger in 1973.

name: Udupi
tagline: Coastal temple town and birthplace of Udupi cuisine
overview: Udupi (Kannada: [uɖupi]), also known as Odipu ([oɖipu]) in Tulu, is a city in the Indian state of Karnataka. It is the administrative headquarters and taluka of Udupi district, and one of the fastest-growing cities in Karnataka.

name: Shravanabelagola
tagline: Monolithic Gommateshwara statue atop Vindhyagiri hill
overview: Shravanabelagola (pronunciation: [ɕɾɐ.ʋɐˈɳɐ bɛ.ɭɐ.go.ɭɐ]) is a town located near Channarayapatna taluk of Hassan district in the Indian state of Karnataka and is 144 km (89 mi) from Bengaluru. The Gommateshwara Bahubali statue at Shravanabelagola is one of the most important tirthas (pilgrimage destinations) in Jainism, one that reached a peak in…

name: Vijayapura
tagline: Adil Shahi domes and the acoustic Gol Gumbaz
overview: Bijapur (officially Vijayapura) is the district headquarters of the Bijapur district of the Karnataka state of India. It is also the headquarters for Bijapur Taluk.

name: Bidar
tagline: Deccan plateau fort city and Bidriware craft hub
overview: Bidar ( Kannada: [biːd̪əɾ] ) is a city and the headquarters of the Bidar district in Karnataka state of India. Bidar is a prominent place on the archaeological map of India.

name: Srirangapatna
tagline: Kaveri river island fortress of Tipu Sultan
overview: Srirangapatna or Srirangapattana is a town and headquarters of one of the seven Taluks of Mandya district, in the Indian state of Karnataka. It gets its name from the Ranganathaswamy Temple consecrated around 984 CE.

name: Wayanad
tagline: Emerald spice hills, Edakkal caves, and wildlife
overview: Wayanad district (Malayalam: [ʋɐjɐnaːɖɨ̆]), or Wynad, is a district in the north-east of the Indian state of Kerala, with its administrative headquarters at the municipality of Kalpetta. It is the only plateau in Kerala.

name: Kovalam
tagline: Crescent beaches framed by a striped lighthouse
overview: Kovalam (Malayalam: [koːʋɐɭɐm]) is a beach and seaside resort in the city of Thiruvananthapuram in Kerala, India. Kovalam is located 12.6 km (7.8 mi) southeast of the city center.

name: Kumarakom
tagline: Vembanad Lake bird sanctuary and serene canals
overview: Kumarakom is a tourism destination near the city of Kottayam in Kerala, India. It is near the Vembanad Lake, the largest lake in the state of Kerala.

name: Bekal Fort
tagline: Keyhole-shaped laterite sea fort in Kasaragod
overview: Bekal Fort (Malayalam: [beːkːɐl]) is a medieval fort built by Shivappa Nayaka of Keladi in 1650 AD, at Bekal. It is the largest fort in Kerala, spreading over 40 acres (160,000 m2)

name: Thrissur
tagline: Cultural capital famed for Vadakkunnathan and Pooram
overview: Thrissur (Malayalam: തൃശൂർ, pronounced [triˈʃ(ː)uːr] ), formerly Trichur, also known by its historical name Thrissivaperur (Thiru-siva-perur), is a city and the headquarters of the Thrissur district in Kerala, India. It is the third largest urban agglomeration in Kerala after Kochi and Kozhikode, and the 21st largest in India.

name: Guruvayur
tagline: Historic Krishna pilgrimage town near Thrissur
overview: Guruvayur IPA: [guɾuʋɐːjuːr]) is a municipal temple town in Thrissur district, of Kerala State in India. It is a suburban town of Thrissur city, located 26 kilometres (16 mi) from Thrissur towards the north-west.

name: Yercaud
tagline: Shevaroy Hills coffee town around Emerald Lake
overview: Yercaud or Erkadu, is a town and hill station in Salem District in Tamil Nadu, India. Located in Servarayan Hills in the Eastern Ghats, it is situated at an altitude of 1,515 m (4,970 ft).

name: Velankanni
tagline: Coromandel coast basilica and pilgrim shoreline
overview: Velankanni (Vēḷāṅkaṇṇi) is a special grade town panchayat in Nagapattinam district in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It lies on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal, 350 km south of Chennai (Madras), 12 km south of Nagapattinam, and 33 km southeast of Thiruvarur.

name: Tharangambadi
tagline: Danish-era Fort Dansborg by the Bay of Bengal
overview: Tharangambadi (Tamil: [t̪aɾaŋgambaːɖi]), formerly Tranquebar (Danish: Trankebar, pronounced [ˈtsʰʁɑŋkəˌpɑˀ]), is a town in the Mayiladuthurai district of the Indian state of Tamil Nadu on the Coromandel Coast. It lies 15 kilometres (9.3 mi) north of Karaikal, near the mouth of a distributary named Uppanar of the Kaveri River.

name: Tiruchirappalli
tagline: Rockfort Temple and Srirangam island complex
overview: Thiruchchirappalli (Tamil pronunciation: [ˈt̪iɾɯtːʃiɾapːaɭːi] ), also known as Tiruchchi or Trichy or historically known as Trichinopoly, is a major tier II city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu and the administrative headquarters of Tiruchirappalli district. The city is credited with being the most livable and cleanest city in all of Tamil Nadu, as…

name: Chidambaram
tagline: Nataraja temple complex and Pichavaram mangroves
overview: Chidambaram (also known as Thillai) is a major town and municipality in Cuddalore district in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu, on the banks of the Vellar River where it meets the Bay of Bengal. It is the headquarters of the Chidambaram taluk.

name: Kumbakonam
tagline: Chola temple town and brass craft workshops
overview: Kumbakonam or Kudanthai is a city municipal corporation in the Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu, India. Located 40 km (25 mi) from Thanjavur and 282 km (175 mi) from Chennai and it is the headquarters of the Kumbakonam taluk.

name: Auroville
tagline: Experimental township centered on the golden Matrimandir
overview: Auroville (; City of Dawn French: Cité de l'aube) is an experimental township in Viluppuram district, mostly in the state of Tamil Nadu, India, with some parts in the Union Territory of Puducherry in India. It was founded in 1968 by Mirra Alfassa (known as "the Mother" or "La Mère") and designed by architect Roger Anger.

name: Karaikal
tagline: Quiet coastal enclave with French boulevards and temples
overview: Karaikal (, Tamil: [kaːɾɐi̯kːaːl], French: Karikal [kaʁikal]) is a port city of the Indian Union Territory of Puducherry. It is the administrative headquarters of the Karaikal District and the second-largest city in the territory after its capital, Pondicherry.

name: Ramoji Film City
tagline: Sprawling studio complex and themed gardens near Hyderabad
overview: Ramoji Film City is an integrated film studio facility located right outside of Hyderabad, India. Spread over 2,000 acres (810 ha), it was recognized as the world's largest film studio complex by the Guinness World Records in 2005.

name: Visakhapatnam
tagline: Port city of Kailasagiri hills and Rushikonda Beach
overview: Visakhapatnam (English: /vɪˌsɑːkəˈpʌtnəm/, Telugu: [ʋiʃaːkʰɐpɐʈnɐm]; formerly known as Vizagapatam, and also referred to as Vizag, Visakha, and Waltair) is the largest and most populous city in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It is between the Eastern Ghats and the coast of the Bay of Bengal.

name: Lepakshi
tagline: Vijayanagara Veerabhadra temple and hanging pillar
overview: Lepakshi is a village in the Sri Sathya Sai district of Andhra Pradesh, India. It is situated15 km (9.3 miles) eastward of Hindupur, 82 km (51 miles) westward of Kadiri and 120 km (75 mi) north of Bangalore.

name: Srisailam
tagline: Nallamala forest Jyotirlinga overlooking Krishna gorge
overview: Srisailam is a census town in Nandyal district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It is the mandal headquarters of Srisailam mandal in Atmakur revenue division.

name: Bhubaneswar
tagline: City of Kalinga sandstone temples like Lingaraja
overview: Bhubaneswar (/bʊbəˈneɪswəɹ/; Odia: [ˈbʱubɔneswɔɾɔ] ), also known as Bhubaneswara, is the capital and the largest city of the Indian state of Odisha. It is located in the Khordha district.

name: Simlipal National Park
tagline: Sal forests, Joranda waterfall, and biosphere reserve
overview: Simlipal National Park (ISO: Śimiḷipāḷa Jātīya Udyāna) is a national park and tiger reserve in the Mayurbhanj district in the Indian state of Odisha covering 2,750 km2 (1,060 sq mi). It is part of the Mayurbhanj Elephant Reserve, which includes three protected areas, Simlipal Tiger Reserve, Hadgarh Wildlife Sanctuary with 191.06 km2 (73.77 sq mi) and…

name: Bhitarkanika National Park
tagline: Estuarine mangrove creeks and saltwater crocodiles
overview: Bhitarkanika National Park is a 145 km2 (56 sq mi) national park in northeast Kendrapara district in Odisha in eastern India. It was designated on 16 September 1998 and obtained the status of a Ramsar site on 19 August 2002.

name: Kalimpong
tagline: Himalayan ridge town of monasteries and flower nurseries
overview: Kalimpong is a town and the headquarters of an eponymous district in the Indian state of West Bengal. It is located at an average elevation of 1,250 metres (4,101 ft).

name: Santiniketan
tagline: Visva-Bharati campus founded by Rabindranath Tagore
overview: Santiniketan (IPA: [ʃantiniketɔn]) is a neighbourhood of Bolpur town in the Bolpur subdivision of Birbhum district in West Bengal, India, approximately 152 km north of Kolkata. It was established by Debendranath Tagore, and later expanded by his son, Rabindranath Tagore whose vision became what is now a university town with the creation of Visva-Bharati.

name: Murshidabad
tagline: Hazarduari Palace and Bengal Nawabi river heritage
overview: Murshidabad (Bengali pronunciation: [murʃidabad]) is a town in the Indian state of West Bengal. This town is the headquarters of Lalbag subdivision of Murshidabad district.

name: Jaldapara National Park
tagline: Dooars tall grasslands and one-horned rhinos
overview: Jaldapara National Park (Pron: ˌʤʌldəˈpɑ:rə) is a national park situated at the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas in Alipurduar District of northern West Bengal, India, and on the banks of the Torsa River. It is situated at an elevation of 61 m (200 ft) and is spread across 216.51 km2 (83.59 sq mi) of vast grassland with patches of riverine forest.

name: Gorumara National Park
tagline: Riverine forests of Murti and Jaldhaka in Dooars
overview: Gorumara National Park (Pron: ˌgɔ:rʊˈmɑ:rə; Gorumara Jatio Uddan) is a national park in northern West Bengal, India. Located in the Dooars region of the Himalayan foothills, it is a medium-sized park with grasslands and forests.

name: Purulia
tagline: Chhau mask villages and Ayodhya Hills granite peaks
overview: Purulia, officially Purulia Sadar, is a city and a municipality in the Indian state of West Bengal. It is the headquarters of the Purulia district and is located on the north of the Kangsabati River.

name: Rajgir
tagline: Ringed hills of Vishwa Shanti Stupa and hot springs
overview: Rajgir (old name Rajagriha, meaning "The City of Kings") is an ancient city and university town in the Nalanda district of Bihar, India. It is also considered a cultural capital of Magadh.

name: Sasaram
tagline: Lake-encircled sandstone tomb of Sher Shah Suri
overview: Sasaram (), also spelled as Shahasaram and Sasseram, is a historical city and a municipal corporation region in the Rohtas district of Bihar state in eastern India. The city served as the capital of the Sur dynasty during Sher Shah Suri's rule over India in the 16th century, and was residence place sub capital of epic monarch Sahasrabahu (Kartivirya Arjuna).

name: Valmiki Tiger Reserve
tagline: Himalayan foothill forest on the Gandak river
overview: Valmiki National Park is a national park and tiger reserve in the West Champaran District of Bihar, India covering 898.45 km2 (346.89 sq mi). It is the only National park in Bihar.

name: Ujjain
tagline: Shipra river ghats and Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga
overview: Ujjain (, Hindi pronunciation: [ʊ̯d͡ːʑæn] , [əʋən̪t̪ɪkaː]), also known as Ujjayini, is a city in Ujjain district of the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh. It is the fifth-largest city in Madhya Pradesh by population and is the administrative as well as religious centre of Ujjain district and Ujjain division.

name: Pachmarhi
tagline: Satpura biosphere hill station of sandstone caves and falls
overview: Pachmarhi is a hill station in Madhya Pradesh state of central India. It has been the location of a cantonment (Pachmarhi Cantonment) since the British Raj.

name: Kanha National Park
tagline: Sal meadows and hard-ground barasingha sanctuary
overview: Kanha Tiger Reserve, also known as Kanha–Kisli National Park, is one of the tiger reserves of India and the largest national park of the state of Madhya Pradesh. It covers an area of 940 km2 (360 sq mi) in the two districts Mandla and Balaghat.

name: Bandhavgarh National Park
tagline: Vindhya hill grasslands and ancient forest fort
overview: Bandhavgarh National Park is a national park of India, located in the Umaria district of Madhya Pradesh. It spreads over an area of 105 km2 (41 sq mi) and was declared a national park in 1968.

name: Omkareshwar
tagline: Om-shaped Narmada river island pilgrimage town
overview: Omkareshwar Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva, located in Mandhata, nearby Khandwa city in Khandwa district of the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh. It is one of the 12 revered Jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva.

name: Maheshwar
tagline: Ahilya Fort ghats and handloom Maheshwari sarees
overview: Maheshwar is a town in Khargone district of Madhya Pradesh state, in central India. It is located on State Highway-38 (Khargone city-Barwaha- Bandheri Highway),13.5 km east of National Highway 3 (Agra-Mumbai highway) and 91 km from Indore, the commercial capital of the state.

name: Satpura National Park
tagline: Walking safaris and canoeing through rugged Satpura hills
overview: Satpura Tiger Reserve is a tiger reserve located in the Narmadapuram district of Madhya Pradesh in India. Its name is derived from the Satpura range.

name: Chanderi
tagline: Medieval fort, stepwells, and sheer Chanderi silk
overview: Chanderi, is a town of historical importance in Ashoknagar District of the state Madhya Pradesh in India. It is situated at a distance of 127 km from Shivpuri, 38 km from Lalitpur, 57 km from Ashok Nagar, 348 km from Jhansi and 46 km from Isagarh.

name: Netarhat
tagline: Chotanagpur plateau sunrise point and pine groves
overview: Netarhat is a hill station in Latehar district in the Indian state of Jharkhand. The hill station is among the highest points of the Chotanagpur plateau.

name: Betla National Park
tagline: Palamau forest reserve and historic Chero forts
overview: Betla National Park is a national park located in the Latehar and Palamu district of Jharkhand, India. Its the only national park in the state.

name: Parasnath Hill
tagline: Sacred Shikharji peak and highest summit in Jharkhand
overview: Parasnath Hill (also Sammet Shikhar, Marang Buru) is a mountain peak in the Parasnath hill range. It is located towards the eastern end of the Chota Nagpur Plateau in the Giridih district (Hazaribagh district in British India) of the Indian state of Jharkhand.

name: Ranchi
tagline: City of waterfalls, Tagore Hill, and Kanke Dam
overview: Ranchi (Hindi: rāñcī, pronounced [ˈɾaːɲt͡ɕiː]) is the capital city and largest district by population in the Indian state of Jharkhand. Ranchi was the centre of the Jharkhand movement, which called for a separate state for the tribal regions of South Bihar, northern Odisha, western West Bengal and the eastern area of what is present-day Chhattisgarh.

name: Attari-Wagah Border
tagline: Ceremonial lowering-of-flags border crossing near Amritsar
overview: Wagah (; Punjabi: واگھا [ʋäː˦ˈgä]; Urdu: واہگہ [ˈwɑːɦˌgɑː]), also spelled Wagha or Wahga, is a village located in Wagah Tehsil of Lahore District in the Punjab province of Pakistan. The town is famous for the Wagah border ceremony and also serves as a goods transit terminal and a railway station between Pakistan and India.

name: Patiala
tagline: Qila Mubarak, Sheesh Mahal, and royal Punjabi heritage
overview: Patiala (Punjabi pronunciation: [pʌʈeɑ̈ːɭɑ]) is a city in southeastern Punjab, northwestern India. It is the fourth largest city in the state and is the administrative capital of Patiala district.

name: Kapurthala
tagline: Jagatjit Palace and Moorish Mosque architecture
overview: Kapurthala (Punjabi pronunciation: [kə.puːɾ.t̪ʰə.läː]) is a city in the Punjab state of India. It is the administrative headquarters of the Kapurthala District.

name: Red Fort
tagline: Shah Jahan’s sandstone Mughal citadel on the Yamuna
overview: The Red Fort (Lal Qila in Hindi; Hindi pronunciation: [laːl 'qɪlaː]) is a historic Mughal fort located in the Old Delhi area of Delhi, India. Serving as the main residence of the Mughal emperors, it was commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan on the 12th of May 1639; the fort was constructed following his decision to shift the Mughal capital from Agra to Delhi.

name: Humayun’s Tomb
tagline: UNESCO Charbagh garden mausoleum in Nizamuddin
overview: Humayun's tomb (Persian: Maqbara-i Humayun) is the tomb of the Mughal Emperor Humayun located in Delhi, India. The tomb was commissioned by Humayun's first wife and chief consort, Empress Bega Begum, under her patronage in 1558, and designed by the Persian architects Mirak Mirza Ghiyas and his son, Sayyid Muhammad, whom she personally chose.

name: India Gate
tagline: Iconic sandstone war memorial arch on Kartavya Path
overview: The India Gate (formerly known as All India War Memorial) is a war memorial arch that’s located near the Rajpath (officially called Kartavya Path) on the eastern edge of the "ceremonial axis" of New Delhi, India. It stands as a memorial to exactly 74,187 Indian soldiers of the British Indian Army who died between 1914 and 1921 during the First World War,…

name: Lodhi Gardens
tagline: 15th-century Sayyid and Lodi tombs in landscaped lawns
overview: Lodi Gardens is a city park situated in New Delhi. Spread over 90 acres (360,000 m2), it contains Muhammad Shah's tomb, the tomb of Sikandar Lodi, the Shisha Gumbad and the Bara Gumbad.

name: Hauz Khas
tagline: Medieval madrasa ruins overlooking Deer Park lake
overview: Hauz Khas Complex in Hauz Khas, South Delhi, India, houses a water tank, an Islamic seminary, a mosque, a tomb, and pavilions built around an urbanized village with a medieval history traced to the 13th century of Delhi Sultanate reign. It was part of Siri, the second medieval city of India of the Delhi Sultanate of Alauddin Khalji Dynasty (1296–1316).

name: Kurukshetra
tagline: Sacred Brahma Sarovar and Mahabharata heritage town
overview: Kurukshetra (Hindi: kurukṣetra, pronounced [kʊrʊkʃeːtɾə]) is a historical region in India, also known as Dharmakshetra ("Realm of duty") and as the "Land of the Bhagavad Gita". It also refers to the city Kurukshetra, situated in the area and administrative headquarters of Kurukshetra district in the Indian state of Haryana.

name: Sukhna Lake
tagline: Shivalik-backed promenade reservoir designed by Le Corbusier
overview: Sukhna Lake is a reservoir and wetland hosting the Sukhna Wildlife Sanctuary located in Chandigarh, India, at the Shivalik hills of the Himalayas. This 3 km2 rain-fed lake was created in 1958 by damming the Sukhna Choe, a seasonal stream coming down from the Shivalik hills.

name: Mussoorie
tagline: Queen of the Hills overlooking the Doon Valley
overview: Mussoorie (Garhwali: [məsuːɾiː]) is a hill station and a municipal board in the Dehradun district of the Indian state of Uttarakhand. It is about 26 kilometres (16 mi) from the state Winter capital Dehradun and 289 km (180 mi) north of the national capital of New Delhi.

name: Haridwar
tagline: Ganga enters the plains at sacred Har Ki Pauri
overview: Haridwar (; Hindi: [ɦəɾɪd̪waːɾ] ; formerly Mayapuri) is a city and municipal corporation in the Haridwar district of Uttarakhand, India. With a population of 228,832 according to 2011 census, it is the second-largest city in the state and the largest in the district.

name: Badrinath
tagline: High-altitude Garhwal shrine flanked by Nar-Narayan peaks
overview: Badrinath is a town and nagar panchayat in Chamoli district in the state of Uttarakhand, India. It is a Hindu holy place, and is one of the four sites in India's Char Dham pilgrimage.

name: Jim Corbett National Park
tagline: India’s oldest national park along the Ramganga river
overview: Jim Corbett National Park is a national park in the Nainital district of the state of Uttarakhand, India. It was established in 1936 as the country's first national park and is named in honour of Jim Corbett, who had played a leading role in its establishment.

name: Gangotri
tagline: Sacred Bhagirathi river origin shrine at 3,100 m
overview: Gangotri is a town and a Nagar Panchayat (municipality) in Uttarkashi district in the state of Uttarakhand, India. It is 99 km from Uttarkashi, the main district headquarter.

name: Yamunotri
tagline: Thermal springs and alpine source shrine of the Yamuna
overview: Yamunotri, also Jamnotri, is the source of the Yamuna River and the seat of the Goddess Yamuna in Hinduism. It is situated at an altitude of 3,293 metres (10,804 ft) in the Garhwal Himalayas and located approximately 150 kilometres (93 mi) North of Uttarkashi, the headquarters of the Uttarkashi district in the Garhwal Division of Uttarakhand, India.

name: Dharamshala
tagline: Dhauladhar foothill valley of cricket and monasteries
overview: Dharamshala (, Hindi: [d̪ʱərmʃaːlaː]; also spelled Dharamsala) is a town in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh. It serves as the winter capital of the state and the administrative headquarters of the Kangra district since 1855.

name: Dalhousie
tagline: Five-hill colonial retreat near Chamba
overview: Dalhousie (Hindi pronunciation: [ɖəlɦɔːziː]) is a hill station, near the town of Chamba in Chamba district in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh. It is situated across five hills and has an elevation of 1,970 m (6,460 ft) above sea level.

name: Khajjiar
tagline: Cedar-ringed emerald saucer meadow in Chamba
overview: Khajjiar is a hill station near the town of Chamba in Chamba district of Himachal Pradesh, India. Located approximately 24 kilometres (15 mi) from Dalhousie, it lies on a small plateau about 2,000 meters (6,500 feet) above sea level in the foothills of the Dhauladhar ranges in the Western Himalayas.

name: Kalpa
tagline: Kinnaur apple village facing the Kinner Kailash massif
overview: Kalpa is a small village lying above Reckong Peo, the district headquarters of the Kinnaur district, Himachal Pradesh state, north India. Geographically, Kalpa lies in the Sutlej river valley of the Indian Himalaya.

name: Chitkul
tagline: Last inhabited village along the Baspa River border trail
overview: Chitkul is a village in Kinnaur district of Himachal Pradesh. During winters, the place mostly remains covered with snow and the inhabitants move to lower regions of Himachal.

name: Kullu
tagline: Beas river valley of Dussehra traditions and handlooms
overview: Kullu (Hindi: [kʊlːuː]) is a municipal council town that serves as the administrative headquarters of the Kullu district of the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh. It is located on the banks of the Beas River in the Kullu Valley about 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) north of the airport at Bhuntar, Kullu.

name: Keylong
tagline: Lahaul valley crossroads above the Bhaga River
overview: Kyelang (also spelled Keylong) is a town and the administrative centre of the Lahaul and Spiti district in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh, 71 kilometres (44 mi) north of Manali via Atal Tunnel and 120 km (75 mi) from the Indo-Tibetan border. It is located along the Manali-Leh Highway and on the banks of the Bhaga River.

name: Chamba
tagline: Ancient Ravi river town of Chamba rumal and Chaugan
overview: Chamba is a town in the Chamba district in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh. According to the 2001 Indian census, Chamba has a population of 20,312.

name: Kasauli
tagline: Misty lower-Himalayan ridge walk and Gilbert Trail
overview: Kasauli (Hindi: [kəsɔːliː]) is a town and cantonment located in Solan district of the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh. The cantonment was established by the British Raj in 1842 as a Colonial hill station, 25 km (16 mi) from Solan, 77 km (48 mi) from Shimla, 58 km (36 mi) from Chandigarh, and 94 km (58 mi) from Ambala Cantt (Haryana), an important…

name: Sonamarg
tagline: Meadow of Gold leading toward Thajiwas Glacier
overview: Sonamarg or Sonmarg (Urdu pronunciation: [soːnɑːməɾɡ]), known as Sonamarag (Kashmiri pronunciation: [sɔnɨmarɨɡ]; lit. 'meadow of gold') in Kashmiri, is a hill station located in the Ganderbal District of Jammu and Kashmir, India in the disputed Kashmir region.

name: Gurez Valley
tagline: Remote Kishanganga valley framed by Habba Khatoon peak
overview: Gurez, or Gurais (Guráai in Shina language), is a tehsil in Bandipore District in Jammu and Kashmir in India. It contains most of the Gurez Valley, located in the high Himalayas to the north of the Kashmir Valley, separated from it by the great Himalayan range, and is situated about 86 kilometres (53 mi) from district headquarters Bandipore and 123…

name: Pangong Tso
tagline: High-altitude cobalt salt lake stretching into Tibet
overview: Pangong Tso or Pangong Lake is an endorheic lake spanning eastern Ladakh in India and Ngari Prefecture in Tibet. Situated at an elevation of 14,200 ft (4,300 m), it occupies an area of approximately 604 km2 (233 sq mi).

photoCredit.author: Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, NASA Johnson Space Center

name: Nubra Valley
tagline: Sand dunes of Hunder and Diskit across Khardung La
overview: Nubra, also called Dumra, is a historical region of Ladakh, India in the Nubra district. Its inhabited areas form a tri-armed valley cut by the Nubra and Shyok rivers.

name: Tso Moriri
tagline: Remote Changthang glacial lake above 4,500 m
overview: Tso Moriri or Lake Moriri (Tibetan: ལྷ་མོའི་བླ་མཚོ, Wylie: lha mo bla mtsho, 'Mountain Lake'), 4,522 m (14,836 ft), is a high-altitude lake and a Ramsar wetland site in the remote Changthang Plateau (literally: northern plains) in the Changthang district of the union territory of Ladakh in India. As the largest high-altitude lake entirely within India…

name: Kargil
tagline: Suru river valley crossroads between Srinagar and Leh
overview: Kargil (English: /ˈkɑrɡɪl/ KAR-ghil, Hindi: [kaːɾɡɪl]) or Kargyil is a city and headquarter of the eponymous district, tehsil, and community development block of Indian-administered Ladakh in the disputed Kashmir region. It is the joint capital of Ladakh, an Indian-administered union territory, and the headquarters of the Kargil district.

name: Zanskar Valley
tagline: High-altitude river valley of Padum and Phugtal
overview: Zanskar is an administrative district in the Union Territory of Ladakh in India with headquarters at Padum. It was carved out of the Kargil district in 2026 to give autonomy to this historically isolated Himalayan region.

name: Sivasagar
tagline: Ahom capital of Rang Ghar, Talatal Ghar, and tanks
overview: Sivasagar (Assamese: [xi.βɔ.xaɡɔ(ɹ)]) is a city and headquarter of the Sivasagar district, Assam. It is known for its Ahom palaces and monuments.

name: Guwahati
tagline: Brahmaputra gateway city with Umananda river island
overview: Guwahati (Assamese: [ɡua.ɦa.ti]), formerly known as Gauhati, is the largest city of the Indian state of Assam, and the largest metropolis in northeastern India. Dispur, the capital of Assam, is in the circuit city region located within Guwahati and is the seat of the Government of Assam.

name: Haflong
tagline: Assam’s sole hill station in Dima Hasao
overview: Haflong is a town and the headquarters of the Dima Hasao district of the northeast Indian state of Assam. It is the only hill station in the state.

name: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park
tagline: Brahmaputra river-island wetlands and feral horses
overview: Dibru-Saikhowa National Park is a national park in Dibrugarh and Tinsukia districts, Assam, India. It was designated a Biosphere Reserve in July 1997 with an area of 765 km2 (295 sq mi), including a core area of 340 km2 (130 sq mi) and a buffer zone of 425 km2 (164 sq mi).

name: Shillong
tagline: Pine-clad capital of waterfalls, cafés, and live music
overview: Shillong (English: , Khasi: [ʃɨlːɔːŋ]), the capital of Meghalaya, India, is a hill station and the headquarters of the East Khasi Hills district. It is the 330th most populous city in India, with a population of 143,229 according to the 2011 census.

name: Namdapha National Park
tagline: Biodiverse rainforest stretching from plains to snow peaks
overview: Namdapha National Park is a 1,985.23 km2 (766.50 sq mi) large national park in Arunachal Pradesh of Northeast India. The park was established in 1983.

name: Sela Pass
tagline: Snowy 13,700 ft mountain pass with Sela Lake
overview: The Sela Pass (Tibetan: གཟེ་ལ།) (more appropriately called Se La, as La means Pass in Tibetan language) is a high-altitude mountain pass located on the border between the Tawang and West Kameng districts in the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh. It has an elevation of 4170 m (13,700 ft) and connects the Indian Buddhist town of Tawang to Dirang and Guwahati.

name: Pasighat
tagline: Oldest town in Arunachal where the Siang exits the gorges
overview: Pasighat is the headquarters of East Siang district in the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh. Situated at the eastern foothills of the Himalayas at 155 metres (509 ft) above mean sea level, Pasighat is Arunachal's oldest town.

name: Imphal
tagline: Kangla Fort, Ima Keithel women’s market, and valley hills
overview: Imphal (UK: IM-fahl, US: IMP-hul; Meitei: [impʰal]) is the capital city of the Indian state of Manipur. The metropolitan centre of the city contains the ruins of Kangla Palace (officially known as Kangla Fort), the royal seat of the former Kingdom of Manipur, surrounded by a moat.

name: Dzüko Valley
tagline: Seasonal lily-carpeted valley on the Manipur-Nagaland border
overview: The Dzukou Valley (also spelt Dzüko, Dzükou or Dzukuo) is a high-altitude valley in Northeast India, straddling the inter-state border of the states of Nagaland and Manipur. Lying behind Mount Japfü at an elevation between 2,438 and 2,452 m (7,999 and 8,045 ft) above sea level in the Kohima and Senapati districts, it is known for its rolling meadows,…

name: Ukhrul
tagline: Tangkhul hill town famous for Shirui Lily peak
overview: Ukhrul (Tangkhul pronunciation:/ˈuːkˌɹəl or ˈuːkˌɹʊl/ is the headquarters of Ukhrul district, one of the hilly district in the state of Manipur, India. Ukhrul is the home of the Tangkhul Nagas.

name: Kohima
tagline: Angami hill capital of WWII cemetery and Japfu slopes
overview: Kohima ( ; Tenyidie: Kewhira (IPA: [ˈkɛʍɪɻə])) is the capital of the North East Indian state of Nagaland. With a resident population of almost 100,000, it is the second largest city in the state.

name: Vantawng Falls
tagline: Highest waterfall in Mizoram plunging into bamboo forest
overview: The Vantawng Khawhthla is located 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) south of Thenzawl in Serchhip district in the Indian state of Mizoram. It is the highest uninterrupted waterfall in Mizoram.

name: Champhai
tagline: Terraced rice bowl overlooking the Chin Hills
overview: Champhai is the third largest town in Mizoram, northeast India and is one of the oldest settlements founded by the Mizo people that initially served as a capital for the Hmar dynasty. Located near the India–Myanmar border, it facilitates cross-border trade and serves as a hub for trade and commerce in the region.

name: Agartala
tagline: Ujjayanta Palace gardens and royal Tripura heritage
overview: Agartala (, Bengali: [ˈagɔɾˌtɔla] , Kok Borok: [aguli]) is the capital and the largest city of the Indian state of Tripura, situated on the banks of Haora/Saidra River, about 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) east of the border with Bangladesh and about 2,499 km (1,552 mi) from the national capital, New Delhi. According to 2022 AMC data, Agartala is the second most…

name: Lachung
tagline: Apple-orchard mountain village en route to Yumthang
overview: Lachung is a town and hill station in Mangan district in the Indian state of Sikkim. It is about 50 km from Mangan, the district headquarters.

name: Yumthang Valley
tagline: Valley of Flowers alpine meadow carpeted in rhododendrons
overview: The Yumthang Valley or Sikkim Valley of Flowers sanctuary, is a nature sanctuary with river, hot springs, yaks and grazing pasture on rolling meadows surrounded by the Himalayan mountains in Yumthang in the Mangan district of Sikkim state in India. It is approx.

name: Yuksom
tagline: First capital of Sikkim and Dzongri trek trailhead
overview: Yuksom (Nepali pronunciation: [jaksom]), also spelt Yuksum, is a historical town about 40 km north of Gyalshing in the Gyalshing district, in the northeast Indian state of Sikkim. It was the first capital of the Kingdom of Sikkim, established in 1642 by Phuntsog Namgyal, the first Chogyal of Sikkim.

name: Namchi
tagline: South Sikkim hilltop home to Char Dham and Samdruptse
overview: Namchi is a town and the administrative headquarters of the South Sikkim district in the Indian state of Sikkim.

name: Gurudongmar Lake
tagline: Sacred glacial lake at 17,800 ft in North Sikkim
overview: Gurudongmar Lake is one of the highest lakes in the world and in India, at an elevation of 5,430 m (17,800 ft) according to the Government of Sikkim. It is located in the Great Himalayas in the Mangan district in Indian state of Sikkim, and considered sacred by Buddhists.

name: Tsomgo Lake
tagline: Glacial mountain lake along the Nathu La road
overview: Tsomgo Lake, also known as Tsongmo Lake or Changgu Lake, is a glacial lake in Changu in the Gangtok district of the Indian state of Sikkim, some 40 kilometres (25 mi) from the capital Gangtok. Located at an elevation of 3,753 m (12,313 ft), the lake remains frozen during the winter season.

name: Baratang Island
tagline: Limestone caves, mud volcanoes, and mangrove creeks
overview: Baratang Island is an island of the Andaman Islands. It belongs to the North and Middle Andaman administrative district, part of the Indian union territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
