name: Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair)
tagline: Island capital, Corbyn’s Cove, and Samudrika museum
overview: Port Blair (), officially named Sri Vijaya Puram (Hindi pronunciation: [ˌɕɾˈɨː ˈʋɪ̯ˌd͡ʑʌjᵊ pʊˈɾ.əm]), is the capital city of the Indian union territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It is located on the South Andaman Island situated between the Bay of Bengal to the west and the Andaman Sea to the east.

name: Jabalpur
tagline: Narmada river city of Dhuandhar Falls and Madan Mahal
overview: Jabalpur (IPA: [ˈd͡ʐəˌbəlpʊɾ]), formerly anglicised as Jubbulpore, is the fourth largest city by area of the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh. It is situated on the banks of the Narmada River in the state of Madhya Pradesh, India.

name: Indore
tagline: Rajwada Palace and Sarafa night street-food bazaar
overview: Indore ( ; ISO: Indaura, Hindi: [ɪn̪d̪ɔːr]) is the largest city of the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh where it serves as the capital and the administrative headquarters of the eponymous district and division. Modern-day Indore was established on the banks of the Kanh and Saraswati rivers and traces its roots to its 16th-century founding as a trading hub…

name: Bhopal
tagline: City of Lakes, Upper Lake boat club, and tribal museum
overview: Bhopal (Hindi: Bhōpāl, pronounced [bʱoːpaːl] ) is the capital city of the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh and the administrative headquarters of both Bhopal district and Bhopal division. It is known as the City of Lakes, due to presence of various natural and artificial lakes near the city boundary.

name: Ahmedabad
tagline: UNESCO walled pols, Sabarmati Ashram, and stepwells
overview: Ahmedabad ( AH-mə-də-ba(h)d, Hindustani: [ɛʱ(ɛ).m(ə).d̪ɑː.bɑːd̪]), also spelt Amdavad (Gujarati: [ˈəmdɑʋɑd]) and historically known as Karnavati (Sanskrit: [kɐrɳaːʋɐt̪iː]), is the most populous city in the Indian state of Gujarat. It is the administrative headquarters of the Ahmedabad district and the seat of the Gujarat High Court.

name: Surat
tagline: Tapi river port, Dumas coast, and diamond craft city
overview: Surat (Gujarati: [suːɾət̪]) is a city in the western Indian state of Gujarat. The word Surat directly translates to countenance in Gujarati, Hindi and Urdu.

name: Porbandar
tagline: Arabian Sea port and Kirti Mandir birthplace of Gandhi
overview: Porbandar is a city and the headquarters of the Porbandar district in the Indian state of Gujarat. It is the birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi and Sudama.

name: Kochi
tagline: Spice port of backwaters, Mattancherry, and Marine Drive
overview: Kochi ( KOH-chee, Malayalam: [kotˈt͡ʃi] ), formerly known as Cochin ( KOH-chin), is a major port city along the Malabar Coast of India bordering the Laccadive Sea. It is part of the district of Ernakulam in the state of Kerala and is the financial, industrial and commercial capital of the state.

name: Thiruvananthapuram
tagline: Padmanabhaswamy Temple and Napier Museum gardens
overview: Thiruvananthapuram (Malayalam pronunciation: [t̪iɾuʋənən̪d̪ɐˈbuɾəm] tirr-ROO-və-nun-Tə-poor-əm), also known as Trivandrum, is the capital city of the Indian state of Kerala. As of 2011, the Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation had a population of 957,730 over an area of 214.86 km2, making it the most populous city in Kerala.

name: Kozhikode
tagline: Malabar spice shore, Kappad Beach, and SM Street
overview: Kozhikode (pronounced [koːɻikːoːɖɨ̆] ), also known as Calicut, is a historic city along the Malabar Coast in the state of Kerala in India. The city is also known as the City of Spices.

name: Tawang
tagline: High Himalayan town of Sela views and Monpa heritage
overview: Tawang (Tibetan: རྟ་དབང་, Wylie: Rta-dbang) is a town and administrative headquarter of Tawang district in the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh. It lies on NH-13 section of Trans-Arunachal Highway.

name: Itanagar
tagline: Ita Fort brick ramparts and Ganga Lake hills
overview: Itanagar () is the capital and largest town of the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh. The seat of Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly, the seat of government of Arunachal Pradesh, and the seat of Gauhati High Court permanent bench at Naharlagun are all in Itanagar.

name: Anini
tagline: Misty Dibang valley plateau near Mehao sanctuary
overview: Anini is the headquarters of the Dibang Valley district in the state of Arunachal Pradesh in Northeast India. Anini was also the district headquarters of the undivided Dibang Valley district.

name: Tezpur
tagline: Agnigarh hillock and Da-Parbatia Gupta-era carvings
overview: Tezpur (Assamese: [tɛz.pʊɹ]) is a city in Sonitpur district, Assam state, India. Tezpur is located on the banks of the river Brahmaputra, 175 kilometres (109 mi) northeast of Guwahati, and is the largest of the north bank cities.

name: Umiam Lake
tagline: Pine-bordered reservoir on the Shillong plateau
overview: Nongpoh (Khasi: [nɒŋˈpɒ(ə)]) is the administrative centre of Ri-Bhoi district in the Indian state of Meghalaya. Nongpoh is located on National Highway 40, fifty-two kilometers from the state capital Shillong and forty-eight kilometers from Guwahati in the state of Assam.

name: Tura
tagline: Garo Hills town below misty Tura Peak
overview: Tura (IPA: ˈtʊərə) is a municipality in the West Garo Hills district of the Indian state of Meghalaya. One of the largest towns in Meghalaya, Tura is located in the foothills of the Nokrek range of Garo Hills.

name: Dimapur
tagline: Kachari monolith ruins and Nagaland’s commercial hub
overview: Dimapur () is the largest city and municipality in the Indian state of Nagaland. As of 2024, the municipality had a population of 172,000.

name: Lunglei
tagline: Scenic southern ridge town named after a stone bridge
overview: Lunglei (, locally ), formerly rendered Lungleh, is the second-largest town in Mizoram, northeastern India, situated in the south-central part of the state. The town served as the capital of British South Lushai Hills from 1889 to 1898.

name: Pithoragarh
tagline: Soar Valley fort town on the Kailash Mansarovar route
overview: Pithoragarh (Kumaoni: Pithor'garh) is a Himalayan town and a municipal corporation in Pithoragarh district, Kumaon division, Uttarakhand state, northern India. It is the largest hill town in Uttarakhand.

name: Tehri Lake
tagline: Vast turquoise Himalayan reservoir for water sports
overview: The Tehri Dam is a multi-purpose rock and earth-fill embankment dam on the Bhagirathi River in New Tehri, Tehri Garhwal district in Uttarakhand, India. With a height of 260.5 m (855 ft), it is the tallest dam in India and the 13th-tallest dam in the world.

name: Devprayag
tagline: Sacred confluence of Alaknanda and Bhagirathi rivers
overview: Srinagar is a city and municipal corporation in Pauri Garhwal district in the Indian state of Uttarakhand. It is located about 33 km from Pauri town, the administrative headquarters of Pauri Garhwal district, Uttarakhand, India.

name: Palampur
tagline: Kangra tea gardens below snow-dusted Dhauladhar peaks
overview: Palampur is a hill station and a municipal corporation situated in the Kangra District in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh. Palampur is served by the Palampur Himachal railway station (PLMX), situated in Maranda.

photoCredit.author: Sumeet Jain from San Francisco, USA

name: Kangra Fort
tagline: Ancient Katoch stone fortress overlooking Banganga
overview: The Kangra Fort is a historic fort located in the Kangra district of Himachal Pradesh, India. The fort is also known as 'Nagarkot' and 'Kot Kangra'.

name: Mashobra
tagline: Quiet cedar reserve forest above Shimla
overview: Mashobra is a town in Shimla district of Himachal Pradesh. It is connected to the state capital Shimla (erstwhile Simla) through the historic Hindustan–Tibet Road built in 1850 by Lord Dalhousie.

name: Prashar Lake
tagline: Floating-island alpine lake with pagoda temple
overview: Parashar Lake is a freshwater lake located at an elevation of 2,730 metres (8,960 ft) in the Mandi district of Himachal Pradesh, India. It lies 12 km (7.5 mi) north of the town of Mandi, and has a three storied pagoda-like temple dedicated to the sage Parashara situated on its bank.

name: Bhaderwah
tagline: Mini Kashmir meadow valley in Doda district
overview: Bhaderwah (also spelled Bhadarwah, locally also known as Bhadarkashi) is a town and a tehsil in the Doda district of Jammu Division of Jammu and Kashmir, India.

name: Amritsar
tagline: Vibrant walled bazaars, Gobindgarh Fort, and langar heritage
overview: Amritsar, also known as Ambarsar, is a city in the northwestern Indian state of Punjab, 28 kilometres (17 mi) from the border with Pakistan. It is the second-largest city in Punjab, after Ludhiana.

name: Phillaur Fort
tagline: Sutlej-side Mughal sarai turned historic fortress
overview: Ludhiana (Panjabi: Ludhiāṇā, pronounced [lʊ́d̪͜tɪ̀ɪˈäːɳäː]) is the most populous city in the Indian state of Punjab. The city has an estimated population of 1,618,879 as of the 2011 census and distributed over 310 km2 (120 sq mi), making Ludhiana the most densely populated urban centre in the state.

name: Qila Mubarak, Bathinda
tagline: 1,800-year-old brick fort on the Malwa plains
overview: Bathinda (Punjabi pronunciation: [bəʈʰɪ˩˥ɳɖä]) is a city and municipal corporation in Punjab, India. The city is the administrative headquarters of Bathinda district.

name: Karnal
tagline: Karna Lake and historic Grand Trunk Road town
overview: Karnal (Punjabi pronunciation: [ˌkʌ̯ˈɾ.ˈnɐː˩˥l]) is a city located in the Indian state of Haryana and serves as the administrative headquarters of the Karnal district. The city lies on National Highway 44, which connects it to the national capital, New Delhi, and the state capital, Chandigarh, placing Karnal almost midway between the two.

name: Firoz Shah Palace Complex
tagline: Tughlaq sandstone arches and underground passages
overview: Hisar (), also known as Hissar, is the administrative headquarters of Hisar district in the state of Haryana in northwestern India. It is located 164 km (102 mi) to the west of the national capital New Delhi, and has been identified as a counter-magnet city for the National Capital Region to develop as an alternative center of growth to Delhi.

name: Rakhigarhi
tagline: Largest Indus Valley Civilization archaeological mound
overview: Rakhigarhi or Rakhi Garhi (Hindi: [ɾaːkʰiːɡəɽʰiː]) is a village and an archaeological site in the Hansi district of the northern Indian state of Haryana, situated about 150 km northwest of Delhi. It is located in the Ghaggar River plain, some 27 km from the seasonal Ghaggar river, and belonged to the Indus Valley Civilisation, being part of the…

name: Thanjavur
tagline: Chola bronze galleries, Saraswathi Mahal, and Maratha palace
overview: Thanjavur (Tamil: [t̪aɲdʑaːʋuːɾ]), also known as Thanjai, previously known as Tanjore, is a city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is the 12th biggest city in Tamil Nadu.

name: Madurai
tagline: Vaigai river city of jasmine markets and Thirumalai Nayakkar
overview: Madurai is a major city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is the cultural capital of Tamil Nadu and the administrative headquarters of Madurai district, which is governed by the Madurai Municipal Corporation established on 1 November 1866.

name: Srirangam
tagline: Kaveri river island temple town with 21 gopurams
overview: Srirangam is a neighbourhood in the city of Tiruchirappalli in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. Forming a river island, Srirangam is bounded by the Kaveri River to the south and its distributary, Kollidam to the north.

name: Vijayawada
tagline: Prakasam Barrage, Undavalli Caves, and Kanaka Durga hill
overview: Vijayawada ( Vijay-uh-waw-duh), also called as Bezawada, is the second largest city and a major commercial hub in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. The city forms an integral part of the Andhra Pradesh Capital Region and is situated on the banks of the Krishna River, flanked by the Eastern Ghats and the Indrakeeladri Hills.

name: Orvakal Rock Garden
tagline: Sculpted quartz and silica rock formations in Kurnool
overview: Kurnool is a city in the state of Andhra Pradesh, India. It formerly served as the capital of Andhra State (1953–1956).

name: Nagarjunakonda
tagline: Island museum preserving Ikshvaku Buddhist stupas
overview: Nalgonda is a city and municipal corporation in the Indian state of Telangana. It is the headquarters of the Nalgonda district, as well as the headquarters of the Nalgonda mandal in the Nalgonda revenue division.

name: Agumbe
tagline: Rainforest sunset point and king cobra research station
overview: Shimoga, officially Shivamogga (Kannada: [ʃiʋɐmoɡːɐ]), is a city, taluka and the district headquarters of Shimoga district in the Karnataka state of India. The city lies on the banks of the Tunga River.

name: Mangaluru
tagline: Tulu coast beaches, Kadri hills, and maritime spice heritage
overview: Mangaluru (Kannada: [mɐŋɡɐɭuːru]), formerly called Mangalore ( MANG-gə-lor, -⁠LOR), is a major industrial port city in the Indian state of Karnataka and on the west coast of India. It is located between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats about 352 km (219 mi) west of Bengaluru, the state capital, 14 km (8+1⁄2 mi) north of the Karnataka–Kerala border…

name: Karwar
tagline: Kali river estuary, Rabindranath Tagore beach, and Kurumgad
overview: Karwar is a coastal city, taluka and the administrative headquarters of Uttara Kannada district, formerly part of the Bombay Presidency, located at the mouth of the Kali river along the Konkan Coast in the present-day state of Karnataka, India.

name: Kabini
tagline: Lush reservoir shores famous for black panther sightings
overview: The Kabini River is one of the major tributaries of the river Cauvery in southern India, It originates in Wayanad district of Kerala state by the confluence of the Panamaram River and the Mananthavady River. It flows eastward through Wayanad district, entering Mysore district of Karnataka, to join the Kaveri River in Mysore district of Karnataka.

name: Ganpatipule
tagline: Swayambhu beachside temple on Maharashtra’s Ratnagiri coast
overview: Ganpatipule (Marathi: गणपतीपुळे) is a coastal town in Ratnagiri district of Maharashtra. Due to its Ganpati mandir, the town is a popular Hindu pilgrimage and tourist destination.

name: Pratapgad
tagline: Mist-wreathed Sahyadri fortress above Mahabaleshwar
overview: Pratapgad is a mountain fort located in Satara district, in the Western Indian state of Maharashtra. The fort is situated 24 kilometres from the Mahabaleshwar hill station.

name: Sikandra
tagline: Red sandstone and marble garden mausoleum of Emperor Akbar
overview: Agra (; Hindi: Āgarā, pronounced [ˈaːɡɾaː] ) is a city on the banks of the Yamuna river in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh. It is a part of Western Uttar Pradesh, about 230 kilometres (140 mi) south-east of the national capital Delhi and 330 km west of the state capital Lucknow.

name: Kannauj
tagline: Ancient Ganga city of traditional copper-still attar perfumes
overview: Kannauj (Hindustani pronunciation: [kənːɔːd͡ʒ]) is an ancient city in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh and a municipal board (nagar palika) home to the administrative headquarters of the eponymous district. Known as Kanyakubja during the ancient Vedic period, it was successively the capital city of the Mahajanapada Panchala Kingdom and then of the…

name: Hastinapur
tagline: Historic Ganga plains pilgrimage and wetland sanctuary
overview: Hastinapur (Hastināpur) is a city in the Meerut district in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh. It is described as the capital of the Kuru kingdom in Hindu texts such as the Mahabharata and the Puranas; Hastinapur is located on the right bank of the Ganga river.

name: Bithoor
tagline: Quiet Ganga ghats and Valmiki Ashram near Kanpur
overview: Bithoor or Bithur is a town in Kanpur district, 25 km (15mi) by road north of the centre of Kanpur city, in Uttar Pradesh, India. Bithoor is situated on the right bank of the River Ganges, and is a centre of Hindu pilgrimage.

name: Gagron Fort
tagline: UNESCO water-and-hill fortress encircled by Ahu and Kali Sindh
overview: Jhalawar ([dʒʱaːlaːʋaːɽ] ) is a city, municipal council and headquarter in Jhalawar district of the Indian state of Rajasthan. It is located in the southeastern part of the state.

name: Deeg Palace
tagline: Jat summer water palaces and monsoon fountains
overview: Deeg is a historical city in the Deeg district of the Indian state of eastern Rajasthan. It is renowned for its architectural heritage, including palaces, forts, gardens, and fountains.

name: Menal Waterfall
tagline: Vindhyan gorge cascade and medieval Mahanal temple
overview: Bhilwara ( ) is a city Municipal Corporation and administrative headquarters in Bhilwara district of the Mewar region of Rajasthan, India. It has been termed as 'Textile city'.

name: Gaya
tagline: Vishnupad ghats on the Falgu and Barabar hill trails
overview: Gaya (IAST: Gayā) is a city, municipal corporation and the administrative headquarters of Gaya district and Magadh division of the Indian state of Bihar. Gaya is 116 kilometres (72 mi) south of Patna and is the state's second-largest city, with a population of 470,839.

name: Dungeshwari Cave
tagline: Mahakala hillside caves overlooking the Mohane valley
overview: Bodh Gayā is a religious site and place of pilgrimage associated with the Mahabodhi Temple complex, situated in the Gaya district in the Indian state of Bihar. It is famous for being the place where Gautama Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment (Pali: bodhi) under what became known as the Bodhi Tree.

name: Munger Fort
tagline: Ancient Ganga bend fortress and Bihar School of Yoga
overview: Munger, formerly spelt as Monghyr, is a twin city and a Municipal Corporation situated in the Indian state of Bihar. It is the administrative headquarters of Munger district and Munger Division.

name: Hazaribagh
tagline: Canary Hill, sal woodlands, and Konar Dam
overview: Hazaribagh (Hindustani pronunciation: [ɦəzɐ̞ɾɨ.baːɣ]) is a city and a municipal corporation in Hazaribagh district, Jharkhand, India. It is the administrative headquarters of Hazaribagh district and divisional headquarters of North Chotanagpur division.

name: Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary
tagline: Elephant hills overlooking the Subarnarekha valley
overview: Jamshedpur (Hindi: [d͡ʒəmˈʃeːd̪pʊɾ] ; Bengali: [ˈd͡ʒamʃedpuɾ]), also known as Tatanagar, is a major industrial city in eastern India. Located on the confluence of the Swarnarekha and Kharkai rivers, the city is surrounded by the Dalma Hills.

name: Maithon Dam
tagline: Barakar river island reservoir on the Jharkhand-Bengal border
overview: DhanbadHindi pronunciation: [dʱənˌbɐːd̪] is the second-most populated city in the Indian state of Jharkhand after Jamshedpur and a major financial hub of Jharkhand. In terms of economy, Dhanbad has the largest economy in the state of and is often referred to as the 'economic capital of Jharkhand'.

name: Asirgarh Fort
tagline: Satpura pass citadel guarding the Deccan trade route
overview: Burhanpur is a historical city in the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh. It is the administrative seat of Burhanpur District.

name: Datia Palace
tagline: Seven-storey Bundela stone palace of Bir Singh Deo
overview: Datia is a city and the headquarters of the Datia District of Gwalior Chambal region in north Madhya Pradesh, Central India. Datia is famous for Pitambara Peeth, decidated to Maa Baglamukhi, a shakti pilgrimage site.

name: Dongargarh
tagline: Hilltop Bambleshwari shrine reached by stone steps
overview: Durg is a city in the Indian state of Chhattisgarh, east of the Shivnath River and is part of the Durg-Bhilai urban agglomeration. With an urban population of 1,064,077, Durg-Bhilai is the second most populous urban area in Chhattisgarh after Raipur.

name: Jagdalpur
tagline: Bastar cultural hub of Danteshwari and tribal markets
overview: Jagdalpur is a city located in the southern part of Chhattisgarh state in India. It is the administrative headquarters of the Bastar district and Bastar division.

name: Mukutmanipur
tagline: Kangsabati and Kumari river dam surrounded by hills
overview: Bishnupur (; Bengali: [biʃnupur]; alternatively spelled as Vishnupur) is a city and a municipality in Bankura district, West Bengal, India. It has terracotta temples built by the Malla rulers, historic Radha Krishna temples built during 1600–1800 CE and the Baluchari sarees.

name: Mirik
tagline: Sumendu Lake surrounded by cryptomeria pines and tea
overview: Mirik is a small town and a Notified Area of Darjeeling district ruled by Shri L.B.Rai since 30years in the state of West Bengal, India. It is the headquarters of the Mirik subdivision.

name: Lava
tagline: Neora Valley cloud forest hamlet near Kalimpong
overview: Lava (also known as Lava Bazar) is a town in the Kalimpong II CD block in the Kalimpong subdivision of the Kalimpong district in the Indian state of West Bengal. As it lies in the high altitude, it is also visible from high altitude towns and villages of East Sikkim, high areas of Bhutan and also from Pakyong Airport.

name: Kiltan Island
tagline: Traditional coir-weaving coral island in Amindivi group
overview: Kiltan or Kilthān Island is a coral island in the Amindivi subgroup of the Indian Union Territory of Lakshadweep. It is at a distance of 291 km away from Kannur, 303 km away from Kozhikode, and 394 km (245 mi) west of the city of Kochi.

name: Little Andaman
tagline: Hut Bay surf breaks and White Surf waterfall
overview: Little Andaman Island (Onge: Gaubolambe) is the fourth largest of the Andaman Islands of India with an area of 707 km2, lying at the southern end of the archipelago. It belongs to the South Andaman administrative district, part of the Indian union territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

name: Ranakpur Forest
tagline: Aravalli leopard and sloth bear reserve
overview: Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Rajsamand district of Rajasthan State in western India. It surrounds the Kumbhalgarh Fortress and covers an area of 610.528 km2 (236 sq mi).

name: Guru Shikhar
tagline: Highest peak in the Aravalli Range above Mount Abu
overview: Mount Abu Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Aravalli Range, one of the oldest mountain ranges in India. It was declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1980.

name: Hawa Mahal
tagline: Honeycomb sandstone facade in Jaipur’s old bazaar
overview: The Hawa Mahal is a palace in the city of Jaipur, Rajasthan, India. Built from red and pink sandstone, it is on the edge of the City Palace, Jaipur, and extends to the Zenana, or women's chambers.

name: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
tagline: UNESCO astronomical stone instruments of Sawai Jai Singh
overview: The Jantar Mantar is a collection of 19 astronomical instruments built by the Rajput king Sawai Jai Singh, the founder of Jaipur, Rajasthan, India. The monument was completed in 1734.

name: Sankissa
tagline: Ancient Buddhist archaeological mound in Farrukhabad
overview: Sankissa ( Pali: Saṅkassa, Sanskrit: Sāṅkāśya ) is an ancient city in India renown for the descent of Gautama Buddha from the Tushita heavens where he taught his mother before landing at Sankissa. Considered among the eight great pilgrimage sites, it was thirty leagues from Sravasti.

name: Shravasti
tagline: Jetavana monastic ruins along the Rapti river
overview: Shravasti (Sanskrit: श्रावस्ती, IAST: Śrāvastī; Pali: 𑀲𑀸𑀯𑀢𑁆𑀣𑀻, romanized: Sāvatthī) is a town in Shravasti district in Indian state of Uttar Pradesh. It was the capital of the ancient Indian kingdom of Kosala, where the Buddha lived most after his enlightenment.

photoCredit.author: Varun Shiv Kapur from New Delhi, India

name: Rumi Darwaza
tagline: Sixty-foot Awadhi gateway in old Lucknow
overview: The Rumi Darwaza (sometimes known as the Turkish Gate), in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India, is a gateway which was built by Nawab Asaf-Ud-Daula in 1784. It is an example of Awadhi architecture.

name: Laxmi Vilas Palace
tagline: Indo-Saracenic royal residence in sprawling parkland
overview: Lakshmi Vilas Palace (Gujarati: લક્ષ્મી વિલાસ મહેલ) is a historic palace and royal residence located in Vadodara, Gujarat, India. The palace was commissioned in 1878 by Sayajirao Gaekwad III, the ruler of Baroda State, and constructed in 1890 by British architects Charles Mant and Robert Chisholm.

name: Sidi Saiyyed Mosque
tagline: 16th-century Ahmedabad mosque famed for stone jali lattice
overview: The Sidi Saiyyed Mosque, popularly known locally as Sidi Saiyyed ni Jali, is a Sunni mosque located in Ahmedabad, in the state of Gujarat, India. The mosque was built by Sidi Sayyad, a Habshi nobleman, in 980 AH (1572/1573 CE).

name: Pirotan Island
tagline: Marine National Park coral island in the Gulf of Kutch
overview: The Sun Temple of Modhera is a Hindu temple dedicated to the solar deity Surya, located in the village of Modhera in Mehsana district, Gujarat, India. The temple is situated on the bank of the river Pushpavati, and was constructed in the 11th century during the reign of Bhima I and Karna I of the Chaulukya dynasty.

name: Dandi
tagline: Arabian Sea village of the 1930 Salt March
overview: Dandi is a village in the Jalalpore taluka, Navsari District, Gujarat, India. It is located on the coast of the Arabian Sea near the city of Navsari.

name: Kankaria Lake
tagline: Polygonal 15th-century lakefront promenade in Ahmedabad
overview: Kankaria Lake is the largest lake in Ahmedabad in the Indian state of Gujarat. It is located in the southeastern part of the Ahmedabad, in the Maninagar area.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus
tagline: UNESCO Victorian-Gothic railway landmark in Mumbai
overview: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST), officially Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) and formerly known as Victoria Terminus (VT), is a historic railway terminus and UNESCO World Heritage Site in Mumbai (Bombay), Maharashtra, India. The terminus was designed by a British architectural engineer Frederick William Stevens from an initial design by…

name: Kanheri Caves
tagline: 109 basalt rock-cut Buddhist caves inside Mumbai forest
overview: Sanjay Gandhi National Park is a 103.84 km2 (40.09 sq mi) national park in Mumbai, Maharashtra, with its headquarters situated in Borivali. The national park attracts more than 2 million visitors every year.

name: Bhimashankar
tagline: Sahyadri rainforest Jyotirlinga and giant squirrel habitat
overview: Bhimashankar Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva situated in its eponymous village, Bhimashankar, in Pune district of Maharashtra. It is a key pilgrimage centre and contains one of the 12 Jyotirlingas.

name: Trimbakeshwar
tagline: Brahmagiri hill shrine at the source of the Godavari
overview: Trimbakeshwar Shiva Temple (श्री त्र्यंबकेश्वर ज्योतिर्लिंग मंदिर) is an ancient Hindu temple in the town of Trimbak, in the Trimbakeshwar tehsil, in the Nashik District of Maharashtra, India, 28 km from the city of Nashik and 40 km from Nashik road. It is dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva and is one of the twelve jyotirlingas where the Hindu genealogy…

name: Daulatabad Fort
tagline: Conical rock-cut Devagiri fortress near Ellora
overview: Daulatabad Fort, originally Devagiri Fort, is a historic fortified citadel located in Daulatabad village near Aurangabad, Maharashtra, India. It was the capital of the Yadavas (9th century – 14th century CE), for a brief time the capital of the Delhi Sultanate (1327–1334), and later a secondary capital of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate (1499–1636).

name: Bibi Ka Maqbara
tagline: 17th-century Deccan marble-and-stucco garden tomb
overview: The Bibi Ka Makbara (lit. 'Tomb of the Lady') is a tomb located in the city of Aurangabad in the Indian state of Maharashtra.

name: Harishchandragad
tagline: Konkan Kada amphitheatre cliff in Ahmednagar
overview: Harishchandragad is a hill fort in Ahilyanagar district, Maharashtra, India. Situated in the Western Ghats, it contains rock-cut caves, temples and water cisterns.

name: Kalsubai
tagline: Highest peak in Maharashtra overlooking Bhandardara
overview: Kalsubai is a mountain in the Western Ghats, located in the Indian state of Maharashtra. Kalsubai is the highest peak in Maharashtra and is located in Ahilyanagar district in Akole Taluka.

name: Vengurla
tagline: Quiet Sindhudurg beach town with historic lighthouse
overview: Vengurla is a town in Sindhudurg district of Maharashtra, India just north of Goa. It is surrounded by a semicircular range of hills with lush green foliage mainly of cashew, mango, coconut, and different kinds of berry trees.

name: Dapoli
tagline: Konkan coast of Murud beach, sea forts, and hot springs
overview: Dapoli is a town and taluka in the Ratnagiri district of Maharashtra, India. It lies 215 km (134 mi) south of the state capital of Mumbai.

name: Colva Beach
tagline: Long white-sand stretch along Salcete’s coast
overview: Colva (Portuguese: Colvá) is a coastal village situated in the Salcete taluka, in South Goa district, of Goa state on the west coast of the Indian subcontinent. Colva Beach (Portuguese: Praia de Colvá) spans about 2.5 km (1.6 mi) along a sandy coastline of approximately 25 km (16 mi) extending from Bogmalo in the north to Cabo de Rama in the south.

name: Chamundi Hills
tagline: Hilltop Chamundeshwari shrine overlooking Mysuru
overview: Mysore Palace, also known as Amba Vilas Palace, is a historic palace and royal residence located in Mysore, Karnataka, India. It served as the official residence of the Wadiyar dynasty and the seat of the Kingdom of Mysore, and was commissioned by Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV in August 1897 following the destruction of the previous structure in a fire.

name: Gol Gumbaz
tagline: Whispering gallery beneath India’s largest masonry dome
overview: The Gol Gumbaz (; lit. 'Round Dome'), also written as Gol Gumbad, is a dark gray basalt mausoleum located in the city of Bijapur in northern Karnataka, India.

name: Abbey Falls
tagline: Coffee-estate cascade near Madikeri in Kodagu
overview: Abbey Falls (also spelled Abbi Falls and Abbe Falls) is a waterfall in Kodagu, in the Western Ghats of Karnataka, India. It is located 8 km from the Madikeri, 122 km from Mysore, 144 km from Mangalore and 268 km from Bangalore.

name: Dubare Elephant Camp
tagline: Kaveri river forest camp on the edge of Coorg
overview: Dubare is a forest camp on the banks of the river Kaveri in the district of Kodagu, Karnataka.

name: Bannerghatta National Park
tagline: Granite scrub forest and butterfly park south of Bengaluru
overview: Bannerghatta National Park is a national park in India, located In Bengaluru and Bengaluru South District, Karnataka. It was founded in 1970 and declared as a national park in 1974.

name: Kemmanagundi
tagline: Baba Budangiri ridge station of rose gardens and Hebbe Falls
overview: Kemmannugundi (Red Soil Pit) is a hill station in Tarikere taluk of Chikkamagaluru district in the state of Karnataka, India. It is at the elevation of 1434m above sea level, with its peak at 1863m.

name: Valiyaparamba Backwaters
tagline: Quiet island-studded lagoon in Kasaragod
overview: Bekal (Malayalam: [beːkːɐl]) is a small town in the Kasaragod district on the West coast of the state of Kerala, India.

name: Chembra Peak
tagline: Heart-shaped highland lake trek in Wayanad
overview: Chembra Peak (Chembra Mala) is a mountain in the state of Kerala, India, with an elevation of 2,100 m (6,890 ft) above sea level. The highest peak in the Wayanad hills and one of the highest peaks in the Western Ghats, adjoining the Nilgiri Hills and Vellarimala, it is located in the Wayanad district and Malappuram district in Kerala, near Kalpetta town…

name: Eravikulam National Park
tagline: Nilgiri tahr shola grasslands around Anamudi peak
overview: Eravikulam National Park is a 97 km2 national park located along the Western Ghats in the Idukki and Ernakulam districts of Kerala in India. The park is situated between 10º05'N and 10º20' north, and 77º0' and 77º10' east and is the first national park in Kerala.

name: Idukki Arch Dam
tagline: Curved concrete arch dam wedged between Kuravan and Kurathi
overview: The Idukki Dam is a double-curvature thin arch dam constructed across the Periyar River in a narrow gorge between two granite hills locally known as Kuravan and Kurathi, in the Idukki district, in the state of Kerala, India. It is constructed and owned by the Kerala State Electricity Board.

name: Kuttanad
tagline: Below-sea-level paddy dykes and backwater canals
overview: Kuttanad (Malayalam: [kuʈːɐnaːɖə̆]) is a river delta landscape region in the state of Kerala, India, known for its vast paddy fields and geographical peculiarities. It is in the districts of Alappuzha, Kottayam and Pathanamthitta.

name: Padmanabhapuram Palace
tagline: Carved rosewood Travancore timber palace complex
overview: Padmanabhapuram Palace, also known as Kalkulam Palace, is a Travancore-era palace located in Padmanabhapuram in the Kanyakumari district of the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. The palace is owned, controlled and maintained by the Kerala Government.

name: Thiruvalluvar Statue
tagline: Granite island monuments at India’s southern tip
overview: Vivekananda Rock Memorial is a monument and popular tourist attraction in Kanyakumari, India's southernmost tip. The memorial stands on one of the two rocks located about 500 meters off mainland of Vavathurai, Tamil Nadu.

name: Gingee Fort
tagline: Three-hill Maratha and Vijayanagara citadel
overview: Gingee Fort or Senji Fort (also known as Chenji, Chanchi, Jinji or Senchi) in Tamil Nadu, India is one of the surviving forts in Tamil Nadu, India. It is popularly known as Great Wall of South India.

name: Pamban Bridge
tagline: Iconic sea railway span connecting mainland to Rameswaram
overview: Ramanathaswamy Temple (Rāmanātasvāmi Kōyil) is a Hindu temple dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva located on Rameswaram island in the state of Tamil Nadu, India. It is one of the twelve Jyotirlinga temples.

name: Simhachalam Temple
tagline: 11th-century hill shrine overlooking Visakhapatnam
overview: Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha temple, Simhachalam, is a Hindu temple situated on the Simhachalam Hill Range, which is 300 metres above the sea level in the city of Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, India. It is dedicated to Lord Vishnu, who is worshipped there as Varaha Narasimha.

name: Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary
tagline: Godavari delta mangrove boardwalks and fishing cats
overview: Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary is an estuary situated near Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh, India. It is the third largest stretch of mangrove forests in India with 24 mangrove tree species and more than 120 bird species.

name: Mahanandi
tagline: Perennial crystal springs beside Nallamala forest
overview: Mahanandi is a village located east of the Nallamala Hills of Nandyal District, Andhra Pradesh, India. It is surrounded by forests.

name: Ahobilam
tagline: Nine-shrine Nallamala canyon pilgrimage trail
overview: Ahobilam is a town and holy site in the Allagadda mandal of Nandyal district in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It is surrounded by the Eastern Ghats with several mountain hills and gorges.

name: Ubbalamadugu Falls
tagline: Forest stream trek in Kambakam hills near Sullurpeta
overview: Ubbalamudugu Falls (also called Tada Falls) is a waterfall located near Oneness Temple and Sricity in the Tirupati district of India. It is a clear waterfall falling from a height of 100 meters.

name: Basar
tagline: Gnana Saraswati temple along the Godavari
overview: Basara is a census town in Nirmal district in the state of Telangana, India. It is located about 208 kilometres (129 mi) north of the state capital Hyderabad, 34 kilometres (21 mi) from Nizamabad and 73 kilometres (45 mi) from the district headquarters Nirmal.

name: Khandadhar Falls, Sundagarh
tagline: Horsetail waterfall plunging into Sundargarh forest
overview: Rourkela (Odia: [ɾauɾɔkela] ) officially Raurkela is a planned city located in the northern district Sundargarh of Odisha, India. It is a Tier-2 city and the third-largest city in Odisha after Bhubaneswar and Cuttack.

name: Nandankanan
tagline: Forest sanctuary and Kanjia Lake north of Bhubaneswar
overview: Nandankanan Zoological Park is a 437-hectare (1,080-acre) zoo and botanical garden located in Barang village, Odisha, India. It is 10 km to south of Cuttack and 10 km north of Bhubaneswar.

name: Howrah Bridge
tagline: Cantilever steel icon spanning the Hooghly River
overview: The Howrah Bridge (Bengali: [ɦaoɽa]) is a balanced steel bridge over the Hooghly River in West Bengal, India. Commissioned in 1943, the bridge was originally named the New Howrah Bridge, because it replaced a pontoon bridge at the same location linking both sides of Kolkata.

name: Dakshineswar
tagline: Navaratna riverside temple north of Kolkata
overview: Dakshineswar Kali Temple is a Hindu navaratna style temple in Dakshineswar, Kolkata, West Bengal, India, on the eastern bank of the Hooghly River. The presiding deity of the temple is Bhavatarini (Kali), a form of Mahadevi or Parashakti Adya Kali, otherwise known as Adishakti Kalika.

name: Buxa Fort
tagline: Duars forest trek to historic Bhutan-border fort
overview: Buxa Tiger Reserve is a tiger reserve and national park in northern West Bengal, India, covering an area of 760 km2 (290 sq mi). It ranges in elevation from 60 m (200 ft) in the Gangetic Plains to 1,750 m (5,740 ft) bordering the Himalayas in the north.

name: Tiger Hill
tagline: Sunrise ridge facing Kanchenjunga and Mount Everest
overview: Tiger Hill (2,590 metres (8,500 ft)) is a mountain located in Darjeeling, in the Indian State of West Bengal. It has a panoramic view of Mount Everest and Mount Kanchenjunga together.

name: Neora Valley National Park
tagline: Red panda cloud forest in Kalimpong hills
overview: Neora Valley National Park is a national park in Kalimpong district, West Bengal, India that was established in 1986. Spread over an area of 88 km2 (34 sq mi), it is a rich biological zone in eastern India.

name: Janakpur Road (Sitamarhi)
tagline: Punaura Dham tank and Mithila heritage
overview: Sitamarhi (IAST: Sītāmaṛhī) is the headquarters of the Sitamarhi district in Tirhut Division, Bihar. The city was named in honour of Sītā, wife of Rāma, she appeared in Sitamarhi according to Hindu legends.

name: McCluskieganj
tagline: Anglo-Indian woodland bungalow settlement near Ranchi
overview: McCluskieganj is a small hilly town in Jharkhand State, India, about 40 miles (64 km) northwest of the capital, Ranchi. The town used to have a significant Anglo-Indian community.

name: Malhar
tagline: Ancient Kalachuri and Somavanshi stone ruins near Bilaspur
overview: Malhar is a small town situated in Bilaspur district of Chhattisgarh, India. A historically important site that once was a major city and served as a capital in the 1st millennium, it has been referred to as Mallar, Mallari and Sarabhapur in inscriptions and Indian literature.

name: Ratanpur
tagline: Mahamaya temple tanks and medieval hill fort
overview: Ratanpur is a town and a nagar palika in Bilaspur district in the Indian state of Chhattisgarh. It is located about 25 kilometres (16 mi) from Bilaspur on National Highway 130 towards Ambikapur.

name: Morni Fort
tagline: Shivalik ridge fort overlooking Morni villages
overview: Panchkula (ISO: Pañckulā) is a city and district headquarter in the Panchkula district in Haryana, India. It is a satellite city of the state capital Chandigarh.

name: Virasat-e-Khalsa
tagline: Sandstone and steel Sikh heritage museum in Anandpur Sahib
overview: Rupnagar (; formerly known as Ropar or Rupar) is a city and a municipal council in Rupnagar district in the Indian state of Punjab. Rupnagar is a newly created fifth Divisional Headquarters of Punjab comprising Rupnagar, Mohali, and its adjoining districts.

name: Pushpa Gujral Science City
tagline: Interactive science campus between Jalandhar and Kapurthala
overview: Jalandhar (Punjabi pronunciation: [d͡ʐəˈlənˌdə̀ɾᵊ]) is a city in the state of Punjab in India. With a considerable population, it ranks as the third most-populous city in the state and is the largest city in the Doaba region.

name: Purana Qila
tagline: 16th-century citadel along the Yamuna on Indraprastha mound
overview: Purana Qila (lit. 'Old Fort') is one of the oldest forts in Delhi, India.

name: Sunder Nursery
tagline: Restored 90-acre Mughal heritage park beside Humayun’s Tomb
overview: The Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah is the dargah and mosque complex of the Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya, located in the Nizamuddin West area of Delhi, India. The dargah, or mausoleum, is a Sufi shrine and is visited by thousands of pilgrims every week.

name: Bedni Bugyal
tagline: High alpine meadow facing Trisul and Nanda Ghunti
overview: Roopkund, locally known as Mystery Lake or Skeleton Lake, is a high-altitude glacial lake in Himalayas at an altitude of 5,020 m (16,470 ft), between Trishul peak (7,120 m) and Nanda Ghunti peak (6,310 m), in the Chamoli District of Uttarakhand state of India. Surrounded by rock-strewn glaciers and snow-clad mountains, Roopkund is a popular trekking…

name: Chaukori
tagline: Tea-estate ridge facing Nanda Devi and Panchachuli
overview: Chaukori is a hill station in the Pithoragarh district set among the lofty peaks of the western Himalayan Range in the Kumaon Division of Uttarakhand, India. To its north is Tibet and to its south is Terai.

name: Atal Tunnel & Sissu
tagline: Waterfall-laced Chandra valley village north of Pir Panjal
overview: Rohtang Pass (Rohtang, literally meaning "pile of corpses") is a high mountain pass (elevation 3,980 m (13,058 ft)) on the eastern end of the Pir Panjal Range of the Himalayas around 51 km (32 mi) from Manali in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh, It connects the Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti Valleys of Himachal Pradesh, India.

name: Chandra Taal
tagline: Crescent turquoise glacial lake at 4,250 m in Lahaul
overview: Chandra Taal (lit. 'moon lake') is a lake in the upper Chandra valley of the Lahul and Spiti district of Himachal Pradesh, India.

name: Malana
tagline: Secluded Parvati valley village beneath Chandrakhani Pass
overview: Malana is an Indian village in the state of Himachal Pradesh. The only village in the Malana Nala, a side valley of the Parvati Valley northeast of the Kullu Valley, it is shadowed by the peaks of Chanderkhani and Deo Tibba.

name: Renuka Lake
tagline: Natural lion-shaped forest lake in Sirmaur
overview: Renuka lake is in the Sirmaur district of Himachal Pradesh in India and it is 672 m above sea level. It is the largest lake in Himachal Pradesh, with a circumference of about 3,214 m.

name: Shalimar Bagh, Srinagar
tagline: Terraced Mughal chinar garden built by Jahangir
overview: Shalimar Bagh (Urdu pronunciation: [ʃɑːliːmɑːr bɑːɣ] ; Kashmiri pronunciation: [ʃaːlɨməːr baːɣ]) is a Mughal garden in Srinagar, Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, located at the northeast of Dal Lake. It is also known as Shalimar Garden, Farah Baksh, and Faiz Baksh.

name: Sangam (Indus-Zanskar)
tagline: Emerald-and-cobalt confluence of Indus and Zanskar rivers
overview: Magnetic Hill is a gravity hill located, between Khalatse and Leh in Sham district of Ladakh, India. The layout of the area and surrounding slopes create the optical illusion of a hill.

name: Nohkalikai Falls
tagline: India’s tallest plunge waterfall tumbling off Sohra plateau
overview: Cherrapunji ( ), also known as Sohra, is a sub-divisional town (Proposed District) in the East Khasi Hills district in the Indian state of Meghalaya. It was the traditional capital of ka hima Sohra (Khasi tribal kingdom).

name: Hajo
tagline: Ancient pilgrimage hills of Poa Mecca and Hayagriva Madhava
overview: Hajo is a historic town set in the hills northwest of Guwahati, Assam, India. It is a meeting point of Buddhists, Hindus and Muslims due to the various pilgrimage sites on the different hills of Hajo.

name: Umrangso
tagline: Dima Hasao lakeside hills and Panimoor waterfalls
overview: Diphu (Assamese pronunciation: [ˈdifu: / di.ɸu]) is a town in the Karbi Anglong district of the state of Assam, India. It is the meeting place of the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council and the headquarters of Karbi Anglong district.

name: Mayudia Pass
tagline: Snowy Lower Dibang ridge pass above Roing
overview: Roing is the district headquarter of Lower Dibang Valley district in the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh. It is the last major township at the north-eastern frontier of India.

name: Mount Tiyi
tagline: Lotha Naga mountain ridge and Doyang reservoir
overview: Wokha is a town and municipality in the Indian state of Nagaland. It is the headquarters of Wokha District and is located about 75 km north of the state capital, Kohima.

name: Ghoshu Bird Sanctuary
tagline: Sema highland forests and Sumi cultural villages
overview: Zünheboto (), also known as Zünhebo, is a town in Zünheboto district in the Indian state of Nagaland. Zünheboto is inhabited by the Sümi Nagas.

name: Palak Dil
tagline: Natural highland lake in southern Saiha district
overview: Kolasib is a town located in the northern part of Mizoram, India. It serves as the headquarters of the Kolasib District.

name: Rumtek Monastery
tagline: Seats of the Karmapa overlooking Gangtok valley
overview: Rumtek Monastery (Tibetan: རུམ་ཐེག་དགོན་པ་, Wylie: rum theg dgon pa), also called the Dharma Chakra Centre, is a gompa located in the Indian state of Sikkim near the capital Gangtok. It is the seat in exile of the Gyalwang Karmapa, inaugurated in 1966 by the 16th Karmapa.

name: Barren Island
tagline: India’s only active volcanic island in the Andaman Sea
overview: Barren Island is an uninhabited island in the Andaman Sea. It is the only confirmed active volcano in the Indian subcontinent, and the only active volcano along a chain of volcanoes from Sumatra to Myanmar.

name: Undavalli Caves
tagline: Four-storey monolithic sandstone rock-cut caves near Vijayawada
overview: The Undavalli Caves are monolithic Indian rock-cut architecture, located in Guntur district in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. The caves are located south west of Vijayawada.

name: Belum Caves
tagline: India’s second-longest accessible karst limestone cavern
overview: Belum Caves are a limestone cave system located in Nandyal district of Andhra Pradesh, India. Extending over 3.23 km (2.01 mi), it is the second-largest cave network in the country.

name: Kanipakam
tagline: Historic Swayambhu Vinayaka temple in Chittoor district
overview: Kanipakam is a minor town in Irala mandal, located in Chittoor district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. Kanipakam is situated at a distance of 11 km from Chittoor town on the Chittoor-Irala road.

name: Yaganti
tagline: Cave-studded Nallamala shrine of Uma Maheswara and Pushkarini
overview: Yaganti Temple or Sri Yaganti Uma Maheswara Temple is a temple of Shiva in Nandyal district in the India state of Andhra Pradesh. It was built according to Vaishnavaite traditions.

name: Mantralayam
tagline: Tungabhadra riverside Raghavendra Swamy matha town
overview: Mantralayam is a pilgrim village and Mandal in the Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh, on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.

name: Puttaparthi
tagline: Prasanthi Nilayam and Chitravathi river valley town
overview: Puttaparthi (IAST: Puṭṭaparthy) is a municipality and district headquarters of Sri Sathya Sai district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It is located in Puttaparthi mandal of Puttaparthi revenue division.

name: Penukonda Fort
tagline: Second capital fortress of the Vijayanagara Empire
overview: Penukonda also called Penugonda is a town in the Sri Sathya Sai district of Andhra Pradesh, India. It is 70 km away from Anantapur town.

name: Pulicat Lake
tagline: Brackish coastal lagoon famed for flamingos and Nellapattu birds
overview: Pulicat Lake is the second-largest brackish-water lagoon in India (after Chilika Lake), measuring 759 square kilometres (293 sq mi). A major part of the lagoon lies in the Tirupati district of Andhra Pradesh and rest with Thiruvallur district of Tamil Nadu.

name: Bheemunipatnam
tagline: 17th-century Dutch cemetery, red cliffs, and Gosthani estuary
overview: Bheemunipatnam (also known as Bheemili) is a suburb of Visakhapatnam, India. The town was named after Bhima, a character in the Hindu epic Mahabharata.

name: Srikurmam
tagline: Unique Kurma avatar temple with 108 carved stone pillars
overview: Sri Kurmam also known as Srikurmu or Srikurma is a village near Srikakulam, Andhra Pradesh, India, 14.5 km southeast of Srikakulam town in the Gara mandal of Srikakulam district. It was named after the Srikurmam temple dedicated to Kurma avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu, which was re-established by Eastern Ganga Dynasty king Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva.

name: Draksharamam
tagline: Pancharama Kshetra Bhimeswara sandstone temple in Konaseema
overview: Draksharamam is a village in Konaseema district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. The Bhimeswara Swamy Temple in this town is one of the five temples of Shiva known as Pancharama Kshetras.

name: Konaseema
tagline: Lush Godavari delta of coconut canals and backwater villages
overview: Konaseema is a group of islands between the tributaries of the Godavari River and Bay of Bengal located in Dr. B.

name: Hope Island, Kakinada
tagline: Natural 16 km sandspit sheltering Kakinada Bay
overview: Hope Island (Krachchu Lanka) is a small tadpole shaped Island situated off the coast of Andhra Pradesh near Kakinada, India, in the Bay of Bengal.

name: Maredumilli
tagline: Eastern Ghats bamboo forests and Jalatarangini waterfalls
overview: Maredumilli is a village in Polavaram district in the state of Andhra Pradesh in India. It is the mandal headquarters of Maredumilli mandal.

name: Rajamahendravaram
tagline: Historic Godavari riverfront and Papikondalu boat hub
overview: Rajamahendravaram, previously known as Rajahmundry ( RAH-juh-mun-dree), is a Tier-2 city in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh and the district headquarters of the East Godavari district. It is the seventh most populated city in the state.

name: Kolleru Lake
tagline: Vast freshwater Ramsar wetland between Krishna and Godavari
overview: Kolleru Lake is one of the largest freshwater lakes in India and forms the largest shallow freshwater lake in Asia (with 245 km2 of lake area and 302 km2 of total Ramsar designated wetland). 15 kilometers away from Eluru and 65 km from Rajamahendravaram, the lake is located between the Krishna and Godavari river deltas.

name: Machilipatnam
tagline: Historic Coromandel port famed for Kalamkari textiles
overview: Machilipatnam (Telugu: [mɐt͡ʃiliːpɐʈnɐm] ), also known as Masulipatnam, Masulipatam, or Bandar (Telugu: [bɐn̪d̪ɐɾu]), is a city in Krishna district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, located 60 kilometres (37 mi) from Vijayawada. It is a municipal corporation and the administrative headquarters of Krishna district.

name: Mangalagiri
tagline: Hilltop Panakala Narasimha shrine and handloom cotton town
overview: Mangalagiri - Tadepalli is one of the two cities in Guntur district, Andhra Pradesh, India. It was established on 23 March 2021 by combining Managalagiri and Tadepalli towns and adjacent villages.

name: Kondaveedu Fort
tagline: 14th-century Reddy dynasty hill fort in Guntur
overview: Kondaveedu Fort is a historically significant ancient hill fortress located in Kondaveedu, a village in the Chilakaluripet constituency of Palnadu district, Andhra Pradesh, India. The site is located 16 miles west of the city of Guntur.

name: Tadipatri
tagline: Chintala Venkataramana and Bugga Ramalingeswara carved temples
overview: Tadipatri is a town in Anantapur district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh at the border of Nandyala district and Kadapa district. It is a Selection Grade Municipality City Council.

name: Ameen Peer Dargah (Kadapa)
tagline: Historic Rayalaseema town and Gandikota gateway
overview: Kadapa is a city in the southern part of Andhra Pradesh, India. It is located in the Rayalaseema region, and is the district headquarters of YSR Kadapa district.

name: Vontimitta
tagline: Grand Vijayanagara Kodandarama stone temple in Kadapa
overview: Vontimitta (Telugu: ఒంటిమిట్ట) or Ekasilanagaram, is a village in Kadapa district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It is located in Vontimitta mandal of the Kadapa revenue division.

name: Kambalakonda Sanctuary
tagline: Dry evergreen forest reserve bordering Visakhapatnam
overview: The Kambalakonda Wildlife Sanctuary is a forest situated near Visakhapatnam. It has been under the control of Andhra Pradesh Forest Department since 10 March 1970.

name: Paderu
tagline: Highland tribal valley of Matsyagundam and coffee hills
overview: Paderu is a village located in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It is the administrative headquarters of ASR district, and the Headquarters of Paderu revenue division and Paderu Mandal.

name: Antarvedi
tagline: Sacred Godavari sea-confluence beach and lighthouse
overview: Antarvedi is a village in the Sakhinetipalle mandal, located in the Dr. B.

name: Bhadrachalam
tagline: Historic Godavari riverfront Sri Rama temple town
overview: Bhadrachalam is a census town in Bhadradri Kothagudem district in the Indian state of Telangana. It is an important Hindu pilgrimage town with the Bhadrachalam Temple of Rama, situated on the banks of Godavari River.

name: Kondagattu
tagline: Forested granite hillock shrine of Anjaneya Swamy
overview: Kondagattu Anjaneya Swamy Temple is a temple dedicated to Lord Anjaneya Swamy. It is one of the famous temples, located in Muthyumpeta village of Mallial mandal, Jagitial district, Telangana, India.

name: Pakhal Lake
tagline: 13th-century forest-rimmed lake and wildlife sanctuary
overview: Pakhal Lake is a man-made lake in the Pakhal Wildlife Sanctuary in the Warangal district of Telangana, a state in Southern India.

name: Eturnagaram Sanctuary
tagline: Dense Godavari valley reserve of bison and spotted deer
overview: Eturnagaram Wildlife Sanctuary is a wildlife sanctuary located in Eturnagaram village in Mulugu district in Telangana, India. It is located 100 km (62 mi) from Warangal and 250 km (160 mi) from Hyderabad.

name: Thousand Pillar Temple
tagline: Star-shaped Kakatiya basalt shrine in Hanamkonda
overview: The Thousand Pillar Temple or Rudreswara Swamy Temple is a historical Hindu temple located in the city of Hanamakonda, Telangana, India. It is dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu and Surya.

name: Rachakonda Fort
tagline: 14th-century Padmanayaka boulder hill citadel
overview: Rachakonda Fort is a historic fort located in Rachakonda, Yadadri Bhongir district of Telangana, India. It was built by the Recherla Nayaka king Anapotanayaka in the 14th century AD.

name: Nagarjuna Sagar
tagline: Massive Krishna masonry dam and island museum backdrop
overview: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is a masonry dam across the Krishna River at Nagarjuna Sagar, which straddles the border between Nalgonda district in Telangana, and Palnadu district in Andhra Pradesh. The dam provides irrigation water to the districts of Nalgonda, Suryapet, Khammam, Bhadradri Kothagudem districts of Telangana and also Krishna, Guntur, Palnadu,,…

name: Medak Cathedral
tagline: Towering Gothic-revival white granite church with stained glass
overview: Medak Cathedral at Medak in Telangana, India, is one of the largest churches in India and has been the cathedral church of the Diocese of Medak of the Church of South India since 1947. Originally built by Charles Walker Posnett British Wesleyan Methodists, it was consecrated on 25 December 1924.

name: Mallela Theertham
tagline: Sacred forested waterfall inside Amrabad Tiger Reserve
overview: Mallela Theertham is a waterfall located in the Nallamala Forest in Nagarkurnool, Telangana, India. The River Krishna flows through this forest.

name: Salar Jung Museum
tagline: World-renowned Musi riverfront art and antiquities museum
overview: The Salar Jung Museum is an art museum located at Dar-ul-Shifa, on the southern bank of the Musi River in the city of Hyderabad, Telangana, India. It is one of the notable National Museums of India.

name: Chowmahalla Palace
tagline: Restored Asaf Jahi Nizams’ palace complex in old Hyderabad
overview: Chowmahalla Palace or Chowmahallat is the palace of the Nizams of Hyderabad State located in Hyderabad, Telangana, India. It was the seat of power of the Asaf Jahi dynasty (1720–1948) and was the official residence of the Nizams during their reign.

name: Qutb Shahi Tombs
tagline: Granite-domed Golconda royal necropolis in Ibrahim Bagh
overview: The Qutub Shahi tombs are a series of Islamic tombs and mosques built by the various kings of the Qutub Shahi dynasty, located in the Ibrahim Bagh (garden precinct), close to the famous Golconda Fort in Hyderabad, in the Hyderabad district of the state of Telangana, India. A stunning and concentrated example of Indo-Islamic and Qutb Shahi architecture,…

name: Birla Mandir, Hyderabad
tagline: White marble hilltop shrine overlooking Hussain Sagar
overview: Birla Mandir is a Hindu temple built on a 280 feet (85 m) high hillock called Naubath Pahad 13 acres (53,000 m2) plot in Hyderabad, Telangana, India. Naubat Pahad which was once also known as Band Rock so called because long ago all official communications from Mughals to the Nizams were proclaimed from this hill accompanied by music.

name: Chilkur Balaji
tagline: Osman Sagar lakeside shrine on Hyderabad’s outskirts
overview: Chilkur Balaji Temple is an ancient Hindu temple of Lord Balaji on the banks of Osman Sagar in Rangareddy District in Telangana. It is one of the oldest temples in the Hyderabad Dist earlier now in Rangareddy Dist, built during the time of Madanna and Akkanna, the uncles of Bhakta Ramadas.

name: Nirmal
tagline: Town of wooden craft toys and Shyamgarh hill fort
overview: Nirmal is a city and the district headquarters of Nirmal district in the Indian state of Telangana. It is famed for Nirmal paintings, Nirmal furniture and Nirmal toys and craft made out of wood.

name: Elgandal Fort
tagline: Manair river hill fortress framed by palm groves
overview: Elgandal Fort is situated amidst palm groves on the banks of the Manair River (a tributary of the Godavari River), approximately 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) from Karimnagar on the Sircilla Road in the Indian state of Telangana. It was once under the control of the Qutub Shahi dynasty, the Mughal Empire, and the Nizams of Hyderabad.

name: Chennai
tagline: Marina Beach, Mylapore temples, and Fort St George heritage
overview: Chennai, also known as Madras, is the capital and largest city of Tamil Nadu, the southernmost state of India. It is located on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal.

name: Marina Beach
tagline: Thirteen-kilometre urban promenade on the Bay of Bengal
overview: Marina Beach, or simply the Marina, is a natural urban beach in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India, along the Bay of Bengal. The beach runs from near Fort St.

name: Fort St. George
tagline: 1644 coastal citadel housing St Mary’s Church and museum
overview: Fort St. George (or historically, White Town) is a fortress at the coastal city of Chennai, India.

name: Mylapore (Kapaleeshwarar)
tagline: Dravidian gopuram and stepped temple tank in Chennai
overview: The Kapaleeshwarar Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to the god Shiva. It is located in Mylapore, Chennai in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu.

name: Pazhaverkadu (Pulicat)
tagline: Dutch colonial lagoon town on Tamil Nadu’s northern coast
overview: Pulicat or Pazhaverkadu is a historic seashore town in Chennai Metropolitan Area at Thiruvallur District, of Tamil Nadu state, India. It is about 60 kilometres (37 mi) north of Chennai and 3 kilometres (1.9 mi) from Elavur, on the southern periphery of the Pulicat Lake.

name: Kanchipuram
tagline: Pallava sandstone temples and handwoven mulberry silk
overview: Kanchipuram (IAST: kāñcipuram; [kaːɲdʑipuɾam]), also known as Kanjeevaram or Kancheepuram, is a city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu in the Chennai metropolitan area. Known as the City of Thousand Temples, Kanchipuram is known for its temple architectures, 1000-pillared halls, huge temple towers, and silk saris.

name: Gangaikonda Cholapuram
tagline: UNESCO Chola granite temple built by Rajendra Chola I
overview: Gaṅgaikoṇḍa Chōḻapuram is a village located near Jayankondam in Ariyalur district of Tamil Nadu, India. The Chola emperor Rajendra I established it as the capital of the Chola dynasty in c.

name: Airavatesvara Temple (Darasuram)
tagline: UNESCO Chola stone chariot temple near Kumbakonam
overview: Darasuram or Dharasuram is a neighbourhood in the city of Kumbakonam, Tamil Nadu, India. The area is known for the Airavateswara temple constructed by the Rajaraja Chola II in the 12th century CE.

name: Karaikudi
tagline: Antique lanes, Athangudi tile workshops, and heritage stays
overview: Karaikudi is a city and municipal corporation in Sivaganga district in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is the largest city in the district, and the centre of the Karaikudi Metropolitan Area, that forms part of the Chettinad region.

name: Pollachi
tagline: Coconut groves and gateway to Topslip and Aliyar Dam
overview: Pollachi is a town and municipality in Coimbatore district of the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is the administrative headquarters of Pollachi taluk.

name: Topslip (Anamalai Reserve)
tagline: Teak forests, elephants, and Nilgiri langurs
overview: Anamalai Tiger Reserve, earlier known as Indira Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary and National Park and as Anaimalai Wildlife Sanctuary, is a protected area in the Anaimalai Hills of Pollachi and Valparai taluks of Coimbatore District and Udumalaipettai taluk in Tiruppur District, Tamil Nadu, India. The Tamil Nadu Environment and Forests Department by a…

name: Mudumalai National Park
tagline: Nilgiri foothill safari forest beside Moyar River
overview: Mudumalai National Park is a national park in the Nilgiri Mountains in Tamil Nadu in southern India. It covers 321 km2 (124 sq mi) at an elevation range of 850–1,250 m (2,790–4,100 ft) in the Nilgiri District and shares boundaries with the states of Karnataka and Kerala.

name: Kotagiri
tagline: Quiet Nilgiri tea ridge above Catherine Falls
overview: Kotagiri is a hill station and a municipality in the Nilgiris district of the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. The Nilgiri Hills have been the traditional home of the "Kota" tribes.

name: Courtallam
tagline: Herbal Western Ghats waterfalls in Tenkasi district
overview: Rajah Courtallam, natively spelt Kutrālam or Kuttālam, is a panchayat town situated at a mean elevation of 160 m (520 ft) in the foothills of the Western Ghats in Tenkasi district of Tamil Nadu, India. The Coutrallam Falls on the Chittar River is a major tourist attraction.

name: Thoothukudi
tagline: Pearl-fishing Gulf of Mannar port and Hare Island
overview: Thoothukudi (Tamil: [t̪uːt̪ːukːuɖi] , formerly called Tuticorin) is a port industrial city in Thoothukudi district in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It lies on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal.

name: Tiruchendur
tagline: Shoreline Murugan temple directly beside Gulf of Mannar waves
overview: Tiruchendur (Tamil: Tiruccentūr [ˈt̪iɾɯtːʃen̪d̪uːr], also jayantipuram, also Thirucheeralaivay) is a town in Thoothukudi district, Tamil Nadu, India. It is home to the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple, one of the Six Abodes of Murugan.

name: Tirunelveli
tagline: Nellaiappar temple, Tamiraparani river, and halwa bazaars
overview: Tirunelveli (Tamil: [tiɾɯnelʋeːli] ), also known as Nellai, is a city and municipal corporation in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is located on the southern part of the state, on the west bank of the Thamirabarani River.

name: Nagapattinam
tagline: Historic Coromandel seaport near Velankanni and Kodiakarai
overview: Nagapattinam (nākappaṭṭinam, previously spelt Nagapatnam or Negapatam) is a city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu and the administrative headquarters of Nagapattinam district. The town came to prominence during the period of Medieval Cholas (9th–12th century CE) and served as their important port for commerce and east-bound naval expeditions.

name: Point Calimere (Kodikkarai)
tagline: Coastal dry evergreen sanctuary for flamingos and blackbuck
overview: Point Calimere, also called Cape Calimere or Kodiakkarai, is a low headland of the Coromandel Coast, in the Nagapattinam district of the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. The Cape is located about 9 kilometres (5.6 mi) south of Vedaranyam in the Kaveri delta, and marks a nearly right-angle turn in the coastline.

name: Golden Temple, Sripuram
tagline: Gold-foil spiritual park in Malaikodi near Vellore
overview: Vellore (Tamil: ['ʋeːluːɾ] WAY-loor), also spelled Velur, is a city and municipal corporation in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is the administrative headquarters of Vellore district.

name: Javadi Hills
tagline: Sandalwood and bamboo Eastern Ghats hills with Vainu Bappu
overview: The Javadhu Hills (also Javadi Hills, Jawadhu Hills, and Jawadhu Malai) are an extension of the Eastern Ghats spread across parts of Vellore, Tirupattur and Tiruvannamalai districts in the northern part of the state of Tamil Nadu in south-eastern India. The hills separate Vellore, Tirupattur and Tiruvannamalai districts: Tirupattur district, with its…

name: Mettur Dam
tagline: 1934 Kaveri masonry dam and Stanley Reservoir
overview: The Mettur Dam is one of the largest dams in India, built during colonial rule, and the largest in Tamil Nadu, located across the river Kaveri where it enters the plains. Built in 1934, it took nine years to complete.

name: Coimbatore
tagline: Textile hub framed by Marudamalai and Siruvani hills
overview: Coimbatore (Tamil: Kōyamputtūr, IPA: [koːjɐmbut̪ːuːɾ] ), also known as Kovai (IPA: [koːʋaj] ), is a metropolitan city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is located on the banks of the Noyyal River and surrounded by the Western Ghats.

name: Palani
tagline: Hilltop Dhandayuthapani shrine reached by winch or steps
overview: Palani or Pazhani (Tamil: [paɻani]) is a town in Dindigul district of Tamil Nadu state in India. It is located about 60 kilometres (37 mi) west of Dindigul, 106 kilometres (66 mi) south-east of Coimbatore, 122 kilometres (76 mi) north-west of Madurai, 67 kilometres (42 mi) from Kodaikanal.

name: Namakkal Fort
tagline: Monolithic granite hill fort and rock-cut Narasimha temple
overview: Namakkal (Tamil: [nɑːməkkəl]) is a city and the headquarters of Namakkal district, Tamil Nadu. It is the first ISO 14001-2004 certified municipality in Asia for environmental management, specifically the provision and maintenance of water supply, solid waste and sewage management, town planning, lighting and other social services.

name: Salem
tagline: Steel city at the foot of Yercaud and Kanjamalai
overview: Salem (pronounced [seːlam] ) is a city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is located on the banks of the Thirumanimutharu River and surrounded by the Eastern Ghats.

name: Thekkady
tagline: Spice plantations and bamboo rafting beside Periyar Lake
overview: Thekkady (Malayalam: [t̪eːkːɐɖi]) in Idukki district is a town near Periyar National Park, a tourist attraction in the Indian state of Kerala. The name Thekkady is derived from the word "thekku" which means teak and "adi" meaning bottom.

name: Silent Valley National Park
tagline: Pristine Nilgiri tropical rainforest of lion-tailed macaques
overview: Silent Valley National Park is a national park in Kerala, India. It is located in the Nilgiri hills and has a core area of 89.52 km2 (34.56 sq mi).

name: Nelliyampathy
tagline: Cloud-kissed tea and orange estates above Palakkad Gap
overview: Nelliyampathy (also spelled as Nelliampathi) is a hill station, located 60 kilometres (37 mi) from Palakkad district in the state of Kerala, India.

name: Ponmudi
tagline: Twenty-two misty hairpin bends above Thiruvananthapuram
overview: Ponmudi (the Golden Peak) is a hill station in the Peringamala gramapanchayath of Thiruvananthapuram district of Kerala in India. It is located 22km west of Vithura town, 53 km north-east of Thiruvananthapuram City, 78 km south-east of Varkala town and 69 km north-east of Kovalam Beach at an altitude of 1,100 m (3,600 ft).

name: Ashtamudi Lake
tagline: Eight-armed palm backwater estuary in Kollam
overview: Ashtamudi Lake (Ashtamudi Kayal, ml: "അഷ്ടമുടിക്കായൽ" ), in the Kollam District of the Indian state of Kerala is a unique wetland ecosystem and a large palm-shaped (also described as octopus-shaped) water body. It is second only in size to the Vembanad estuary ecosystem of the state.

name: Munroe Island
tagline: Quiet mangrove-lined canal island in Ashtamudi Lake
overview: Munroe Island is an inland island group located at the confluence of Ashtamudi Lake and the Kallada River, in Kollam district, Kerala, South India. It is a group of eight small islets comprising a total area of about 13.4 km2.

name: Thenmala
tagline: India’s first planned ecotourism forest in Kollam hills
overview: Thenmala is a tourist destination on the eastern side of Kollam district in Kerala, India. It is home to the first ecotourism centre in India.

name: Aranmula
tagline: Heritage Pamba river village of snake boats and metal mirrors
overview: Aranmula is a temple town located in Pathanamthitta district in Kerala, India.

name: Ilaveezhapoonchira
tagline: Tree-free high meadow bowl with 360-degree valley views
overview: Kottayam (IPA: [ko:ʈ:ajam]) is a city in the Kottayam district of Kerala, India. It is the headquarters of Kottayam district, located about 66 km (41 mi) south of the commercial city of Kochi and 154 km (95.7 mi) north of the state capital Thiruvananthapuram.

name: Marayoor
tagline: Natural sandalwood forest and prehistoric Muniyara dolmens
overview: Marayur or Marayoor is a town in Devikulam taluk of Idukki district in the southwestern Indian state of Kerala. It is located 42 kilometers north of Munnar on SH 17 connecting Munnar with Udumalpet, Tamil Nadu.

name: Edakkal Caves
tagline: Prehistoric rock engravings inside Ambukuthi hill cleft
overview: The Edakkal caves are two natural caves at a remote location in Sultan Bathery in the Wayanad district of Kerala in India. They lie 1,200 m (3,900 ft) above sea level on Ambukutty Mala, near an ancient trade route connecting the high mountains of Mysore to the ports of the Malabar Coast.

name: Pookode Lake
tagline: Freshwater forest lake shaped like India’s map in Wayanad
overview: Pookode Lake is a scenic freshwater lake in the Wayanad district in Kerala, South India. A major tourist destination in the district, Pookode is a natural freshwater lake nestling amid evergreen forests and mountain slopes at an elevation of 770 meters above sea level.

name: Kannur
tagline: St Angelo sea fort, handlooms, and Theyyam sacred groves
overview: Kannur (Malayalam: [kɐɳːuːr] ), formerly known in English as Cannanore, is a city and municipal corporation in the state of Kerala, India. It is the administrative headquarters of the Kannur district and situated 280 kilometres (170 mi) north of the major port city and commercial hub Kochi and 146 kilometres (91 mi) south of the major port city and…

name: Payyambalam Beach
tagline: Quiet red-laterite and palm beach in Kannur
overview: Kannur Beach is a group of five beaches on the western side of Kannur city in Kerala, India. They are: Payyambalam Beach Meenkunnu Beach Adikadalayi Beach Baby Beach Thayyil Beach

name: Thalassery Fort
tagline: 18th-century red-laterite sea fort on Malabar coast
overview: Tellicherry Fort is a fortress located in Thalassery (Tellicherry), a town in North Malabar region of Kerala state, India. Thalassery was one of the most important European trading centers in Kerala.

name: Kappad Beach
tagline: Rocky Malabar shoreline where Vasco da Gama landed in 1498
overview: Kappad is a beach and village near Koyilandy, in the Kozhikode district, Kerala, India. A stone monument installed by government commemorates the "landing" by Vasco da Gama with the inscription, 'Vasco da Gama landed here, Kappakadavu, in the year 1498'.

name: Beypore
tagline: Traditional wooden Uru dhow boatyard at Chaliyar estuary
overview: Beypore or Beypur (Malayalam: [beːpːuːr], formerly Beypoor) is a port town in Kozhikode district in the state of Kerala, India. It is located opposite to Chaliyam, the estuary (Azhimukham in Malayalam) where the river Chaliyar empties into the Arabian Sea.

name: Nilambur Teak Museum
tagline: Conolly’s Plot oldest teak plantation and Chaliyar hills
overview: Nilambur (Malayalam: [n̪ilɐmbuːr]) is a major town, a municipality and a taluk in the Malappuram district of the Indian state of Kerala. It is located close to the Nilgiris range of the Western Ghats on the banks of the Chaliyar River.

name: Ranipuram
tagline: Shola grass hills and forest treks on the Kodagu border
overview: Kasaragod (Malayalam: [kaːsɐrɐɡoːɖɨ̆] ) is a municipal town and the administrative headquarters of the Kasaragod district in the state of Kerala, India. Established in 1966, Kasaragod was the first municipal town in the district.

name: Chandragiri Fort, Kasaragod
tagline: 17th-century Payaswini riverfront fort near Bekal
overview: Chandragiri Fort (Malayalam: ചന്ദ്രഗിരിക്കോട്ട ) is a fort built in the 17th century, situated in Kasaragod District of Kerala, India. This large squarish fort is 150 feet (46 m) above sea level and occupies an area of about seven acres the adjacent to Chandragiri river.

name: Malayattoor
tagline: Periyar river valley and hilltop Kurisumudi forest
overview: Kalady or Kaladi is a village located between Angamaly and Perumbavoor, east of the Periyar River, near Malayattoor in Ernakulam district of Kerala, India. The town is not far from Cochin International Airport.

name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
tagline: 18th-century heritage garden and Kempegowda peninsula rock
overview: Lalbagh Botanical Garden, or simply Lalbagh (lit. 'red garden'), is a botanical garden in Bengaluru, India.

name: Talakaveri
tagline: Brahmagiri mountain origin of the sacred Kaveri River
overview: Kodagu district (Kodava: [koɖɐɡɨ, -ʋɨ], also known by its former name Coorg, Kodava: koḍagï, koḍavï) is an administrative district in the Karnataka state of India. Before 1956, it was an administratively separate Coorg State at which point it was merged into an enlarged Mysore State.

name: Nagarhole National Park
tagline: Lush teak forests along the Kabini and Lakshmana Tirtha
overview: Nagarahole National Park is a national park located in Kodagu district and Mysore district in Karnataka, India. This park was declared the 37th Tiger Reserve of India in 2003.

name: Kudremukh
tagline: Horse-face mountain peak and shola valley grasslands
overview: Kudremukha is the name of a mountain range and an individual mountain peak located in Chikmagalur district, in Karnataka, India. It is also the name of a small hill station and iron ore-mining town situated near the mountain, about 20 kilometres from Kalasa in Kalasa Taluk.

name: Baba Budangiri
tagline: Dattatreya Peetha mountain ridge and Manikyadhara Falls
overview: Baba Budangiri (lit. 'Baba Budan hill'), also known as Chandradrona (lit.

name: Sringeri
tagline: Tunga riverside Vidyashankara temple and Adi Shankara matha
overview: Sringeri (IAST: Śṛṅgerī; Kannada: [ʃriŋɡeːri]) also called Shringeri is a hill town and Taluk headquarters located in Chikmagalur district in the Indian state of Karnataka. Sringeri is the site of Sri Sharadamba temple, a part of the Sringeri Sharada Peetham established by Adi Shankaracharya.

name: Horanadu
tagline: Bhadra valley Annapoorneshwari shrine amid coffee hills
overview: Horanadu, also known as Sri Kshetra Horanadu, is a Panchayat village in Kalasa taluk of Chikkamagaluru district, Karnataka, India. It is the site of the Annapoorneshwari Temple.

name: Dandeli
tagline: Kali River white-water rapids and hornbill canopy trails
overview: Dandeli is a taluk in Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka, India, in the Malenadu region.

name: Anshi (Kali Tiger Reserve)
tagline: Western Ghats black panther forest above Karwar
overview: Kali Tiger Reserve (formerly Dandeli-Anshi Tiger Reserve) is a protected area and tiger reserve. It is located in Uttara Kannada district, in Karnataka, India.

name: Sirsi & Unchalli Falls
tagline: Arecanut hills, Marikamba temple, and Aghanashini gorge
overview: Sirsi or Shirasi is a city located in the Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka state in India. Administratively, Sirsi functions as the headquarters for the eponymous taluk, subdivision, and educational district.

name: Honnavar & Sharavathi Backwaters
tagline: Mangrove boardwalks, Kasarkod beach, and ferry islands
overview: Honnavar or Honavar is a town, taluka in Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka, India.

name: Malpe & St. Mary’s Islands
tagline: Fishing harbour and hexagonal columnar basalt sea stacks
overview: Malpe is a natural port in the Udupi District in Karnataka, India. Located at the mouth of the Malpe River about six kilometers to the west of Udupi, it is an important port and a major fishing harbor on the Karnataka coast.

name: Kodachadri
tagline: Western Ghats grass-ridge trek overlooking Mookambika park
overview: Kodachadri is a mountain peak with dense forests (elevation - 1,343 metres above sea level) in the Western Ghats in South India (Shivamogga District, Karnataka), 78 km from Shimoga. Kodachadri is the highest peak in Shivamogga district.

name: Dharmasthala
tagline: Nethravathi valley Manjunatha temple and heritage museum
overview: Dharmasthala () (earlier known as Kuduma) is an Indian temple town on the banks of the Nethravathi River in the taluk of Belthangady of the Dakshina Kannada or southern district in Karnataka, India. The town is known for its centuries-old Dharmasthala Temple, devoted to the Hindu god Manjunatha.

name: Talakadu
tagline: Sand-dune buried Kaveri river temples
overview: Talakādu is a town on the left bank of the Kaveri river 45 km (28 miles) from Mysore and 133 km (82 miles) from Bangalore in Karnataka, India. Latinizations of the towns name vary, but include Talkād, Talakadu, Talakkadu, or Thalakadu.

name: Shivanasamudra Falls
tagline: Twin Kaveri waterfalls Gaganachukki and Bharachukki
overview: Shivanasamudra Falls is a series of segmented waterfalls on the Kaveri river. It is situated in Malavalli taluk in Mandya district, Karnataka.

name: Banavasi
tagline: Karnataka’s oldest town and Kadamba Madhukeshwara temple
overview: Banavāsi is an ancient temple town located near Sirsi in Karnataka. Banavasi was the ancient capital of the Kadamba dynasty that ruled all of modern-day Karnataka state.

name: Lakkundi
tagline: Kalyana Chalukya stepped wells and Kasivisvesvara temple
overview: Lakkundi, also referred to as Lokkugundi, was a major city before the 14th century and is now a village in the Gadag District of Karnataka, India. By the 10th century, it was already a major economic and commercial centre, hosting mint operations for South India.

name: Gadag-Betageri
tagline: Trikuteshwara Saraswati temple and Magadi bird sanctuary
overview: Gadag-Betageri is a city municipal council in Gadag district in the state of Karnataka, India. It is the administrative headquarters of Gadag District.

name: Kittur Fort
tagline: Historic Rani Chennamma citadel south of Belagavi
overview: Kittur or Kitturu, historically known as Kittoor or Kittore, is a town and a taluk in the Belagavi district of the Indian state of Karnataka. It was part of Bailhongal taluka but was declared as an independent taluka on 23 October 2012 by the Chief Minister of Karnataka on the inauguration of Kittur Utsav.
