name: Gokak Falls
tagline: Horseshoe Ghataprabha waterfall and suspension bridge
overview: The Gokak Falls is a waterfall located on the Ghataprabha River in Belagavi district of Karnataka, India. The waterfall is 6.5 kilometers away from Gokak town.

name: Belagavi
tagline: Kamal Basadi fort, Jamboti forests, and Sahyadri passes
overview: Belgaum (Kannada ISO: Beḷagāvi, IPA: [beɭɐɡaːʋi]; Marathi ISO: Beḷagāṃva, IPA: [beɭɡaːũ]), officially known as Belagavi (also Belgaon), is a city in the Indian state of Karnataka located near its northern western border in the Western Ghats. It is the administrative headquarters of the eponymous Belagavi division and Belagavi district.

name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
tagline: Kaveri river rocky islands of painted storks and crocodiles
overview: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary (also known as Pakshi Kashi of Karnataka), is a bird sanctuary in the Mandya District of Karnataka, in India. It is the largest bird sanctuary in the state, 40 acres (16 ha) in area, and comprises six islets on the banks of the Kaveri river.

name: Biligirirangana Hills (BR Hills)
tagline: Forest bridge connecting Eastern and Western Ghats
overview: The Biligirirangana betta or Biligiriranga Hills (as referred to in biology and geology) is a hill range situated in Chamarajanagar District in south-western Karnataka, at its border with Tamil Nadu (Erode District) in South India. The area is called Biligiri Ranganatha Swamy Temple Wildlife Sanctuary or simply BRT Wildlife Sanctuary.

name: Tungabhadra Dam (Hosapete)
tagline: Reservoir viewpoints and sunset gardens near Hampi
overview: Jogimatti is a hill station and forest reserve in Chitradurga district, Karnataka, India. The reserve covers 10,048.97 hectares (38.7993 sq mi) in Chitradurga, Holalkere and Hiriyur taluks, 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) south of the city of Chitradurga.

name: Anthargange (Kolar)
tagline: Volcanic granite boulder caves and spring temple
overview: Kolar Gold Fields (K.G.F.) is a mining region in K.G.F. taluk (township), Kolar district, Karnataka, India.

name: Lambasingi
tagline: Misty Chintapalli plateau known as the Kashmir of Andhra
overview: Lambasingi (or Lammasingi) is a small village in the Eastern Ghats of Chintapalli Mandal of Alluri Sitharama Raju district in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It's also referred as the "Kashmir of Andhra Pradesh".

name: Chandragiri Fort
tagline: Raja Mahal and Rani Mahal granite fortress near Tirupati
overview: Chandragiri Fort is a historical fort located in Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh, India. The fort, with its rectangular bastions and steep moat, was built around 1000AD during the reign of Immadi Narasimha Yadavaraya, who ruled from Narayanavanam.

name: Suryalanka Beach
tagline: Wide golden Bay of Bengal shoreline near Bapatla
overview: Suryalanka Beach or Bapatla Beach is a beach in Bapatla district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It is located approximately 9 kilometers from Bapatla Bhavanarayana Swamy Temple and 50 miles south of Guntur City.

name: Kailasagiri
tagline: Hilltop ocean-view park and ropeway above Visakhapatnam
overview: Kailasagiri is a hilltop park in the city of Visakhapatnam in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. The park was developed by the Visakhapatnam Metropolitan Region Development Authority (VMRDA) and consists of land filled with native trees and other flora.

name: INS Kursura Submarine Museum
tagline: Decommissioned Kalvari-class submarine museum on RK Beach
overview: INS Kursura (S20) was a Kalvari-class (variant of the Foxtrot-class) diesel-electric submarine of the Indian Navy. It was India's fourth submarine.

name: Thotlakonda
tagline: Hilltop Hinayana Buddhist monastery overlooking the sea
overview: Thotlakonda Buddhist Complex is situated on a hill near Bheemunipatnam about 15 kilometres (9.3 mi) from Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, India. The hill is about 128 metres (420 ft) above sea level and overlooks the ocean.

name: Bavikonda
tagline: Excavated 3rd-century BCE Buddhist stupas near Visakhapatnam
overview: Bavikonda Buddhist Complex lies about 16 km from Visakhapatnam, in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, on a hill about 130 metres above mean sea level. The term Bavikonda in Telugu means a hill of wells.

name: Kotappakonda
tagline: Trikuteswara hill shrine rising above Palnadu plains
overview: Kotappakonda is a hill and Hindu pilgrimage site in Palnadu district, Andhra Pradesh, India. It lies about 62 km from Guntur city and 20 km from Narasaraopet.

name: Ethipothala Falls
tagline: Seventy-foot Chandravanka cascade near Nagarjuna Sagar
overview: Ethipothala Falls is a 70 feet (21 m) high river cascade situated in Palnadu district, Andhra Pradesh, India. Located on the Chandravanka river, a tributary of the River Krishna joining on its right bank, the waterfall is formed by the confluence of three streams: Chandravanka Vagu, Nakkala Vagu, and Tummala Vagu.

name: Nallamala Hills
tagline: Eastern Ghats tiger corridor spanning Kurnool and Prakasam
overview: The Nallamalas (also called the Nallamalla Range) are a section of the Eastern Ghats which forms the eastern boundary of Rayalaseema region of the state of Andhra Pradesh and Nagarkurnool district of the state of Telangana, in India. They run in a nearly north–south alignment, parallel to the Coromandel Coast for close to 430 km between th rivers,…

name: Katiki Waterfalls
tagline: Forest trek waterfall fed by the Gosthani near Borra
overview: Katiki Waterfalls is located in Alluri Sitharama Raju district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. The waterfall originates at River Gosthani.

name: Kuntala Waterfall
tagline: Telangana’s tallest 45-metre cascade in Adilabad forests
overview: Kuntala Waterfall is a waterfall of Telangana state in India, located on Kadam river in Neradigonda mandal of Adilabad district. It is the highest waterfall in the state with a height of 150 feet.

name: Bhongir Fort
tagline: Monolithic egg-shaped granite rock fortress near Hyderabad
overview: Bhongir Fort, also known as Bhuvanagiri Fort, is a fort located in the heart of Bhongir a town in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana, India. It is located on a huge rock at a commanding height.

name: Ananthagiri Hills
tagline: Misty Vikarabad coffee hills and Musi River origin
overview: Ananthagiri Hills is located in Vikarabad district, Telangana, India. The water flows from these hills to Osman Sagar, also known as Gandipet lake, and Himayathsagar.

name: Medak Fort
tagline: 12th-century Kakatiya hill fortress above Medak town
overview: Medak Fort is situated in Medak district in the Indian state of Telangana, about 100 kilometres from the state capital, Hyderabad. Medak fort was constructed by the Kakatiya Kings.

name: Hussain Sagar
tagline: 16th-century heart-shaped lake and monolithic Buddha statue
overview: Hussain Sagar (alternatively referred to as Tank Bund; Telugu pronunciation: [ɦusen sɑːgər]) is a heart-shaped lake in Hyderabad, Telangana, India, built by Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah in 1562. It is spread across an area of 5.7 square kilometres (2.2 sq mi) and is fed by the River Musi.

name: Nelakondapalli
tagline: Excavated 3rd-century brick Buddhist mahastupa in Khammam
overview: Nelakondapally, also referred to as Nelakondapalli or Nela Kondapalli, is a town and headquarters of a mandal in Khammam district, Telangana, India. It is also an archaeological site important to early Buddhism and Hinduism, where excavations have discovered a major stupa site near an ancient manmade lake, another site where Buddhist and Hindu artwork…

name: Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary
tagline: India’s oldest waterbird sanctuary in Chengalpattu
overview: Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary is a bird sanctuary in the Madurantakam taluk of the Chengalpattu district in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. Established in 1936, it is the oldest wildlife sanctuary in India.

name: Vellore Fort
tagline: 16th-century granite moat fortress and Jalakandeswarar temple
overview: Vellore Fort is a large 16th-century fort situated in heart of the Vellore city, in the state of Tamil Nadu, India built by Chinna bommi reddy and Timma reddy ,nayakas( feudal lords) under Vijayanagar empire. The fort was at one time the imperial capital of the Aravidu Dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire.

name: Yelagiri Hills
tagline: Fourteen hairpin bends up to Punganoor Lake and orchards
overview: Yelagiri (Tamil: [jeːlaɡiɾi]), also spelled Elagiri, is a hill station located in Tirupathur district of Tamil Nadu, India. Located at an altitude of 1,410 m (4,630 ft), it forms a part of the Eastern Ghats mountain range.

name: Pichavaram Mangrove Forest
tagline: Backwater maze of mangrove islands near Chidambaram
overview: Pichavaram is one of the villages of Parangipettai near Chidambaram in Cuddalore District, Tamil Nadu, India. It is located between the Vellar estuary in the north and Coleroon estuary in the south.

name: Hogenakkal Falls
tagline: Carbonatite river gorges and bamboo coracles on the Kaveri
overview: Hogenakkal Falls is a waterfall in South India on the Kaveri river on the border between Dharmapuri district of Tamil Nadu and Chamrajnagar district of Karnataka. It is located 46 km (29 mi) from Dharmapuri and 199 km (124 mi) from Chamrajnagar.

name: Valparai
tagline: Anamalai tea plateaus and Sholayar rainforest bends
overview: Valparai (originally known as Poonachimalai) is a Town and hill station in the Coimbatore district of Tamil Nadu, India. It consists of Anamalai Tiger Reserve (earlier known as Indira Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary and National Park (IGWLS&NP) and prior to that as Anaimalai Wildlife Sanctuary).

name: Kolli Hills
tagline: Seventy hairpin bends to Agaya Gangai forest waterfall
overview: Kolli Malai, also known as Kolli Hills, is a hill station and taluk in Namakkal district, Tamil Nadu, India.

name: Papanasam & Agasthiyar Falls
tagline: Tamiraparani rainforest reserve in Tirunelveli hills
overview: Kalakkad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve is located in the South Western Ghats montane rain forests in Tirunelveli district and Kanyakumari district in the South India. It is the second-largest protected area in Tamil Nadu and part of Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve.

name: Athirappilly Falls
tagline: Thundering 80-foot Chalakudy River cascade in Sholayar woods
overview: Athirappilly Falls (Malayalam: [ɐd̪iɾɐpːiɭːi]) is situated in Athirappilly Panchayat in Chalakudy Taluk of Thrissur District in Kerala, India on the Chalakudy River, which originates from the upper reaches of the Western Ghats at the entrance to the Sholayar ranges. It is the largest waterfall in Kerala, which stands tall at 83.7 feet.

name: Vagamon
tagline: Rolling green meadows, pine valleys, and Kurisumala hills
overview: Vagamon (Malayalam: [ʋaːɡɐmɐɳ]) is an Indian hill station and a revenue village located in Peerumedu Taluk of Idukki district, and also Meenachil taluk and Kanjirappally taluk of Kottayam district in the state of Kerala, India. name: Poovar
tagline: Golden estuary sandbar between Neyyar river and Arabian Sea
overview: Poovar is a tourist town in Neyyattinkara (tehsil) in the Thiruvananthapuram district of Kerala state, South India. This village is almost at the southern tip of Thiruvananthapuram while the next village, Pozhiyoor, marks the end of Kerala.

name: Marari Beach
tagline: Peaceful coconut-palm fishing coast near Alappuzha
overview: Marari Beach is a beach at Mararikulam village in Alappuzha District of Kerala, India, 11 km from Alappuzha (Alleppey) town.

name: Cherai Beach
tagline: Seashell shoreline separating Vypeen backwaters from the sea
overview: Cherai Beach is located in Cherai on the northern side of Vypin Island, a suburb of the city of Kochi in the state of Kerala, India. One of the most visited beaches in the state, it is situated around 25 km (15 mi) from downtown Kochi and 20 km (12 mi) from Cochin International Airport.

name: Palakkad Fort
tagline: 18th-century granite Tipu’s Fort encircled by a moat
overview: Palakkad Fort is an old fort situated in the heart of Palakkad city in Kerala state, southern India.

name: Malampuzha
tagline: Western Ghats garden reservoir, yakshi sculpture, and ropeway
overview: Malampuzha Dam is the largest dam and reservoir in Kerala, located near Palakkad, in the state of Kerala in South India, built post-independence by the then Madras state. Situated in the scenic hills of the Western Ghats in the background, it is a combination of a masonry dam with a length of 1,849 metres and an earthen dam with a length of 220 metres…

name: Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary
tagline: Rain-shadow thorny scrub forest and Thoovanam waterfall
overview: Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary is a wildlife sanctuary in the Idukki district of India's Kerala state. It is one of 18 wildlife sanctuaries among the protected areas of Kerala.

name: Banasura Sagar Dam
tagline: India’s largest earth dam ringed by Wayanad islands
overview: Banasura Sagar Dam, situated in Padinjarathara in Kerala is the largest earth dam in India and second largest dam in Asia. Banasura Dam is under the control of Padinjarathara KSEB Station.

name: Soochipara Falls
tagline: Three-tier Sentinel Rock waterfall near Meppadi
overview: Soochipara Falls also known as Sentinel Rock Waterfalls is a three-tiered waterfall in Vellarimala, Wayanad, India. It is surrounded by deciduous, evergreen and montane forests.

name: Kuruwadweep (Kuruva Island)
tagline: Protected 950-acre Kabini river island of bamboo bridges
overview: Kuruvadweep is a 950-acre (3.8 km2) protected river delta in the Indian state of Kerala. It comprises three densely wooded uninhabited islands and a few submergible satellite islands which lies on the banks of the tributaries of Kabini River in the Wayanad district of the state.

name: Muzhappilangad Beach
tagline: Four-kilometre hard-packed sand drive-in beach near Kannur
overview: Muzhappilangad Beach is a drive-in beach in Tellichery Kannur district of Kerala, on the Malabar Coast of India. It is 4 kilometers in length.

name: Dharmadam Island
tagline: Tide-accessible green island off Thalassery
overview: Dharmadam Island (Green Island) is a small 2-hectare private island in Thalassery, Kannur District, Kerala. It lies about 100 metres from the mainland at Dharmadam.

name: Kodanad & Abhayaranyam
tagline: Periyar riverside elephant rescue forest near Perumbavoor
overview: Kodanad is a rural riverside village of Perumbavoor, Ernakulam district in Keralam, South India. It is 18 km from Angamaly.

name: Mattancherry
tagline: Dutch Palace murals and Jew Town spice lanes in Kochi
overview: The Mattancherry Palace is a palace popularly known as the Dutch Palace, in Mattancherry, Kochi, in the Indian state of Kerala which features Kerala murals depicting portraits and exhibits of the Rajas of Kochi. The palace was included in the tentative list of UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

name: Nandi Hills
tagline: Sunrise cloud sea and Tipu’s Drop fortress near Bengaluru
overview: Nandi Hills (Anglicised forms include Nandidurg and Nandydoorg) is an ancient hill fortress built by the Ganga dynasty in the Chikkaballapur district of Karnataka state. It is now a locality situated 10 km from Chickballapur town and approximately 60 km from Bengaluru.

name: Namdroling Monastery (Bylakuppe)
tagline: Golden Temple Tibetan settlement in Kodagu
overview: The Thegchog Namdrol Shedrub Dargye Ling (བོད་ཡིག ཐེག་མཆོག་རྣམ་གྲོལ་བཤད་སྒྲུབ་དར་རྒྱས་གླིང་།) (Wylie: theg mchog rnam grol bshad sgrub dar rgyas gling), informally known as Namdroling Monastery (or ನಮ್ಡ್ರೋಲಿಂಗ್ ವಿಹಾರ, Namdroling Vihara) is the largest teaching center of the Nyingma lineage of Tibetan Buddhism in the world. Located in Bylakuppe, part of…

name: Sakleshpur
tagline: Manjarabad star-shaped fort and misty Malnad coffee ridges
overview: Sakleshpur or Sakaleshapura, is a town and the taluk in Hassan district in the state of Karnataka, India. The town is located on the banks of Hemavati River and it lies in the foot-hills of the Western Ghats range.

name: Sathodi Falls
tagline: Rectangular forest waterfall feeding Kodasalli backwaters
overview: Sathodi Falls (also spelt as Sathoddi Falls) is a waterfall located in the Western Ghats, Uttara Kannada District Located 32 km (20 mi) from Yellapur and 74 km (46 mi) from Sirsi. It is about 15 metres (49.2 feet) tall.

name: Murdeshwar
tagline: Arabian Sea peninsula crowned by towering Shiva statue
overview: Murdeshwar or Murudeshwara is a town in Uttara Kannada district in the state of Karnataka, India, and lies on the coast of the Arabian Sea. It contains the world's third tallest Shiva statue, as well as the Murudeshwara Temple.

name: Kaup Beach & Lighthouse
tagline: Rocky Arabian Sea headland and 1901 stone lighthouse
overview: Kapu or Kaup is a town in the Udupi district of Karnataka, India. It is situated on National Highway 66, approximately 13 km south of Udupi and 40 km north of Mangalore.

name: Moodabidri
tagline: Thousand Pillar Basadi Jain heritage town near Mangaluru
overview: Moodabidri or Moodubidire (Mūḍubidire; also called Mudbidri, Moodbidri, Bidrem and Bedra) is a city and taluk in Dakshina Kannada district. It lies 34 km northeast of the district headquarters, Mangaluru, in Karnataka, India.

name: Kukke Subramanya
tagline: Kumara Parvatha forest shrine beside Kumaradhara River
overview: Kukke Subramanya (IAST: Kukke Subrahmaṇya) is a Hindu temple on the banks of Kumaradhara River in the village Subramanya in Kadaba taluk (previously in Sullia taluk) in Dakshina Kannada district, Karnataka, India. The priests in the temple are Shivalli Madhwa Brahmins.

name: Nehru Zoological Park
tagline: Sprawling Mir Alam Tank wildlife park in Hyderabad
overview: Nehru Zoological Park (also known as Zoo Park) is a zoo located near Mir Alam Tank in Bahadurpura, Telangana, India. It is one of the most visited destinations in Hyderabad.

name: Mrugavani National Park
tagline: Chilkur deer and scrub woodland park near Hyderabad
overview: Mrugavani National Park is a national park located in Hyderabad, Telangana State, India. It is situated at Chilkur in Moinabad mandal, 20 km from MGBS and covers an area of 3.6 square kilometres (1.4 sq mi) or 1211 acres.

name: Mahavir Harina Vanasthali
tagline: Blackbuck grassland sanctuary on Hyderabad’s eastern edge
overview: Mahavir Harina Vanasthali National Park is a deer national park located in Vanasthalipuram, Hyderabad, Telangana, India. It is spread over 3605 acres.

name: Gadwal Fort
tagline: 18th-century mud-and-stone citadel famed for Gadwal sarees
overview: Gadwal is a City and the district headquarters of Jogulamba Gadwal district in the Indian state of Telangana. It is located 188 km (117 mi) from the state capital Hyderabad And 59 km From Kurnool and is a state assembly constituency.

name: Parnasala
tagline: Forested Godavari riverside hermitage near Bhadrachalam
overview: Khammam is the city in Khammam district of the Indian state of Telangana. It is the fourth largest city in the state.

name: Kakinada
tagline: Planned coastal city beside Hope Island and Coringa mangroves
overview: Kakinada (; formerly known as Cocanada, and also referred to as Coringa and Kakinandiwada) is a port city and municipal corporation in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. Situated along the Bay of Bengal, it serves as the headquarters of Kakinada district and is a prominent economic and cultural centre in the region.

name: Anantapur
tagline: Rayalaseema hub for Lepakshi, Penukonda, and Thimmamma Marrimanu
overview: Anantapur, officially Ananthapuramu, is a city in Anantapur district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It is the mandal headquarters of Anantapur mandal and also the divisional headquarters of Anantapur revenue division.

name: Nandyal
tagline: Gateway to Mahanandi springs and Nallamala temples
overview: Nandyal, commonly called as Nandyala, is the administrative headquarters of the Nandyal district in the Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh, India. It was officially formed as a separate district on April 4, 2022, after being carved out of the larger Kurnool district.

name: Kothapatnam Beach
tagline: Quiet Prakasam Bay of Bengal coast near Ongole
overview: Ongole (Telugu pronunciation: [oŋɡoːlu]), natively known as Ongolu, is a city in Prakasam district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It is the headquarters of Prakasam district.

name: Nellapattu Bird Sanctuary
tagline: Pelican and painted stork breeding lake in Tirupati district
overview: Nellore, also spelt as Nelluru, is a city located on the banks of Penna River, in Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh, India. It serves as the headquarters of the district, as well as Nellore Urban mandal, Nellore Rural mandal and Nellore revenue division.

name: Salihundam
tagline: Hilltop Buddhist stupas along the Vamsadhara River
overview: Srikakulam is a city and the headquarters of Srikakulam district in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. As of 2011 census, it has a population of 165,735.

name: Vizianagaram Fort
tagline: 18th-century Pusapati square fortress and heritage town
overview: Vizianagaram, also known as Vijayanagaram (Telugu: [ʋidʒɐjɐnɐɡɐrɐw̃]), is a city and the headquarters of the Vizianagaram district in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It is located in the Eastern Ghats, about 24 km (15 mi) west of the Bay of Bengal and 40 km (25 mi) north-northeast of Visakhapatnam.

name: Bobbili Fort
tagline: Historic fort town famed for Bobbili veena craftsmanship
overview: Bobbili is a town in Vizianagaram district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.

name: Kanaka Durga Temple (Indrakeeladri)
tagline: Iconic Indrakeeladri hill shrine above the Krishna in Vijayawada
overview: Kanaka Durga Temple, officially known as Sri Durga Malleswara Swamyvarla Devasthanam, is a Hindu temple dedicated to Kanaka Durga. The deity in this temple is also popularly referred as Kanaka Durga.

name: Kapila Theertham
tagline: Waterfall-fed Shiva shrine at the foot of Tirumala hills
overview: Kapila Theertham is a small Shaivite temple and theertham, located at Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh, India. The idol of Shiva is believed to have been installed by Sage Kapila, so god Shiva here is referred to as Kapileswara.

name: Dwaraka Tirumala (Chinna Tirupati)
tagline: Hilltop Venkateswara pilgrimage town in Eluru district
overview: Dwaraka Tirumala is a census town in Eluru district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. It is located in Dwaraka Tirumala mandal of Jangareddygudem revenue division.

name: Palakollu Ksheerarama
tagline: Pancharama Kshetra white-gopuram temple in West Godavari
overview: Ksheerarama is one of the five Pancharama Kshetras that are sacred to the Hindu god Shiva. The temple is located in Palakollu of West Godavari in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.

name: Bhimavaram Somarama
tagline: Colour-shifting moon-phase Shiva Linga Pancharama shrine
overview: Somarama is one of the five Pancharama Kshetras that are sacred to the Hindu god Shiva. The temple is located in Bhimavaram of West Godavari district in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.

name: Samarlakota Kumararama
tagline: Two-storey Chalukyan Pancharama temple near Kakinada
overview: Kumararama or Bhimarama (Chalukya Kumararama Bhimeswara Temple) is one of the five Pancharama Kshetras that are sacred to the Hindu god Shiva. The temple is located in Samarlakota of Kakinada district in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.

name: Mecca Masjid, Hyderabad
tagline: Monumental 17th-century granite mosque beside Charminar
overview: Mecca Masjid, also called Makkah Masjid, is a mosque located in Hyderabad in the state of Telangana, India. It is the largest mosque in the city, and one of the largest in the country, with a capacity of 10,000 worshippers.

name: Yadadri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple
tagline: Sculpted black-granite hilltop shrine northeast of Hyderabad
overview: The Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple or Yadadri or Yadagiri Gutta Devasthanam (YGD), or Pancha Narasimha Kshetram or Rishi Aradhana Kshetram is a Hindu Temple situated on a hillock in the small town of Yadagirigutta in the Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district of the Indian state of Telangana. Yadadri Temple is touted as Telangana's own Tirupati.

name: Kolanupaka Jain & Someshwara Temple
tagline: 2,000-year-old Svetambara Jain mahavira shrine in Yadadri
overview: Kulpakji, also known as Kolanupaka Temple is a 2,000-year-old Śvetāmbara Jain temple in the village of Kolanupaka in Aler City, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana, India. The temple houses three deities: one each of Lord Rishabhanatha, Lord Neminatha, and Lord Mahavira.

name: Sanghi Temple
tagline: Paramanandagiri hilltop Chola-Chalukya style temple near Hyderabad
overview: Sanghi Temple, which is said to be the replica of Tirumala temple is located at Sanghi Nagar in Telangana in India, is about 35 km from Hyderabad city. The sacred Raja Gopuram, which is very tall, can be seen from several kilometers away.

name: Basar Gnana Saraswati Temple
tagline: Godavari riverside Saraswati shrine in Nirmal district
overview: Gnana Saraswati Temple (Telugu: శ్రీ జ్ఞాన సరస్వతి దేవస్థానము) is a Hindu temple of Goddess Saraswati located on the banks of Godavari River at Basara, Telangana, India. It is one of the two famous Saraswati temples in the Indian subcontinent, the other being Sharada Peeth.

name: Kamakshi Amman Temple, Kanchipuram
tagline: Golden-roofed Shakti Peetha shrine in the heart of Kanchipuram
overview: The Kamakshi Amman Temple, also known as Kamakoti Nayaki Kovil, is a Hindu temple dedicated to the goddess Kamakshi, a primary aspect of Adi Shakti, the supreme goddess in Shaktism. The temple is located in the historic city of Kanchipuram, near Chennai, India.

name: Tiruttani Murugan Temple
tagline: Fifth Arupadaiveedu hilltop shrine overlooking Tiruvallur
overview: Subramaniya Swamy Temple is a Hindu temple located on a hillock in Tiruttani, Tiruvallur district, Tamil Nadu, India. It is dedicated to Murugan, and is one of the six abodes of Murugan (Arupadaiveedu).

name: Swamimalai Murugan Temple
tagline: Fourth Arupadaiveedu temple atop a 60-step hillock
overview: Swaminatha Swamy Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to god Murugan. It is located on the banks of a tributary of river Kaveri in Swamimalai near Kumbakonam, Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu, India.

photoCredit.author: Ravichandar84 (The original uploader was Ravichandar84 at English Wikipedia .)

name: Pazhamudircholai
tagline: Sixth Arupadaiveedu forest shrine in Alagar hills near Madurai
overview: Solaimalai Murugan Temple is a Hindu temple, located atop a hill, in the outskirts of Madurai in Tamil Nadu. It is dedicated to Murugan, and is one of the six abodes of Murugan (Arupadaiveedu).

name: Srivilliputhur Andal Temple
tagline: Eleven-tier gopuram shrine and birthplace of poetess Andal
overview: The Srivilliputhur Andal Temple in Srivilliputhur, a town in Virudhunagar district in the South Indian state of Tamil Nadu, It is one of the 108 Divya Desams dedicated to Vishnu, who is worshipped as Vatapatrasayi and his consort Lakshmi as Andal. It is believed to be the birthplace of two of the Alvars, namely Periyalvar and his foster-daughter, Andal.

name: Samayapuram Mariamman Temple
tagline: Revered Amman pilgrimage temple north of Tiruchirappalli
overview: Arulmigu Sri Mariamman Temple, Samayapuram is an ancient Hindu temple in Tiruchirappalli district in Tamil Nadu, India. The main deity, Samayapuram Mariamman, a form of Adi Parashakti and Mariamman, is made of sand and clay with extractions of medicinal herbs unlike many of the traditional stone idols and is considered as most powerful Goddess, and hence…

name: Thiruvanaikaval Jambukeswarar
tagline: Pancha Bhoota Appu (Water) Linga temple on Srirangam island
overview: Jambukeswarar Temple, Thiruvanaikaval (also Thiruvanaikal, Jambukeswaram) is a temple of Shiva in Tiruchirapalli district, in the state of Tamil Nadu, India. It is one of the five major Shiva Temples of Tamil Nadu representing the Mahābhūta or five elements; this temple represents the element of water, or neer in Tamil.

name: Vaitheeswaran Koil
tagline: Historic temple town of palm-leaf Nadi astrology near Mayiladuthurai
overview: Vaitheeswaran Koil is a Hindu temple dedicated to the Shiva, located in a small town Vaitheeswarankoil near Mayiladuthurai, Mayiladuthurai district the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. Shiva is worshipped as Vaidyanathar or Vaitheeswaran meaning the "God of healing" and it is believed that prayers to Vaitheeswaran can cure diseases.

name: Oppiliappan Temple
tagline: Divya Desam Vishnu shrine famed for salt-free naivedyam
overview: Oppiliappan Temple, is a Hindu temple dedicated to Vishnu, located near Thirunageswaram and also known by its old toponym Thiruvinnagar, a village in the outskirts of the Kumbakonam in the South Indian state of Tamil Nadu. Constructed in the Dravidian style of architecture, the temple is glorified in the Naalayira Divya Prabandham, the early medieval…

name: Padmanabhaswamy Temple
tagline: Iconic gold-gopuram Dravidian-Kerala shrine in Thiruvananthapuram
overview: The Padmanabhaswamy Temple (Malayalam: [pɐd̪mɐnaːbʰɐswaːmi]) is a Hindu temple dedicated to Vishnu in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams which are considered the sacred sites of the Sri Vaishnava tradition.

name: Sabarimala Ayyappa Temple
tagline: Periyar tiger reserve hilltop Ayyappa pilgrimage shrine
overview: The Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple (Malayalam pronunciation: [ʃabəɾimala]) is a Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Sree Dharma Sastha where the deity is worshipped as Lord Ayyappan, an eternal brahmachari, the son of the deities Shiva and Mohini (female avatar of the god Vishnu), and is situated atop the Sabarimala hill in Pathanamthitta district of…

name: Guruvayur Temple
tagline: Historic Dwaraka of the South Krishna shrine in Thrissur
overview: The Guruvayur Temple, also called the Guruvayur Sree Krishna Temple, is situated in the town of Guruvayur, Thrissur district, Kerala, India. Located approximately 26 kilometers (16 miles) northwest of Thrissur city, the temple is dedicated to the deity Guruvayurappan, a form of Krishna-Vishnu.

name: Chottanikkara Bhagavathy Temple
tagline: Famed Mother Goddess pilgrimage shrine near Ernakulam
overview: The Chottanikkara Bhagavathy Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Bhagavathy, located in the village of Chottanikkara within the Ernakulam District of Kerala, India. Managed by the Cochin Devaswom Board, it is one of the most significant shrines among the 409 temples under the board's administration.

name: Mannarasala Nagaraja Temple
tagline: Sacred grove serpent shrine tucked inside Haripad woods
overview: Mannarasala Sree Nagaraja Temple (Malayalam: മണ്ണാറശാല ശ്രീ നാഗരാജാക്ഷേത്രം) is a Hindu temple in Kerala, India, dedicated to the worship of serpent gods.

name: Cheraman Juma Mosque
tagline: Historic mosque in Kodungallur dating to early maritime trade
overview: The Cheraman Juma Mosque is a mosque in Kodungallur, Thrissur district, in the state of Kerala, India. The mosque was built in 629 CE by Malik Bin Dinar though some scholars suggest a later construction date in the 14th–15th century.

name: Malayattoor Kurisumudi
tagline: Hilltop Christian pilgrimage shrine overlooking Periyar valley
overview: The St Thomas Syro Malabar Catholic International Shrine, Malayattoor (or Malayatoor Church or മലയാറ്റൂർ വി. തോമാശ്ലീഹാ സീറോ-മലബാർ തീർത്ഥാടനപള്ളി) is one of the eleven international shrines in the world, situated in Malayattoor Angamaly, Ernakulam district of Kerala, India.

name: Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple
tagline: Pamba riverfront Krishna temple of Vallam Kali snake boats
overview: The Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple is a Hindu temple located in Aranmula, a village in Pathanamthitta District, Kerala, South India, on the southern bank of Pamba river, the third longest river in Kerala. It is dedicated to the Lord Krishna, who is worshipped as Parthasarathy (Arjuna's charioteer).

name: Kollur Mookambika Temple
tagline: Souparnika river Adi Shakti shrine below Kodachadri
overview: Kollur Mookambika Temple (Kannada: ಕೊಲ್ಲೂರು ಮೂಕಾಂಬಿಕಾ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನ) is located at Kollur in Byndoor Taluk of Udupi District in the region of Tulunadu, state of Karnataka, near Kundapur India. It is a Hindu temple dedicated to the mother goddess Mookambika.

name: Udupi Sri Krishna Matha
tagline: 13th-century Kanakana Kindi Krishna matha founded by Madhvacharya
overview: Udupi Shri Krishna Temple is a well-known historic Hindu temple dedicated to Krishna and Dvaita Matha, located in the city of Udupi in Karnataka, India. The Matha area resembles a living ashram, a holy place for daily devotion and living.

name: Kateel Durgaparameshwari
tagline: Nandini river-island temple north of Mangaluru
overview: Kateel or Kateelu is a temple town in the Dakshina Kannada district of the Indian state of Karnataka. It is considered one of the holiest Hindu temple towns in India.

name: Banashankari Temple, Badami
tagline: Haridra Tirtha lakeside Shakti shrine near Badami
overview: Banashankari Devi Temple (or Banashankari temple) is a Hindu shrine located at Cholachagudda near Badami, in Bagalkot district, Karnataka, India. The temple is popularly called 'Shakambhari' 'Banashankari or Vanashankari' since it is located in the Tilakaaranya forest.

name: Ranganathaswamy, Srirangapatna
tagline: Ancient Adi Ranga Kaveri island temple
overview: The Ranganathaswamy temple or Sri Ranganathaswamy temple in Srirangapatna, in the Mandya district of Karnataka state, India, is dedicated to the Hindu god Ranganatha (a manifestation of Vishnu). The temple is classified one among the 108 Abhimana Kshethram of Vaishnavate tradition.

name: Kotilingeshwara (Kolar)
tagline: Shrine complex featuring a towering Shiva Linga and lakh lingas
overview: Kotilingeshwara Temple (Kannada: ಕೋಟಿಲಿಂಗೇಶ್ವರ) a Hindu temple in the village of Kammasandra in Kolar district, Karnataka, India. The presiding deity of the temple is Shiva.

name: Jama Masjid, Delhi
tagline: Shah Jahan’s monumental red-sandstone & marble mosque in Old Delhi
overview: The Masjid-i-Jehan-Numa, commonly known as the Jama Masjid, in Old Delhi area of Delhi, is one of the largest mosques in India. Its builder was the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, between 1644 and 1656, and it was inaugurated by its first Imam, Syed Abdul Ghafoor Shah Bukhari.

name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
tagline: Golden-domed Sikh gurdwara and sacred Sarovar near Connaught Place
overview: Gurdwara Bangla Sahib () is Sikh gurdwara, or Sikh house of worship, in Delhi, India, and is known for its association with the eighth Sikh Guru, Guru Har Krishan, as well as the holy pond inside its complex, known as the "Sarovar." Originally a bungalow of Raja Jai Singh I of Amber, it was rebuilt as a small shrine by Sikh general Sardar Baghel Singh in…

name: Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib
tagline: Historic Chandni Chowk gurdwara on the site of Guru Tegh Bahadur’s martyrdom
overview: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib is one of the nine historical Gurdwaras in Delhi. It was first constructed in 1783 as a small shrine by Baghel Singh to commemorate the martyrdom site of the ninth Sikh Guru, Tegh Bahadur and was probably expanded after Indian Rebellion of 1857 or after Partition of India.

name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
tagline: Golden-spired Jyotirlinga on the western bank of the Ganga
overview: Kashi Vishwanath Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva. It is located in Vishwanath Gali, in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, India.

name: Sankat Mochan Temple, Varanasi
tagline: Serene Assi-riverfront Hanuman shrine founded by Tulsidas
overview: The Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple is a Hindu temple in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, India dedicated to the Hindu deity Hanuman, in his form as sankat mochan (saṅkaṭamocana), meaning the "reliever from troubles". The temple was established by the Hindu preacher and poet-saint Tulsidas in the early 16th century.

name: Har Ki Pauri, Haridwar
tagline: Sacred Brahma Kund ghats hosting nightly Ganga Aarti
overview: Har Ki Pauri is a sacred ghat on the banks of the Ganges River in the Hindu holy city of Haridwar, in the Indian state of Uttarakhand. It is believed to be the place where the Ganges leaves the mountains and enters the plains.

photoCredit.author: Sanatansociety Picture provided by Peter and Chris Marchand, provides free information for promotional purpose

name: Tungnath Temple
tagline: Highest Panch Kedar Shiva temple at 3,680 m in Garhwal
overview: Tungnath Temple (IAST:tuņgnāth) is one of the highest Shiva temples in the world and is the highest of the five Panch Kedar temples located in the Rudraprayag district, in the Indian state of Uttarakhand. The Tungnath (literal meaning: Lord of the peaks) mountains form the Mandakini and Alaknanda river valleys.

name: Madhyamaheshwar
tagline: Remote Chaukhamba-framed Panch Kedar temple meadow
overview: Madhyamaheshwar (Sanskrit: मध्यमहेश्वर) or Madmaheshwar is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva, located in Gaundar, a village in Rudraprayag district, situated amidst the Garhwal Himalayas of Uttarakhand, India. Situated at an elevation of 3,497 m (11,473.1 ft), it is one of the Panch Kedar pilgrimage circuits, comprising five Shiva temples in the Garhwal…

name: Rudranath
tagline: Alpine meadow rock-face Panch Kedar shrine in Chamoli
overview: Rudranath Temple (Sanskrit: रुद्रनाथ) is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva, located in the Garhwal Himalayan mountains in Uttarakhand, India. Located at 2,290 metres (7,510 ft) above sea level, this natural rock temple is situated within a dense forest of rhododendron dwarfs and Alpine pastures.

name: Hemkund Sahib
tagline: Star-shaped Sikh gurdwara beside glacial lake at 4,329 m
overview: Gurdwara Hemkund Sahib is a Sikh place of worship (gurdwara) and pilgrimage site in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand, India. It is devoted to Guru Gobind Singh (1666–1708), the tenth Sikh Guru, and finds mention in Dasam Granth.

name: Amarnath Cave Shrine
tagline: High-altitude Himalayan ice-stalagmite Shiva cave at 3,888 m
overview: Amarnath Temple is a Hindu shrine located in the Pahalgam tehsil of Anantnag district of Jammu and Kashmir, India. It is a cave situated at an altitude of 3,888 m (12,756 ft), about 72 km from Anantnag, the district headquarters, 141 km (88 mi) from Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir, accessible via either Sonamarg or Pahalgam The cave,…

name: Hazratbal Shrine, Srinagar
tagline: White-marble Dal Lake shrine framed by the Zabarwan range
overview: The Hazratbal Shrine, also known as Dargah Hazratbal, is a Sufi dargah and mosque located in Hazratbal area of Srinagar, in the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, India. The shrine houses the Moi-e-Muqqadas, a relic traditionally believed to be a hair strand of the Islamic Prophet Muhammad.

name: Shankaracharya Temple, Srinagar
tagline: Hilltop ancient stone temple overlooking Dal Lake and Srinagar
overview: Shankaracharya Temple or Jyeshteshwara Temple is a Hindu temple situated on top of the Zabarwan Range in Srinagar in the Kashmir Valley of the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, India. It is dedicated to Shiva.

name: Raghunath Temple, Jammu
tagline: Gold-plated Dogra-era seven-shrine complex in Jammu
overview: Raghunath Temple is a Hindu temple located in Jammu in the Indian union territory of Jammu and Kashmir. It consists of a complex of seven Hindu shrines.

name: Kheer Bhawani Temple, Tulmulla
tagline: Sacred spring shrine shaded by chinar trees near Ganderbal
overview: Kheer Bhawani, Ksheer Bhawani or the Ragnya Devi temple is a Hindu temple situated at a distance of 25 kilometres (16 mi) north-east of Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India, in the village of Tulmulla in Ganderbal. It is dedicated to the Hindu goddess Kheer Bhavani constructed over a sacred spring.

name: Hidimba Devi Temple, Manali
tagline: Four-tiered pagoda cedar-forest shrine built in 1553
overview: Hidimba Devi Temple, locally known as Dhungari Temple, also known variously as the Hadimba Temple, is a Hindu Temple, located in Manāli, a hill station in the State of Himāchal Pradesh in north India. It is an ancient cave temple dedicated to Hidimbi Devi, wife of Bhima, a figure in the Indian epic Mahābhārata.

name: Jakhu Temple, Shimla
tagline: Deodar-crowned hilltop Hanuman temple above Shimla Ridge
overview: Jakhu Temple (also Jakhoo Temple) is an ancient Hindu temple in Shimla, Himachal Pradesh, India, dedicated to the Hindu deity Lord Hanuman. It is situated at Jakhu Hill, Shimla's highest peak, 2.5 km (1.6 mi) east of the Ridge at a height of 2,455 m (8,054 ft) above sea level.

name: Chintpurni Temple
tagline: Revered Chhinnamastika Shakti Peetha in Una district
overview: Chintpurni is a small town in the Una district of Himachal Pradesh about 40 km (25 miles) north of Una, not far from the border with the Indian state of Punjab. The elevation is about 977 meters (about 3,200 feet).

name: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib
tagline: Fifth Sikh Takht in Talwandi Sabo, Bathinda
overview: The Takht Sri Darbar Sahib Damdama Sahib, is one of the five takhts or Seat of Temporal Authority of Sikhism, located in Talwandi Sabo, near the city of Bathinda in Bathinda district of Punjab, India. At this place Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, prepared the full version of the Sikh scriptures called Sri Guru Granth Sahib in 1705.

name: Brahma Sarovar, Kurukshetra
tagline: Colossal sacred water tank lined with ghats and shrines
overview: Brahma Sarovar (transl. Brahma's lake) is a natural and divine tank in Kurukshetra, in the state of Haryana, India.

name: Brahma Temple, Pushkar
tagline: 14th-century red-spired temple beside Pushkar Lake
overview: Brahma Temple, Pushkar (also known as Jagatpita Brahma Mandir) is a Hindu temple situated at Pushkar in the Indian state of Rajasthan, close to the sacred Pushkar Lake to which its legend has an indelible link. The temple is one of very few existing temples dedicated to the Hindu creator-god Brahma in India and remains the most prominent among them.

name: Karni Mata Temple, Deshnoke
tagline: Famed white-marble portal temple south of Bikaner
overview: Karni Mata Temple of Deshnoke (Hindi: करणी माता मंदिर), also known as Madh Deshnoke, is a prominent Hindu temple dedicated to Karni Mata at the town of Deshnoke, located 30 km south of Bikaner, in Rajasthan. It has become the most important pilgrimage site for devotees of Charani sagatis after access to Hinglaj was restricted following the partition of…

name: Khatu Shyam Ji Temple
tagline: Major Sikar pilgrimage shrine of Barbarika
overview: Khatu Shyam Ji Temple is a Hindu temple located in KhatuShyamJi town in the Sikar district of Rajasthan. It is a pilgrimage site dedicated to the worship of Khatu Shyam, a divine figure believed to be a manifestation of Barbareek, a character from the Indian epic Mahabharat.

name: Dilwara Jain Temples
tagline: 11th-century translucent white-marble ceilings in Mount Abu
overview: The Delwada Temples or Delvada Temples are a group of Śvētāmbara Jain temples located about 2+1⁄2 kilometres from the Mount Abu settlement in Sirohi District, Rajasthan's only hill station. Delwara Temples are among 5 Maha tirths of Svetambara sect along with Shatrunjay, Girnar, Sammed Shikharji and Ashtapad.

name: Eklingji Temple
tagline: 108-shrine walled marble-and-granite complex north of Udaipur
overview: Eklingji (Hindi: Ekaliṅga jī, pronounced [ekliŋɡᵊ d͡ʒiː]) is a Hindu temple complex in Udaipur District of Rajasthan in western India. It is situated in Kailashpuri village (at Girwa Tehsil, Udaipur), near the former capital of Mewar, i.e., Nagda.

name: Mehandipur Balaji Temple
tagline: Hillside Hanuman shrine in Dausa-Karauli
overview: Mehandipur Balaji Temple is a temple in Mehandipur, Dausa district, in the Indian state of Rajasthan dedicated to the Hindu deity Hanuman. The name Balaji refers to the childhood form of Hanuman, revered in several parts of the country.

name: Akshardham Temple, Gandhinagar
tagline: Pink-sandstone Swaminarayan complex in Gujarat’s capital
overview: Swaminarayan Akshardham in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India is a large Hindu temple complex inspired by Yogiji Maharaj (1892–1971) the fourth spiritual successor of Swaminarayan, and created by Pramukh Swami Maharaj (1921–2016), the fifth spiritual successor of Swaminarayan according to the BAPS denomination of Swaminarayan Hinduism. The complex was built…

name: Shamlaji Temple
tagline: Meshwo riverside Vishnudham shrine in Aravalli hills
overview: Shamlaji, also spelled Shamalaji, is a major Hindu pilgrimage centre in Aravalli district of Gujarat state of India. The Shamlaji temple is dedicated to Vishnu.

name: Shirdi Sai Baba Temple
tagline: World-famous Samadhi Mandir pilgrimage town in Ahilyanagar
overview: Shirdi (; also known as Sainagar) is a town and pilgrimage site in the Indian state of Maharashtra. Shirdi is located in the Rahata taluka of Ahilyanagar district.

name: Siddhivinayak Temple, Mumbai
tagline: Prabhadevi’s iconic gold-domed Ganesha shrine
overview: The Shri Siddhivinayak Ganapati Mandir is a Hindu temple dedicated to Ganesha. It is located in Prabhadevi neighbourhood of Mumbai, Maharashtra.

tagline: Arabian Sea-facing Tridevi shrine at Bhulabhai Desai Road
overview: Mahalaxmi Temple is a Hindu temple, dedicated to Mahalakshmi, the central deity of the Devi Mahatmyam, located in Mumbai, India. It is one of the most famous temples of the city of Mumbai.

name: Babulnath Temple, Mumbai
tagline: Hilltop ancient Shiva temple overlooking Girgaum Chowpatty
overview: Babulnath Temple is a Hindu temple, dedicated to Shiva, in Mumbai, India, on a small hillock near Girgaum Chowpatty. It is one of oldest mandirs in the city, Shiva in the form of the "Lord of the Babul Tree" is the main deity in this temple.

name: Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga
tagline: Twelfth Jyotirlinga sandstone shrine beside Ellora Caves
overview: Ghrishneshwar Jyotirlinga (IAST: Ghṛṣṇeśvara), also known as Grishneswhar, is a Hindu temple of Shiva in Verul village of Aurangabad district, Maharashtra. It is one of the 12 Jyotirlinga mandirs.

name: Aundha Nagnath Jyotirlinga
tagline: 13th-century Yadava-carved Jyotirlinga in Hingoli
overview: Aundha Naganath is a town in the Hingoli district of the Maharashtra state in India. The town is known for the Aundha Nagnath Temple, a Hindu temple.

name: Parli Vaijnath Jyotirlinga
tagline: Hilltop Beed district Jyotirlinga shrine
overview: Parli Vaijnath is a city and a municipal council in Beed district in the Indian state of Maharashtra. Parli is Second largest city in terms of size and population in Bid district.

name: Pandharpur Vithoba Temple
tagline: Bhima (Chandrabhaga) river Warkari pilgrimage heart
overview: The Vithoba Temple, officially known as Shri Vitthal-Rukmini Mandir (Marathi: श्री विठ्ठल-रूक्मिणि देऊळ Kannada: ಶ್ರೀ ವಿಠ್ಠಲ-ರುಕ್ಮಿಣಿ ದೇವಸ್ಥಾನ) is a Hindu temple in Pandharpur, in the Indian state of Maharashtra. It is the main centre of worship for Vithoba, a form of the god Vishnu, and his consort Rakhumai.

name: Kolhapur Mahalaxmi Temple
tagline: 7th-century Chalukyan Shakti Peetha of black stone
overview: Mahalakshmi Temple (also known as Ambabai Mandir) is dedicated to Goddess Mahalakshmi. According to Hinduism, Goddess Mahalakshmi is the consort of Maha Vishnu and it is customary among Hindus to visit Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, Kolhapur Mahalakshmi Temple and Padmavathi Temple as a yatra (pilgrimage).

name: Tuljapur Bhavani Temple
tagline: Bala Ghat hilltop Kuldaivat shrine in Dharashiv
overview: Shree Tulaja Bhavani Temple is a 12th-century-CE Hindu temple dedicated to goddess Bhavani, located in Dharashiv district of Maharashtra, India. It was built in 12th century CE by Mahamandaleshwara Māradadeva of the Kadamb dynasty.

name: Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga, Ujjain
tagline: South-facing Jyotirlinga famed for dawn Bhasma Aarti
overview: Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga (IAST: mahākāleśvara) is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva and is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, shrines which are said to be the most sacred abodes of Shiva. It is located in the ancient city of Ujjain in the state of Madhya Pradesh, India.

name: Taj-ul-Masajid, Bhopal
tagline: One of Asia’s largest pink-sandstone mosques
overview: The Taj-ul-Masajid (Arabic: تَاجُ ٱلْمَسَاجِد, romanized: Tāj-ul-Masājid, lit. 'Crown of Mosques'), also known as the Tāj-ul-Masjid (Arabic: تَاجُ ٱلْمَسْجِد), is a Sunni mosque, affiliated with Tablighi Jamaat, part of the Deobandi movement, located in Bhopal, in the state of Madhya Pradesh, India.

name: Baidyanath Dham, Deoghar
tagline: Revered Jyotirlinga and Shakti Peetha in Santhal Pargana
overview: Baidyanath Temple (IAST: Baidyãnath) is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva. It is located in Deoghar, in the Santhal Parganas division of the Indian state of Jharkhand.

name: Rajrappa Chhinnamasta Temple
tagline: Damodar-Bhairavi river confluence Shakti shrine
overview: Rajrappa is a waterfall and a pilgrimage centre in the Chitarpur CD block in the Ramgarh subdivision of the Ramgarh district in the Indian state of Jharkhand.

name: Takht Sri Patna Sahib
tagline: White-marble Sikh Takht marking Guru Gobind Singh’s birthplace
overview: Takht Sri Patna Sahib also known as Takhat Sri Harimandir Ji, Patna Sahib, is one of the five takhts of the Sikhs, located in Patna, Bihar, India. The edifice has been reconstructed at least twice; in the early 19th century after a fire and in the mid-20th century after an earthquake.

name: Lingaraja Temple, Bhubaneswar
tagline: 11th-century Kalinga sandstone tower overlooking Bindusagar
overview: Lingaraja Temple (Odia: [liŋɡɔraːd͡ʒɔ] ) is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva and is one of the oldest temples in Bhubaneswar, the capital of the Indian state of Odisha, India. The temple is the most prominent landmark of Bhubaneswar city and one of the major tourist attractions of the state.

name: Mukteswara Temple, Bhubaneswar
tagline: Gem of Kalinga sculpture with carved stone torana arch
overview: Mukteshwara Temple (IAST: Mukteśwara; also spelt Mukteswara) is a 10th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva located in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, India. The temple dates back to 950–975 CE and is a monument of importance in the study of the development of Hindu temples in Odisha.

name: Tara Tarini Shakti Peetha
tagline: Kumari hill Rushikulya river shrine in Ganjam
overview: Tara Tarini Pitha (Odia: ତାରାତାରିଣୀ ପୀଠ, romanized: Tārā-Tāriṇī Pīṭha) is a Hindu temple of Adi Shakti and one of the Adi Shakti Pithas, at the Kumari hills on the bank of Rushikulya river near Purushottampur in Ganjam district of Odisha, around 28 km from Brahmapur city.

name: Samaleswari Temple, Sambalpur
tagline: Mahanadi bank shrine of western Odisha’s presiding deity
overview: Samaleswari Temple is a Hindu temple in Sambalpur, Odisha, India, dedicated to the goddess known as 'Samaleswari', also known among the natives as Samalei Maa, meaning Mother Samaleswari. Shree Shree Samaleswari, the revived presiding deity of Sambalpur, holds a profound religious significance across western Odisha and Chhattisgarh in India.

name: Kalighat Kali Temple, Kolkata
tagline: Historic Adi Ganga Shakti Peetha in South Kolkata
overview: Kalighat Kali Temple is a Hindu temple in Kalighat, Kolkata, West Bengal, India, dedicated to the Hindu goddess Kali, one of the 10 Mahavidyas in the Hindu tantric tradition and the supreme deity in the Kalikula worship tradition. The temple is one of the 51 Shakti Pithas in India.

name: St. Paul’s Cathedral, Kolkata
tagline: Indo-Gothic white cathedral beside Victoria Memorial
overview: St. Paul's Cathedral is a Church of North India (CNI) cathedral of Anglican background in Kolkata, West Bengal, India, noted for its Gothic architecture and dedicated to Paul the Apostle.

name: Nakhoda Mosque, Kolkata
tagline: Red-sandstone domes inspired by Akbar’s tomb in Chitpur
overview: The Nakhoda Masjid is a Sunni mosque, located in Kolkata, in the state of West Bengal, India. The mosque is situated in the Chitpur area of the Burrabazar business district in Central Kolkata, at the intersection of Zakaria Street and Rabindra Sarani.

name: Umananda Temple, Guwahati
tagline: Peacock Island hilltop Shiva shrine in the Brahmaputra
overview: Umananda Devaloi (Pron: ˈʊməˌnændə ˈdeɪvəˌlɔɪ) is a Shiva temple located on the Umananda Island (Peacock Island) in the middle of the river Brahmaputra, Assam. Brahmaputra just opposite the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Kamrup or the Kachari Ghat in Guwahati.

name: Hajo Hayagriva Madhava
tagline: Monikut hill temple sacred to Hindus and Buddhists
overview: Hayagriva Madhava Temple is situated on the Manikut hill. The hill is situated in Hajo of Kamrup District in Assam, India.

name: Tirupati
tagline: Sacred foothill gateway city below the seven hills of Tirumala
overview: Tirupati ( Tiru-pa-ti) is a city in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh and serves as the administrative headquarters of Tirupati district. It is known for its significant religious and cultural heritage, being home to the renowned Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, a major Hindu pilgrimage site, as well as other historic temples.

name: Srikalahasti
tagline: Swarnamukhi riverside town of the Vayu Linga Shiva shrine

name: Annavaram
tagline: Ratnagiri hilltop Satyanarayana Swamy shrine on Pampa river
overview: Annavaram is a village in the Kakinada district of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, renowned for its religious and cultural significance. The village is best known for the Sri Veera Venkata Satyanarayana Swamy Temple, dedicated to Lord Satyanarayana, an incarnation of Vishnu.

name: Amareswara Temple, Amaravati
tagline: Pancharama Shiva shrine along the Krishna River
overview: Amaravati is a village located on the banks of the Krishna River in the Palnadu district of Andhra Pradesh, India. It was built by zamindar Vasireddy Venkatadri Nayudu in late 18th century adjacent to the ancient site of the Satavahana capital Dhanyakataka.

The shrine is significant and it is one of the most popular sites of religious visitation for Sunni Muslims in the Indian…

name: Banke Bihari Temple, Vrindavan
tagline: Beloved Krishna shrine in the lanes of Vrindavan
overview: Banke Bihari Temple is a Hindu temple situated in the town of Vrindavan, Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh, India. The temple is dedicated to Banke Bihari who is believed to be the combined form of Radha and Krishna.

name: Arunachaleswarar Temple, Tiruvannamalai
tagline: Pancha Bhoota Agni Linga temple at Arunachala foothills
overview: The Arunachalesvara Temple or Annamalaiyar Temple, is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva and Parvati, located at the foothills of the Arunachala hill in Tiruvannamalai, Tamil Nadu, India. It is regarded as one of the significant temples in the Tamil Shaivite tradition.

name: Adi Kumbeswarar Temple, Kumbakonam
tagline: Mahamaham tank Shiva temple in the heart of Kumbakonam
overview: Adi Kumbeswarar Temple, Kumbakonam is a Hindu temple to Shiva in the town of Kumbakonam in Thanjavur District, Tamil Nadu, India. Shiva is worshiped as Adi Kumbeswarar, and is represented by the lingam.

name: Attukal Bhagavathy Temple
tagline: Renowned Thiruvananthapuram shrine hosting Attukal Pongala
overview: The Attukal Bhagavathy Temple is a Hindu shrine located at Attukal in Kerala, India. It is situated near the heart of the city, two kilometres away from the Padmanabhaswamy Temple, East Fort, in Thiruvananthapuram.

name: ISKCON Temple, Bengaluru
tagline: Hilltop Radha Krishna temple in Rajajinagar, Bengaluru
overview: ISKCON Temple Bengaluru is one of the largest Krishna-Hindu temples in the world. It is situated in Bengaluru in the Indian state of Karnataka.

name: Tiruchanoor Padmavathi Temple
tagline: Sacred Alamelu Mangapuram shrine five km from Tirupati
overview: Padmavati Temple is a Hindu temple to the deity Padmavati (Alamelu Mangamma or Alarmel Mangai), the consort of Venkanna, in Tiruchanur, Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh, India. The temple is under the administration of Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams.

tagline: Musical stone pillars and towering gopuram near Kanyakumari

name: Vaikom Mahadeva Temple
tagline: Ancient Vembanad-side Shiva temple famed for Vaikom Satyagraha

tagline: Ancient Muziris-era shrine in Thrissur district
overview: Sree Kurumba Bhagavati Temple (alternatively Sree Kurumba Bhagavati Temple) is a Hindu temple at Kodungallur, Thrissur District, Kerala state, India. It is dedicated to the goddess Bhadrakali, a form of Mahakali worshipped and significantly revered in Kerala.

tagline: UNESCO-awarded wooden-roofed shrine at Thrissur’s center
overview: The Vadakkumnathan Temple is an ancient Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva in Thrissur, in the Thrissur district of Kerala, India. The temple is a classical example of the architectural style of Kerala and has one monumental tower on each of the four sides in addition to a koothambalam.

tagline: Ancient Aravalli ridge Kali shrine in South Delhi
overview: Kalkaji Mandir is a Hindu temple dedicated to Kali, a Hindu goddess. It is in southern Delhi, in Kalkaji, a place whose name derives from the temple.

tagline: Fort-like 76-step hilltop Hanuman shrine in Ayodhya
overview: Hanuman Garhi Temple is a Hindu temple of Hanuman in Uttar Pradesh, India. Located in Ayodhya, it is one of the most important temples in the city along with other temples such as Ram Mandir and Nageshwar Nath.

tagline: Illuminated Italian-marble temple complex in Vrindavan
overview: Prem Mandir is a Hindu temple in Vrindavan, Mathura district, Western Uttar Pradesh, India. The temple was established by Kripalu Maharaj.

tagline: Sacred birthplace complex in the heart of Mathura
overview: Krishna Janmasthan Temple is a Hindu temple situated in Mathura, Uttar Pradesh, India. tagline: Bilwa Parvat hilltop Siddh Peeth reached by ropeway
overview: Mansa Devi Temple, Haridwar (Hindi: मंसा देवी मंदिर, हरिद्वार) is a Hindu temple dedicated to goddess Mansa Devi in the holy city of Haridwar in the Uttarakhand state of India. The temple is located atop the Bilwa Parvat on the Sivalik Hills, the southernmost mountain chain of the Himalayas.

name: Chandi Devi Temple, Haridwar
tagline: Neel Parvat hilltop shrine facing Mansa Devi across the Ganga
overview: Chandi Devi Temple, Haridwar (Hindi: चण्डी देवी मंदिर, हरिद्वार) is a Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Chandi Devi in the holy city of Haridwar in the Uttarakhand state of India. The temple is situated atop the Neel Parvat on the Eastern summit of the Sivalik Hills, the southernmost mountain chain of the Himalayas.

name: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
tagline: Forested Manikoot hill Shiva shrine above Rishikesh
overview: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Nilkanth, an aspect of Shiva. Located approximately 32 km from Rishikesh in the Pauri Garhwal district of Uttarakhand, India, the temple is constructed in the Dravidian architectural style.

name: Kainchi Dham
tagline: Neem Karoli Baba riverside ashram near Nainital
overview: Kainchi Dham, also known as Neem Karori Ashram, is a Hindu ashram and temple complex located at Kainchi in the Nainital district, Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, India. It is closely associated with the Hindu saint Neem Karoli Baba, also known as Neeb Karori Baba.

overview: Kalpeshwar (Sanskrit: कल्पेश्वर) is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva located at an elevation of 2,200 m (7,217.8 ft) in the Urgam valley in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand state in India. The temple's ancient legend linked to the Pandavas, heroes of the epic Mahabharata, is the fifth temple of the Panch Kedar (five temples) of Shiva's five anatomical…

overview: Shri Chamunda Devi Temple also known as Chamunda Nandikeshwar Dham is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shri Chamunda Devi, a form of Goddess Durga, located at 19 km away from Palampur town in Dharamshala Tehsil of Kangra district of the Northern Indian state of Himachal Pradesh. name: Durgiana Temple, Amritsar
tagline: Silver-doored lake temple echoing the Golden Temple’s architecture
overview: Durgiana Temple or Shri Durgiana Mandir is a Hindu temple situated in the city of Amritsar in Punjab, India. Though a Hindu temple, its architecture is similar to the Sikh Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple).

overview: Salasar Balaji Temple is a Hindu temple for the devotees of Hindu god Hanuman. It is located in the town of Salasar near Sujangarh, in Churu district of Rajasthan, India.

name: Ranakpur Jain Temple

overview: Ranakpur Jain temple or Chaturmukha Dharana Vihara is a Śvētāmbara Jain temple at Ranakpur dedicated to Tirthankara Rishabhanatha. The temple is located in the village of Ranakpur near Sadri in the Pali district of Rajasthan.

tagline: Pushtimarg haveli shrine of Krishna on Banas River
overview: The Shrinathji Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Shrinathji (a form of Krishna) located in Nathdwara. It is considered an important pilgrimage centre by Vaishnavas.

tagline: Iconic Jyotirlinga shrine between Dwarka and Bet Dwarka
overview: Nageshwar Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva located on Dwarka, Gujarat, India. It is one of the legendary temples mentioned in the Shiva Purana and one of the twelve Jyotirlingas.

name: Palitana Shatrunjaya Temples
tagline: 863 marble Jain shrines crowning Shatrunjaya hill
overview: The Palitana temples, often known only as Palitana, are a large complex of Jain temples located on Shatrunjaya hills near Palitana in Bhavnagar district, Gujarat, India. name: Salangpur Hanuman Temple

name: Shani Shingnapur
tagline: Open-air Swayambhu Shanidev shrine in Ahilyanagar
overview: Shani Shingnapur or Shani Shinganapur or Shingnapur is a village in the Indian state of Maharashtra. Situated in Nevasa Taluka in Ahmednagar district, the village is known for its popular temple of Shani, the Hindu god associated with the planet (graha) Saturn.

name: Dagdusheth Ganpati, Pune
tagline: Iconic heritage Ganesha shrine in old Pune
overview: The Dagadusheth Halwai Ganapati Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to the Hindu god Ganesha (Ganapati) in the city of Pune, India. The temple is visited by over one hundred thousand devotees every year.

name: Kaal Bhairav Temple, Ujjain
tagline: Shipra bank shrine of Ujjain’s guardian deity
overview: Kal Bhairav temple is a Hindu temple located in the Ujjain city of Madhya Pradesh, India. It is dedicated to Kal Bhairav, the guardian deity of the city.

name: Bhojpur Shiva Temple

overview: The Bhojeshwar Temple (IAST: Bhojeśvara) is an incomplete Hindu temple in Bhojpur village of Madhya Pradesh, India. Dedicated to Shiva, it houses a 7.5-foot (2.3 m) high lingam in its sanctum.

name: Danteshwari Temple, Dantewada

overview: Danteshwari Temple is Hindu temple, dedicated to Goddess Danteshwari, and is one of the 52 Shakta pithas, shrines of Shakti, the divine feminine, spread across India. The temple built in the 14th century, is situated in Dantewada, a town situated 80 km from Jagdalpur Tehsil, Chhattisgarh.

name: Dongargarh Bambleshwari
tagline: Hilltop Rajnandgaon Devi shrine reached by ropeway or steps
overview: Bambleshwari Temple is a Hindu temple, located at Dongargarh in Rajnandgaon district, Chhattisgarh, India. It is on a hilltop of 1600 feet.

name: Vishnupad Temple, Gaya
tagline: Falgu riverfront octagonal basalt shrine with sacred footprints
overview: Vishnupad Temple (Sanskrit: विष्णुपद मंदिर, IAST: Viṣṇupada Mandira; lit. 'temple of Vishnu's feet') is a Hindu temple in Gaya, Bihar, dedicated to Vishnu.

name: Mundeshwari Temple, Kaimur
tagline: One of the oldest functional octagonal stone temples in India
overview: The Mundeshwari Devi Temple (IAST: Muṇḍeśvarī) is a Hindu temple, located at Ramgarh Village, 608 feet (185 m) on the Mundeshwari Hills of Kaimur plateau near Son River, in the Bhojpuri region of Indian state of Bihar. It is an Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) protected monument since 1915.
